findings.claim: Current mediabunny is 1.60.0 (npm, 2026-09-25, MPL-2.0). Since v1.56.0 (2026-09-08) the ISOBMFF muxer accepts negative packet timestamps and writes an edit list (elst) that trims the negative section. This is the mechanism for frame-accurate start trims and AAC priming compensation without re-encoding. Pin the exact version because releases land almost daily.
sources: https://github.com/Vanilagy/mediabunny/releases/tag/v1.56.0 ('Added support for muxing negative timestamps for ISOBMFF... generates an edit list')
/tmp/hh-clips/pkgs/mediabunny-1.60.0/package/src/isobmff/isobmff-boxes.ts:521-575 (edts: 'Negative offset: the negative section of the media is trimmed off')

findings.topic: mediabunny AAC path, WebKit 302253 fix, polyfill selection
findings.claim: AudioSampleSource routes through AudioEncoderWrapper. Registered custom encoders are checked FIRST (customAudioEncoders.find, media-source.ts:2196), before native AudioEncoder (2233). So registerAacEncoder() overrides native AAC even where native works, and registration must be gated on !(await canEncodeAudio('aac')). The native output callback repairs the WebKit 302253 description: when the description is missing, shorter than 2 bytes, or parses to objectType 0, it is rebuilt from the codec string, sample rate and channel count (2259-2283). onEncodedPacket fires AFTER that repair (2296), so packets harvested from a live AudioSampleSource already carry the fixed ASC. The polyfill path emits FFmpeg extradata as its own description and does not need the fix.

findings.topic: WebKit 302253 reproduced live and mediabunny fix confirmed
findings.claim: WebKit bug 302253 is still NEW. On Safari 26.5 (macOS), raw AudioEncoder AAC decoderConfig.description came back as esds bytes (038080802200...021190...) instead of an ASC. The same stream through mediabunny AudioSampleSource came back with the corrected ASC '1190', and the MP4 played with correct 48 kHz stereo audio.

WebCodecs exposes no AAC priming information, and MediaRecorder MP4 output carries no elst. Measured encode-then-decode onset delay: 2114 samples for native AAC on both Chrome 153/macOS and Safari 26.5 (AudioToolbox's 2112). The FFmpeg WASM AAC (polyfill) delay is 1024 samples: it landed 22.7 ms early when the native 2114 value was applied to it. Fix: shift audio timestamps by -P/sampleRate (P = the measured delay of the encoder actually in use) and let mediabunny write the elst. After that fix, beep onsets matched the flash frames to 0.02 ms in both browsers.
sources: /tmp/hh-clips/proto/out/chromepoly-clippcm.mp4 (beeps at 0.4773 s vs flash 0.5 s = 1090-sample residual)
ffmpeg silencedetect/signalstats runs on chrome3-clip30.mp4 and safari-clip30.mp4

findings.claim: Muxing a 30 s 720p30 clip in memory with fastStart 'in-memory' by packet copy (900 video + about 1,400 AAC packets) took 12.8 ms in Chrome 153 and 19 ms in Safari 26.5 on an M5. Encoding the audio at clip time from a PCM ring took 101 ms (Chrome) and 160 ms (Safari) natively. It took 560 ms through @mediabunny/aac-encoder, whose blob worker needs one postMessage per 1024-sample frame. Phone numbers are unmeasured. The desktop numbers justify a continuous AAC ring, so that 'Clip it!' costs only a mux.

A 29.5 s clip cut from a stream with 1 s GOPs starts at the preceding keyframe with a negative timestamp. mediabunny then writes a video elst with media_time 15 at timescale 30 (0.5 s trimmed). ffprobe reports duration 29.500 s, the flash frames sit at 0.5/1.5/2.5 s, and the beeps align. End trims are exact because the realtime encoder emits no B-frames.

findings.topic: Title/end card splice by packet copy
findings.claim: A second VideoEncoder with the identical config produced a byte-identical avcC on Chrome 153 and on Safari 26.5 (0164001fffe10014...). Title-card GOPs could therefore be spliced ahead of ring packets in one avc1 track with no re-encode, and ffmpeg decoded the result with zero errors. mediabunny stores only the first packet's decoderConfig (isobmff-muxer.ts:402) and writes avc1 unless the codec string starts with avc3 (isobmff-boxes.ts:1888). A splice is valid only when the avcC bytes match, and that must be checked at runtime on every device.

WebKit exposes VideoEncoder, AudioEncoder and VideoFrame on (Window, DedicatedWorker), and SerializedScriptValue serializes VideoFrame. VideoFrame transfer to a worker plus worker-side encoding worked on Safari 26.5 and Chrome 153. Main-thread cost of new VideoFrame(canvas) plus transfer: p50 about 0.1 ms in Chrome, about 1-2 ms in Safari (Safari's timer is coarsened to 1 ms).

With the prod CSP and no COOP/COEP, typeof SharedArrayBuffer === 'undefined' and crossOriginIsolated === false in both Chrome 153 and Safari 26.5, so the audio and video transport must use transferable ArrayBuffers over MessagePorts. Turning on COEP would break the cdn.emulatorjs.org and Cloudflare Insights loads, and Safari has no COEP credentialless.

Under the WebCodecs spec, a UA may reclaim only codecs that are inactive (no progress for 10 s) or background, never active foreground ones, and never active background encoders. Chromium reclaims only when the page is backgrounded AND global pressure is exceeded AND the codec has been inactive for 90 s. A foreground paused game does not lose its encoder in Chrome, but a long backgrounding can close it with QuotaExceededError, so the engine must handle that as a new epoch.

VideoEncoder: Chrome 94, Firefox desktop 130, Firefox Android NO, Safari/iOS 16.4. AudioEncoder, AudioDecoder and AudioData: Safari/iOS 26 only (Chrome 94, Firefox 130). Nested workers inside a dedicated worker: Safari 16.4. WASM SIMD: Safari 16.4, Chrome 91, Firefox 89. FileSystemSyncAccessHandle: Safari 15.2, Chrome 102/109. FileSystemWritableFileStream: Safari 26. StorageManager.estimate: Safari 17. MediaStreamTrackProcessor is Window-only in Chrome and worker-only in Safari 18.

The OpenH264 software encoder is enabled by default on Android for WebCodecs, MediaRecorder and WebRTC (crbug 40519162 comment 70, 2026-05-15, Cr-Commit-Position 1631506, behind a remote kill switch). That position falls between the M149 branch (1625079) and the M150 branch (1639810), so Chrome Android 150+ can encode H.264 without a hardware encoder. The current Android stable is 155.

The isConfigSupported field dataset (about 320k sessions, Jan-Mar 2026) reports avc1.42001f encodable in 99.7% of sessions (Chrome Android 99.79%), avc1.4d001f 98.98% (Chrome Android 97.54%) and avc1.64001f 98.66% (Chrome Android 96.25%). Firefox on Android is 0% for all. So the candidate order must fall back from High to Main to Baseline, and each must be probe-encoded.

findings.topic: mediabunny encoder internals relevant to config
findings.claim: mediabunny always builds High-profile avc1.6400xx strings and picks the level from the macroblock count and bitrate only (it ignores frame rate, codec.ts:258-279). It forces avc.format 'avc' (codec.ts:926-932), throws on odd dimensions for avc/hevc (media-source.ts:704), and test-encodes a frame on Firefox because isConfigSupported is unreliable there (encode.ts:1153-1195, issue #222). It also catches isConfigSupported TypeErrors on iOS (#456). The live path should use explicit codec strings with a probe-encode rather than mediabunny's builder.

In fastStart 'in-memory' mode the ISOBMFF muxer writes chunks in the order they were added, with no sort by time (isobmff-muxer.ts:1649). Clip assembly must feed video and audio merged by timestamp, or the MP4 comes out non-interleaved, which hurts progressive playback of hosted clips.

Safari 26.5 MediaRecorder('video/mp4', timeslice 1000) emitted one moof+mdat fragment per second, each starting on a keyframe, with no options set. Chrome 153 did the same with videoKeyFrameIntervalDuration: 1000. Keeping ftyp+moov plus the newest fragments and remuxing with mediabunny Input/EncodedPacketSink into a fast-start MP4 with a negative-timestamp trim produced an exact 5.5 s clip in 88-142 ms in Node. Neither recorder writes an elst.
sources: https://blog.addpipe.com/duration-in-mp4-files-produced-by-chrome-safari/ (Chrome chunks align to fMP4 fragments; Safari follows timeslice)

findings.claim: Chromium's Web Share rejects more than 10 files or more than 50 MiB in total (kMaxSharedFileCount/kMaxSharedFileBytes). Long Record-mode files on Android/ChromeOS need a re-encoded share copy of at most 45 MiB, or the download path.

Next 16.2.x Turbopack production builds break new Worker(new URL(..., import.meta.url)) ('e.indexOf is not a function' / 'Missing worker bootstrap config'). next dev does not reproduce it. The fix #96307 merged 2026-07-28 and ships in v16.3.0 (commit b368a50 is an ancestor of v16.3.0). The repo pins next 16.2.9, so the encoder worker requires upgrading next and eslint-config-next to 16.3.x (latest 16.3.6) plus a production-build smoke test.
sources: gh api releases/tags/v16.3.0 (line 902 'Fix Turbopack worker URL context lookup: #96307')

findings.claim: @mediabunny/aac-encoder is labelled MPL-2.0 but embeds FFmpeg libavcodec (Lavc62.23.103, LGPL-2.1+). The WASM is compiled with -msimd128 (so it cannot load without WASM SIMD, for example on iOS < 16.4), inlined, and run in a blob worker. The package pins no FFmpeg commit and carries no FFmpeg notice. FFmpeg's LGPL checklist requires source that corresponds exactly to the shipped binary, hosted next to it. Shipping it therefore needs our own pinned, reproducible build. Bundle size is 254 KB gz / 204 KB br.

esbuild minified mediabunny 1.60 subsets: live worker set (Output, Mp4OutputFormat, Buffer/Stream/NullTarget, Encoded*PacketSource, EncodedPacket, AudioSampleSource, AudioSample, Quality, canEncodeAudio, registerEncoder, Custom*Encoder) = 43.9 KB gz / 38.2 KB br. Editor set (Input, BlobSource, BufferSource, MP4, EncodedPacketSink, VideoSampleSink, VideoSampleSource, AudioSampleSink, CanvasSink) = 67.7 KB gz / 57.7 KB br standalone, 94 KB gz for the union. The whole library is 184 KB gz.

findings.topic: WASM H.264 fallback feasibility and licensing
findings.claim: minih264 is CC0 with SSE/NEON intrinsics. The 2020 h264-mp4-encoder WASM build of it (MIT) ran at 18 ms/frame at 640x360, 39 ms at 854x480 and 67 ms at 1280x720 on an M5 in Node, so a phone needs a fresh SIMD build at 360p or below and adaptive fps. mattdesl suspended mp4-h264 over MPEG LA enforcement concerns. Cisco's OpenH264 patent coverage applies only to Cisco-distributed binaries. Via LA AVC terms are $0 for the first 100,000 units per year (a license is still required). The last US AVC pool patents expire 2027-09-09; the EU ones expired 2025-01, and Japan/China 2025-08.

On Safari 26.5, FileSystemSyncAccessHandle.write honors TypedArray view offsets, and truncate works. The corruption in mediabunny #459 is specific to FileSystemWritableFileStream.write writing the whole backing buffer. Record mode therefore uses sync access handles in the worker, and copies views to exact-size buffers defensively. Origin quota is up to 60% of disk for Safari and home-screen apps; persist() is granted heuristically.

A fragmented MP4 (1 s fragments, onMoof positions recorded) truncated at a committed moof boundary after a simulated torn write was read back by mediabunny with 600 video and 921 audio packets intact. It then remuxed with fastStart 'reserve' (maximumPacketCount taken from the recovered counts) into a fast-start MP4 with moov at byte 32, in 14.7 ms, and ffmpeg decoded it without errors.

risksAndMitigations: Nothing has been measured on a phone. VideoFrame cost, encoder drop behaviour, keyframe cadence, avcC identity, priming, clip build time and memory are all desktop-only numbers. Mitigation: the section 10 device matrix is a release gate. Every tunable (fps steps, bitrate, ring seconds) adapts at runtime from measured costs rather than constants.

Safari VideoFrame(canvas) costs about 1-2 ms on an M5, likely 3-6 ms on older iPhones. Mitigation: EWMA budget gate (3 ms at 60 Hz) that steps capture fps 30 -> 24 -> 20 -> 15 and never touches the game loop. The inFlight drop gate means capture can never stall the game.

Next 16.2.9 breaks module workers in production builds (#94015). Mitigation: upgrade to 16.3.x in the same PR, plus a production-build Playwright smoke test that asserts the worker boots. The documented fallback is an esbuild-prebuilt worker in public/.

WebKit 302253 AAC description bug is still open. Mitigation: all native AAC goes through mediabunny AudioSampleSource, which repairs the description before onEncodedPacket (verified live). Our ascFor() check re-validates before every mux.

The custom AAC encoder overrides native if registered unconditionally (mediabunny checks custom encoders first). Mitigation: register only when canEncodeAudio('aac') is false, and unit-test the selection.

AAC priming differs per platform and WebCodecs exposes nothing. Mitigation: per-session encode/decode calibration on native paths, a constant 1024 for our FFmpeg build and 2112 for WebKit MediaRecorder, and negative-timestamp elst compensation (verified to 0.02 ms). The residual on unknown MediaRecorder platforms stays under 44 ms, below the audio-late perception threshold.

The avcC may differ between encoder instances on some Android or iOS encoders, which breaks the packet-copy title-card splice. Mitigation: byte-compare at runtime and fall back to the full render pass automatically. Nothing is spliced unverified.

Some Android SoCs expose only one or two hardware encoder sessions. Mitigation: the one-hardware-encoder rule. The live encoder is flushed and closed before any editor, DOM-replay or card encode, and recreated on resume as a new epoch.

Encoder reclaimed (QuotaExceededError) after long backgrounding, or a platform encode error. Mitigation: the error callback starts a new epoch with a forced keyframe. The ring keeps per-epoch avcC. Cross-epoch clips splice when the avcC matches, and otherwise re-render the older portion with the real length stated.

Players ignoring edit lists would show up to 1 s of pre-roll and a 21-44 ms audio lead. Mitigation: the elst is standard ISO BMFF and honoured by ffmpeg in tests; QuickTime/AVFoundation acceptance is on the device matrix. Where a platform is found to ignore elst, clip starts fall back to keyframe-snapped (1 s GOP) trims.

Memory on low-RAM phones: about 45 MB video ring budget, 11.5 MB/min PCM and about 1 MB/min AAC. Mitigation: 30 s rings on deviceMemory <= 2 or after any allocation or quota failure. availableSec is surfaced in the UI, and budget-driven trims are never silent.

The AAC harness Output on a NullTarget could grow over hour-long sessions. Mitigation: fastStart 'fragmented', which keeps no per-sample list. A 60-minute heap-flat test is on the verification list. The fallback is rotating the harness every 10 min with a 1024+P sample PCM overlap at the join.

T2 MediaRecorder keyframe cadence on iOS 15-16.3 is unverified (proven only on Safari 26.5). Mitigation: an arm-time self-check parses fragment sync flags and switches to two staggered recorders when keyframe-led fragments come less often than every 5 s.

Chromium's 50 MiB Web Share cap blocks sharing long recordings. Mitigation: an automatic 'share copy' render at 45 MiB or less, plus the download path. The cap is stated in the UI rather than failing at the share tap.

OPFS eviction on Safari (LRU / 7-day no-interaction) can delete My Clips and recordings. Mitigation: persist() on first record, 'Save to Photos' framed as the durable copy, and crash-safe committed fragments.

LGPL obligations for FFmpeg AAC. Mitigation: build from a pinned FFmpeg release tarball with a reproducible script and checksums, host the source next to the binary, add the credits notice, and never use --enable-gpl. @mediabunny/aac-encoder is not shipped as-is.

Patent exposure of the self-distributed WASM H.264 encoder (T3 only, well under 1% of users). Mitigation: T3 is isolated behind a flag and loaded only when T1 and T2 fail. Legal facts are recorded in openQuestions for Jack's decision. The primary tiers use platform encoders licensed by Apple, Google and Microsoft.
mediabunny releases almost daily and has had platform-specific regressions. Mitigation: pin 1.60.0 exactly, keep the Node mux test suite as a regression net, and bump deliberately.

Clock mapping jitter on Android, where currentTime advances in 10-20 ms callback bursts. Mitigation: an 8 s rolling median of (perf - currentTime) with re-anchoring on state change or a jump over 50 ms. The expected error is 5-10 ms, well inside A/V tolerance.
rejectedAlternatives: MediaRecorder as the primary encoder. There is no keyframe-aligned ring control on most engines, it emits fragmented zero-duration MP4, Safari defaults to 10 Mbps, there is no per-frame drop control, and it writes no priming elst. It is kept only as tier T2 for pre-16.4 WebKit.
Recording the raw DPR-sized game canvas. The spike measured Monster Truck collapsing from 41 to 4-6 fps. A fixed 720p-class compositor is required.

transferControlToOffscreen compositor in the worker. WebGL without preserveDrawingBuffer must be read in the render task on the main thread. A per-frame ImageBitmap hand-off adds cost for no gain, since VideoFrame creation measured about 0.1 ms in Chrome.

canvas.captureStream plus MediaStreamTrackProcessor as the T1 frame source. Chrome exposes MSTP only on Window and Safari only in workers (BCD), so it is not universal. It is reserved as a per-device optimization if Safari's VideoFrame cost proves too high on real iPhones.

SharedArrayBuffer ring or AudioWorklet ring. The site is not cross-origin isolated (verified). COEP would break the cdn.emulatorjs.org and Cloudflare Insights loads, and Safari lacks COEP credentialless.

Encoding audio only at clip time from PCM. It measured 100-160 ms natively and 560 ms for the polyfill on an M5, and would be several times slower on phones. Replaced by a continuous AAC ring, with PCM kept for the editor.
Keeping only an AAC ring. Perfect junctions, jingles and mixing need PCM, and iOS 16.4-18 has no AudioDecoder.

Shipping @mediabunny/aac-encoder as-is. It embeds an unpinned FFmpeg (Lavc62.23.103) with no LGPL notice or corresponding source, is SIMD-only, and needs one nested-worker postMessage per 1024 samples (560 ms for 30 s). Replaced by our own pinned in-process FFmpeg aacenc build.
ffmpeg.wasm. It is GPL-flavoured, about 10 MB, takes minutes per clip, and needs COOP/COEP.
x264 WASM (GPL) and a self-built OpenH264 WASM (BSD code but no patent coverage for non-Cisco binaries, and larger). minih264 (CC0) is chosen for T3.
VP8/VP9 WebM output, including remuxing WebM into MP4. The codec stays VP8/VP9, which iOS Photos will not import. Allowed only as a labelled last resort.

avc3 / in-band SPS-PPS to allow mixed encoder configs in one track. Apple Photos/AVFoundation acceptance of avc3 progressive MP4 is unverified. Byte-identical avcC plus a render-pass fallback is safer.
Reconfiguring the encoder on rotation or resize. That creates avcC epochs that break ring clips. A fixed output preset with letterboxing is used instead.
Full re-encode for every trim or card. It is slow on phones. elst trims and the smart-cut splice (verified) are used instead, with the render pass as the fallback.
mediabunny Conversion for trims. It copies only at keyframe boundaries (expand or shrink) and has no smart cut. Our negative-timestamp packet copy is frame-exact.

Two overlapping MediaRecorders as the default for T2. That doubles hardware encode load on the weakest phones. A single recorder plus a fragment ring works when fragments are keyframe-led (proven on Safari 26.5), and dual recorders remain only as the self-check fallback.

mediabunny VideoSampleSource or CanvasSource for the live path. Its await-based backpressure (queue >= 4) cannot express 'drop, never wait', and it hides keyframe and epoch control. It is used for offline render passes only.
hardwareAcceleration 'prefer-hardware'. It rejects software-only devices, including Chrome Android's new OpenH264 fallback. 'no-preference' plus probe-encode is used instead.
getOutputTimestamp for A/V mapping. It includes output latency (Bluetooth adds 150-250 ms) that must not end up in recordings.
A hard 10-minute cap on Record mode. It is arbitrary. The limit is derived from storage.estimate() and handles QuotaExceededError gracefully, with the share-size cap solved by a share-copy render.
openQuestions: T3 WASM H.264 (Firefox Android, Chrome Android < 150 without HW H.264, iOS < 15.4) is a self-distributed H.264 encoder. The last US AVC pool patents expire 2027-09-09. Via LA's AVC license charges $0 for the first 100,000 units per year but requires signing. mattdesl suspended mp4-h264 over MPEG LA enforcement worries. Jack decides: (a) sign the free Via LA tier and ship T3 now, (b) ship T3 now and accept the risk, or (c) ship T3 dark and enable it after 2027-09-09. Recommendation: (a) or (c). T1 and T2 cover well over 99% of visitors with platform-licensed encoders.

Whether the audio-bus track guarantees exactly one AudioContext per page. The engine supports N taps with resample-and-mix, but single-context is cheaper and should be the stated contract for kid-built games.

Physical devices are required and cannot be substituted: an iPhone on iOS 26, an iPhone on iOS 18 (XS/XR class), an iPhone or iPad on iOS 15.x/16.0-16.3 (hand-me-down iPhone 7/8 class), a low-end Android, a school Chromebook, and Firefox Android. Who in the household can provide them, or should BrowserStack-style real-device time be used? A paid service would conflict with the no-paid-services rule, so the answer is probably family devices.

Scratch side effects of this research: four Safari tabs pointing at http://127.0.0.1:8765 (test pages, now inert because the server was stopped) remain open in Jack's Safari. They were not closed, to avoid touching his other tabs.

verdicts.claim: mediabunny 1.60.0 is current (2026-09-25); since 1.56.0 the ISOBMFF muxer accepts negative timestamps and writes an elst that trims them
AudioSampleSource checks registered custom encoders before native AudioEncoder, and the native output callback repairs the WebKit 302253 description before onEncodedPacket
verdicts.correction: The repair fires only when the description is missing, shorter than 2 bytes, or parses to objectType 0. If Safari 27 or a later build emits a different wrong ASC (for example the right object type with a wrong sampling-frequency index), the repair will not fire. For AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo the ASC is deterministic ('1190'), so override it unconditionally with ascFor(sr,ch) instead of detecting.

verdicts.claim: WebKit 302253 is still NEW and was reproduced on Safari 26.5; mediabunny's path fixes it
verdicts.correction: Safari 26.5 is two releases stale. Safari 27 and iOS 27 shipped on 2026-09-14 per the BCD 8.1.3 browsers table, so the whole Safari evidence set needs a rerun on 27. The test Mac runs Darwin 25.5 (macOS 26.5).

verdicts.claim: Priming compensation (shift audio by -P/sr and let mediabunny write an elst) makes A/V sync exact to 0.02 ms
sources: /tmp/hh-clips/proto/out/chrome3-clip30.mp4: video elst (1699200, 15, 65536) at mdhd timescale 30, i.e. 0.5 s pre-roll; audio elst (1692363, 3842, 65536) at timescale 48000, i.e. 0.080 s pre-roll (parsed locally)
https://developer.android.com/media/media3/exoplayer/troubleshooting ('does not truncate audio samples or preroll media for edits that don't start on a synchronization sample')

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/ExoPlayer/release-v2/library/extractor/src/main/java/com/google/android/exoplayer2/extractor/mp4/AtomParsers.java:757-760 ('we advance to the next sync sample instead')
androidx/media tags 1.1.0-1.4.0 (advance) vs 1.5.0+ (walk back to the previous keyframe), BoxParser.java:928
verdicts.correction: The result is exact only in players that honor elst with pre-roll (ffmpeg, AVFoundation, Media3 1.5 and later). The audio and video pre-rolls differ (0.080 s vs 0.5 s, and up to 1 s with 1 s GOPs). A player that ignores elst therefore plays audio 0.42-0.92 s ahead of video. ExoPlayer 2.x and Media3 up to 1.4, which many Android apps still bundle, drop video up to the next keyframe, so the clip opens with up to 1 s of missing picture.

verdicts.claim: Muxing a 30 s clip by packet copy takes 12.8-19 ms, so 'Clip it!' is essentially free
sources: ffprobe chrome3-clip30.mp4 and safari-clip30.mp4: video duration 29.500 s, audio duration 29.381 s, last audio pts 29.36 s vs last video pts 29.467 s
verdicts.correction: The timing holds for a synthetic 2D canvas on an M5. However, the produced clips end their audio about 0.12 s before the video. With the spec's 250 ms jitter buffer plus encoder latency, the gap will be 0.3 s or more on real devices. Clip end must be min(video end, AAC watermark), or the build must wait until the AAC ring reaches the video end.

verdicts.claim: Frame-accurate start trim with no re-encode via negative timestamps plus elst
sources: androidx/media BoxParser.java:875-940 (Media3 1.5+ walks back to the sync sample; earlier versions skip forward)
verdicts.correction: The trim is valid ISO BMFF and ffmpeg honors it. Android playback depends on the ExoPlayer or Media3 version that each app embeds. Do not make instant 'Clip it!' depend on a video elst. Start the clip at the keyframe instead (at most 1 s longer, which a kid will not notice), and start the audio at that same instant. Reserve frame-exact starts for the editor, which should smart-cut (re-encode) only the first partial GOP.

verdicts.claim: Title-card splice by packet copy works because a second encoder with the identical config yields byte-identical avcC
sources: ITU-T H.264 7.4.3 (two consecutive IDR access units must differ in idr_pic_id)
verdicts.correction: This is proven only on desktop Chrome and Safari. Separately, when a smart-cut GOP is a single frame, two encoder instances can emit back-to-back IDRs with the same idr_pic_id, which violates the standard. Guarantee that each spliced GOP has at least 2 frames.

verdicts.claim: VideoFrame transfer to a worker plus worker-side encoding works in Safari and Chrome at about 0.1 ms (Chrome) and 1-2 ms (Safari) of main-thread cost
verdicts.correction: The transfer works. The cost figure comes from a synthetic 2D OffscreenCanvas with no drawImage of a WebGL canvas. It says nothing about the real compositor's GPU readback, which the feasibility spike measured at about 15% of frame budget.

verdicts.claim: SharedArrayBuffer is unavailable (no COOP/COEP), so transport must use transferable ArrayBuffers
sources: apps/web/next.config.ts:14-57 (no COOP/COEP headers; CSP worker-src 'self' blob:)

verdicts.claim: Chromium reclaims WebCodecs codecs only when the page is backgrounded, global pressure is exceeded, and the codec has been idle for 90 s
BCD 8.1.3 support matrix (VideoEncoder Safari 16.4, AudioEncoder Safari 26, none on Firefox Android, etc.)
verdicts.correction: The track omitted BCD facts that change the design. api.Navigator.share.data_files_parameter is false on Firefox desktop and Firefox Android, so T3 output there can never reach a share sheet. Navigator.share on Chrome desktop exists only on Windows and ChromeOS, so macOS and Linux Chrome are download-only. navigator.deviceMemory is Chromium-only. StorageManager.estimate arrived in Safari 17. LockManager arrived in Safari 15.4.

verdicts.claim: OpenH264 software H.264 is enabled by default on Chrome Android 150+, so Android devices without a hardware encoder can still encode H.264
sources: chromium commit 5dbbf03c80 (2025-10-24: flag added on Android, disabled by default)
verdicts.correction: This holds only for arm64 Chrome builds. 32-bit ARM Chrome, which ships to low-RAM and 32-bit-OS Android devices, is built without OpenH264. Those are the devices most likely to have a flaky or missing MediaCodec encoder.

verdicts.claim: Field data: avc1.42001f encodable in 99.7% of sessions (Chrome Android 99.79%)
sources: https://webcodecsfundamentals.org/codecs/mp4a.40.2.html (AAC encode: iOS Safari 69.99%, Chrome Android 96.89%, Firefox ~0%)
verdicts.correction: The numbers match the page. They measure isConfigSupported, not a successful encode, on a developer-audience site, so they are not a kids' low-end-phone population. The same dataset shows that about 30% of iOS sessions (Jan-Mar 2026) have no AAC encoder, which confirms the WASM AAC need. It also shows almost no iOS sessions without VideoEncoder, which undercuts the case for building T2 and T3-lite.

verdicts.claim: The in-memory muxer writes chunks in add order, so clip assembly must interleave by timestamp
MediaRecorder with a 1 s timeslice yields keyframe-led fragments, which makes a T2 fragment ring viable for iOS 15.4-16.3
sources: apps/web/package.json and repo root: no browserslist override
verdicts.correction: This is proven only on Safari 26.5. More important, the site itself compiles for Safari 16.4 or later by default (Next 16), so the browsers T2 and T3-lite target are not guaranteed to run Hank's Hits at all.

verdicts.claim: Chromium Web Share rejects more than 10 files or more than 50 MiB
verdicts.correction: The track treats iOS as uncapped. WebKit ShareDataReader.cpp:52-86 reads each shared file fully into memory with FileReaderLoader ReadAsArrayBuffer, then copies it again with SharedBuffer::create. A multi-hundred-MB Record-mode file therefore needs about 2x its size in WebContent memory and will get jetsammed. iOS has a practical cap that must be measured.

verdicts.claim: The fragmented AAC harness on a NullTarget keeps no per-sample list, so memory stays bounded
sources: /tmp/hh-clips/pkgs/mediabunny-1.60.0/package/src/isobmff/isobmff-muxer.ts:1184 (samples pushed into currentChunk), 1390-1403 (only sample.data nulled; chunk pushed to finalizedChunks forever), 58-66 (Sample object shape)

verdicts.claim: Fragmented-MP4 crash recovery: truncate at a committed moof, then finalize with fastStart 'reserve'
verdicts.correction: Proven in Node only. Recovery on next load must skip partial files that another tab still holds open: createSyncAccessHandle takes an exclusive lock, so a second tab will throw on an active recording.

designSpecProblems: Code bug, section 4.5: `new Quality(128000)` is a QUALITATIVE factor of 128000, not a bitrate. Quality(number) maps to {quality:number} (encode.ts:705-708), and the AAC bitrate snaps to the nearest valid rate, so every AAC stream and the canEncodeAudio probe run at 192 kbps. All the size math is off. Use `new Quality({ bitrate: 128000 })`.

The AAC harness (mediabunny AudioSampleSource on a fragmented NullTarget Output) is not memory-bounded. Sample objects accumulate in finalizedChunks (isobmff-muxer.ts:1184, 1402). It is also unnecessary. Call AudioEncoder directly, with an unconditional ascFor() description override (the spec already builds ascFor for calibration). Call the custom WASM encoder directly too. Use mediabunny only to mux. The 'rotate every 10 min' idea would then be moot.

Audio clock drift is not actually corrected. Both encoders count samples from the first timestamp: the WASM encoder via nextSampleTimestampInSamples (encoder.ts:150-151), and native output snapped to the sample rate. mediabunny pads gaps of 64 samples or more with silence and ignores overlaps (media-source.ts:2022-2050). The muxer throws on backward timestamps (muxer.ts:62-71). The 'rolling median' clock map therefore changes nothing in the encoded stream. At about 50 ppm the result is about 180 ms/hour of A/V drift, or 1.3 ms silence clicks every ~27 s, or a crashed ring. Drive the Hermite resampler ratio from the clock map (a PLL) and feed contiguous sample-counted timestamps.

Live timeline with no audio: a suspended context (game mute via ctx.suspend(), iOS 'interrupted', the pre-gesture autoplay lock), or a game with no AudioContext at all. mediabunny fills the gap later with ONE Float32Array of sampleDiff x channels (media-source.ts:2042). Ten minutes suspended means about 230 MB allocated in a single call, which will OOM. Until then, the AAC ring ends before the video. The worker must synthesize chunked silence in real time for every live span that has no tap data.

Clip end is short on audio: the prototype's own clips end audio 0.12 s before video (ffprobe chrome3-clip30.mp4: 29.381 s vs 29.500 s). The 250 ms jitter buffer makes this worse. Set endUs = min(videoRing.endUs, aacWatermark), or delay assembly until the AAC watermark passes the video end.

Pre-roll mismatch: video pre-roll 0.5 s vs audio 0.080 s (parsed elsts). Players that ignore elst desync by 0.42-0.92 s, and ExoPlayer 2.x and Media3 up to 1.4 skip video to the next keyframe (AtomParsers.java:757-760). The 'mitigation' in the risk list ('up to 1 s of pre-roll and a 21-44 ms audio lead') is wrong. Start instant clips at the keyframe with audio aligned to the same instant, and use the editor smart-cut for exact starts.

Keyframe starvation is not guarded. Chromium Android configures MediaCodec with kDefaultGOPLength 3000 frames, which is 100 s at 30 fps (ndk_video_encode_accelerator.cc:58, 480-485), and relies on async 'request-sync' (1176-1182). If a vendor encoder ignores or delays it, VideoRing's single current GOP can never be evicted (the loop needs gops.length > 1), so memory grows without limit. A 30 s clip would then carry up to 100 s of elst pre-roll. Probe the keyframe response at arm time. Fall back to periodic re-configure() with the identical config (a byte-identical avcC keeps it seamless), or to a smart-cut of the leading partial GOP.

Video timestamp grid: `Math.round(tlUs/(1e6/fps)) * Math.round(1e6/fps)` equals n x 33333 at 30 fps, which drifts -10 µs/s (36 ms/hour vs audio, 72 ms after 2 hours). Switching grids when fps adapts creates jumps. Compute ts = Math.round(n * 1e6 / fps) from a frame index instead.

The fps ladder 30->24->20->15 contains 24, which is not an integer divisor of a 60 Hz rAF. It produces 2-3-2-3 cadence judder. Steps must divide the MEASURED rAF rate (60 Hz: 30/20/15; 120 Hz: 30/24/20/15). Separately, `addVideoTrack(vs, { frameRate: fps })` sets timescale 30 (isobmff-muxer.ts:460-465), which snaps adapted 24/20 fps frames onto a 1/30 grid unevenly. Use frameRate 120 (exact for 30/24/20/15) or omit it.

iframe clock domain: rAF callbacks receive a time relative to the document's OWN time origin (HTML 'update the rendering': 'relative high resolution time given frameTimestamp and doc's relevant global object'). The four-wheeler srcdoc and EmulatorJS rAF wrappers therefore hand the parent pump a timestamp offset by the iframe's creation time. FramePump must ignore caller timestamps or convert through performance.timeOrigin. The same applies to any worker-side performance.now() use.

The fps governor looks only at main-thread paint time (EWMA of performance.now deltas). A WebGL-to-2D readback and GPU or encoder contention show up as GAME frame time, not paint time, and Safari coarsens the timer to 1 ms. The controlling signal must be the game's rAF interval or long-frame ratio while armed, compared with an unarmed baseline. The device-matrix target (at most 10% fps loss) must be enforced at runtime, not only measured.

Software-encoder blindness: pickVideoConfig uses 'no-preference' and never learns whether it got a hardware or a software encoder (OpenH264 on Android, platform SW elsewhere). A 720p30 software encode next to a 3D game will crater fps. Probe 'prefer-hardware' first. If only 'no-preference' passes, drop to a 480p or 360p preset at 20 fps.

Low-memory policy keys on navigator.deviceMemory, which is Chromium-only (BCD). The iPhones most at risk of jetsam (2 GB iPhone 7/8 class) never get the 30 s ring. iOS needs its own conservative default, for example keyed on iOS major version or screen class, with a crash-loop detector that downgrades after an unexpected reload.

Record-mode storage guard depends on estimate(), which Safari only has from 17. The 60% quota also only exists from Safari 17 (WebKit blog 14403), yet the spec lists iOS 16.4-18 as T1. Provide a quota-probe fallback: write-ahead preallocation or truncate test, plus QuotaExceededError handling alone.

The iOS share path is capped in practice. ShareDataReader.cpp:52-86 loads the whole file with ReadAsArrayBuffer and copies it into a SharedBuffer, so at about 23 MB/min a 20-minute recording needs about 1 GB of WebContent memory. Measure the ceiling on device, and route large files to a download to Files or to the hosted link.

The 'share copy at 45 MiB' fix does not scale. A 20-minute recording at 45 MiB leaves about 170 kbps of video, which is unwatchable. Set a quality floor, for example 720p needs at least ~1.2 Mbps, which is about 4.5 min per 45 MiB. Above the floor, offer download, the hosted link, or split parts (Chromium also caps the TOTAL across 10 files at 50 MiB, so splitting does not help Web Share). macOS and Linux Chrome have no navigator.share at all (BCD), so download must be primary there.

T2 and T3-lite target Safari below 16.4. Next 16's default browserslist is safari 16.4 / chrome 111 / firefox 111 (modern-browserslist-target.js), and the repo sets no override, so the site is not guaranteed to hydrate on those devices. The field dataset also shows almost no iOS sessions without VideoEncoder. Decide from Hank's Hits' own Cloudflare UA analytics before building two whole tiers. Either lower browserslist site-wide and test every game on iOS 15, or show an honest 'update your iPhone' state.

T3 (minih264 WASM) was benchmarked only on a desktop M5 (18 ms/frame at 360p). On phones, alongside the game, it is unlikely to hold 15 fps. Its main audience (Firefox Android) cannot share files at all (BCD data_files_parameter false). The spec rejects WebM because of iOS Photos, but for Firefox Android a native MediaRecorder VP8/Opus WebM file has no patent question, plays in Android galleries, and plays in iOS Safari via a hosted link (caniuse webm 'y' iOS 18.4-27.2). It is the stronger path to benchmark first.

The OpenH264 fallback does not exist on 32-bit ARM Chrome (media_options.gni:59-61). The tier matrix line 'Chrome Android 150+ without a hardware H.264 encoder uses OpenH264' is false for low-end devices on 32-bit Chrome, so they fall to T3.

Multi-tab: two armed game tabs mean two hardware encoders and 2x ring memory, which violates the spec's own one-hardware-session rule. Record-mode recovery would also try to truncate another tab's live partial file (the exclusive sync-handle lock throws). Use Web Locks (Safari 15.4+) so only the focused tab arms, hold a per-recording lock, and skip locked files during recovery.

Worker lifetime: the engine worker is terminated on GameShell unmount, so a 'Clip it!' result or auto-highlight held in memory is lost when the kid taps Home. Persist every clip and highlight to OPFS the moment it is built, and await pending OPFS writes and Record finalize before termination. Alternatively, hoist the engine to a root layout that survives route changes.

Editor audio for saved clips: PcmRing covers only the last ~62 s, but the editor re-renders all audio from PCM. Editing a My Clips item later means decoding its AAC, and iOS 16.4-18.x has no AudioDecoder. Add a WASM AAC decoder (FFmpeg aacdec in the same pinned build), or a main-thread decodeAudioData fallback, or persist lossless PCM alongside each saved clip.

Auto-highlights on every brag event (every level clear, every high score) accumulate without limit in memory and OPFS on a kid's phone. Retention policy is unspecified. Eviction must be explicit and visible in the UI, never silent.

T2's compositor canvas at 1x1 CSS px with opacity 0: WebKit fixed the off-DOM case (bug 240380, 2022), but invisible or offscreen canvases can still be throttled. This is untested on iOS 15/16 and belongs in the device matrix.

The HD preset 1920x1088 ships 8 junk rows, because mediabunny does not crop and the encoder gets 1088. The multiple-of-16 rule is self-imposed: mediabunny rejects only ODD dimensions, and H.264 encoders crop 1080 through the SPS. Use 1920x1080.
The tap worklet allocates a new Int16Array every 42.7 ms on the real-time audio thread, which invites GC glitches on low-end Android. Recycle a pool of buffers that the worker transfers back.

Dynamic taps: four-wheeler-3d creates three separate AudioContexts (Hunting.tsx:185, TransportActions.tsx:321, radioAudio.ts:65), and the radio creates and closes a context on every start and stop. The mixer watermark must exclude closed or suspended streams, or the whole AAC ring stalls waiting for a dead stream. Hooking contexts must also work for contexts created mid-session.

Prototype versions are stale for a 'proven' claim: Chrome 153 vs current stable 155 (chromiumdash), and Safari 26.5 vs current Safari/iOS 27 (released 2026-09-14). Rerun the whole prototype on current releases before the matrix.
missedIssues: Colorimetry: nobody checked the colr/VUI (BT.601 vs BT.709, limited vs full range) that each platform encoder writes for RGB canvas input, against how it actually converted the pixels. A mismatch shows up as washed-out or oversaturated clips in Photos or WhatsApp. Add a color-bar fixture to the device matrix and set colorSpace explicitly.

Battery and thermal cost of always-on replay: a continuous 30 fps compositor readback plus a hardware encode for an hour of play on a phone. The spec needs an 'Instant replay on/off' control and auto-disable when the game-fps governor bottoms out. It should also avoid arming during menus or the start overlay (GameShell) when nothing is being played.

A generic capture path for FUTURE kid-built games: the pump contract depends on per-game hooks (addAfterEffect, end-of-draw calls). A GameShell-installed requestAnimationFrame dispatcher would run all game rAF callbacks and then composite in the same task. That catches every canvas or WebGL game, including R3F and new ones, with zero per-game code. The per-game hooks would then only add overlays and brag events. The catch is that games rendering from setInterval (monster-truck and space-invaders use setInterval per a grep of src/games) still need an explicit hook.

Unevaluated alternative compositor: transfer VideoFrame(sourceCanvas) to the worker (cheap in Chrome, 0.04 ms measured) and scale and composite there in an OffscreenCanvas. This moves the ~15% main-thread compositor cost off the game thread. The spec rejected only transferControlToOffscreen and ImageBitmap hand-off. A/B it on iPhone, where VideoFrame(canvas) may force a CPU readback.

Use Hank's Hits' own traffic (Cloudflare fronts the site) to get the real iOS, Android, Chrome-bitness and Firefox version mix before committing to T2, T3 and T3-lite. Per the standing research rule, the webcodecsfundamentals percentages describe that site's visitors, not ours.

In-app browsers and WKWebView shells (Chrome, Firefox and Edge on iOS; links opened inside messaging apps) get the 15% storage quota and inconsistent navigator.share. Capability detection must cover share-availability, not just encoders.
The splice and IDR rule: consecutive IDRs from two encoder instances need distinct idr_pic_id (H.264 7.4.3). Enforce GOPs of 2 frames or more in card and smart-cut sessions.

Audio sources the tap cannot see: HTMLMediaElement playback (new Audio()) and speechSynthesis never reach a WebAudio tap. Leaving read-aloud out of clips is correct. A kid-built game using new Audio(), however, would record silent unless the audio-bus track routes it through createMediaElementSource. The make-a-game skill should forbid bare new Audio().

Scratch cruft from the prior research: four Safari tabs at http://127.0.0.1:8765 are still open in Jack's Safari. They can be closed safely by URL match only (osascript over Safari windows/tabs whose URL starts with http://127.0.0.1:8765), without touching other tabs. Close them rather than leaving them.

Record mode's own fragmented Output has the same per-sample retention as the AAC harness (~77 objects/s). Multi-hour recordings should roll to a new fragment file (or a new Output) every N minutes and concatenate at finalize.
verify.summary:
I ran independent checks against mediabunny 1.60.0 source, Chromium/WebKit/Media3 source, BCD 8.1.3, and ffprobe/elst parsing of the track's own output files.

**What held up:** the mediabunny version and negative-timestamp elst, custom-before-native AAC selection, the WebKit 302253 repair, the Next 16.2 worker regression and its 16.3.0 fix, the 50 MiB Chromium share cap, SAB absence, the codec-reclamation rules, and the aac-encoder licensing facts.

**What did not hold up:**
- The 'bounded' fragmented AAC harness is refuted: mediabunny keeps every Sample object in finalizedChunks.
- The spec's `new Quality(128000)` is a quality factor, so AAC silently runs at 192 kbps.
- Clock drift is not actually corrected. The encoders count samples, mediabunny pads gaps and ignores overlaps, and the muxer throws on backward timestamps.
- A suspended AudioContext makes mediabunny allocate one huge silence buffer.
- The track's own clips end audio 0.12 s before video.
- Audio and video pre-roll differ (0.08 s vs 0.5 s), so players that ignore elst desync by 0.4-0.9 s. ExoPlayer 2.x and Media3 up to 1.4 drop video up to the next keyframe.
- Chromium Android's 100 s default GOP means an ignored keyframe request makes the video ring unbounded.
- OpenH264 is absent from 32-bit ARM Chrome.
- iOS share loads whole files into memory twice.
- Safari's 60% quota and estimate() start at 17.
- deviceMemory is Chromium-only.
- iframe rAF timestamps use the iframe's own time origin.
- Video timestamp quantization drifts 36 ms/hour, and the 24 fps step judders at 60 Hz.
- T2 and T3-lite target browsers below Next 16's Safari 16.4 baseline.
- T3's WASM H.264 is unproven on phones, and Firefox Android cannot share files anyway.
- All the 'proven' results are on Safari 26.5 and Chrome 153, while current releases are Safari 27 and Chrome 155.

**Recommended fixes:**
- Start instant clips at the keyframe with audio aligned to it, and keep frame-exact starts for editor smart-cuts.
- Use a PLL-driven resampler with contiguous timestamps and worker-synthesized silence.
- Drop the NullTarget harness and use AudioEncoder directly with an unconditional ASC override.
- Govern capture on game fps rather than paint time.
- Use Web Locks for multi-tab arming and recovery.
- Persist clips and highlights to OPFS immediately.
- Decide T2, T3 and T3-lite from the site's own Cloudflare traffic.

findings.topic: Headless shell is not a valid stand-in
findings.claim: Playwright's default headless Chromium is chromium_headless_shell. It has no navigator.share or canShare. Its GPU is SwiftShader. It supports only software H.264 (isConfigSupported is false with prefer-hardware), and its output is about 2x larger (302 KB vs 158 KB for the same 150 frames). Branded Chrome with headless=true (channel 'chrome') ran on the real 'ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M5' and the hardware encoder. The automated gate should therefore use channel 'chrome' (headed or headless-new), never the headless shell.

On this Mac, Google Chrome 153.0.8010.53 takes 8.7 to 38.3 s to emit the first chunk (TTFC) from the FIRST hardware H.264 VideoEncoder configured with latencyMode 'realtime'. It reproduced 8 times: headed, headless, fresh profile, persistent profile, Baseline and High, 1280x720 and 640x360. Frames queue without limit meanwhile (encodeQueueSize reached 150, which was every frame submitted). Under the same conditions the TTFC was 212 ms with latencyMode 'quality', 145 ms with prefer-software, about 0.54-0.65 s in Chromium 151 (CfT), and 98 ms in Safari 26.5. After the first session starts, later encoders in the same page start in about 33 ms. A 64x64 warm-up encoder did not prevent the stall. The root cause is unknown and I found no existing Chromium bug. Consequences: the always-on replay could be blind for the first 10-40 s of play and hold unbounded GPU frames. TTFC must be a gated metric, and branded Chrome stable and beta channels must be in the matrix.

findings.topic: AAC priming breaks A/V sync differently per decoder family
findings.claim: Test pattern: a white frame and a 1 kHz beep at every whole second. Offsets were measured with ffmpeg (the family used by Chrome, Android and most web players) and with AVFoundation (the family used by iOS Photos, Messages and Safari). (a) Native AAC from Chrome or Safari through AudioToolbox has 2112 priming samples and no edit list: ffmpeg +44.0 ms (audio late), AVFoundation 0 ms. (b) The same file with input timestamps shifted by -2112/48000 (mediabunny writes elst media_time=2112, no roll group): ffmpeg 0 to 1.6 ms, AVFoundation -44 ms (audio early). (c) The WASM @mediabunny/aac-encoder file has 1024 priming samples: ffmpeg +21.4 ms, AVFoundation -22.6 ms. (d) The ffmpeg-authored reference has elst plus sgpd/sbgp roll groups: 0 ms in both. Apple documents an implicit 2112-sample delay and explicit signalling through an edit list plus sample groups. mediabunny #444 (open) reports that elst alone is interpreted inconsistently and that elst plus roll group is correct. So A/V sync MUST be verified in both decoder families, and priming is encoder-specific (2112 vs 1024), so it must be measured per platform.

(1) WebKit bug 302253 is still present in Safari 26.5. AudioEncoder's decoderConfig.description is a full ES_Descriptor ('0380808022...0580808002 1190...'), not a 2-byte AudioSpecificConfig, so a naive parser reads objectType 0. mediabunny's AudioSampleSource replaces it (the muxed file has a valid 2-byte ASC). This is the same bug class that produced the unplayable 'Audio object type 0' files in mediabunny #173. (2) When AudioData chunks are not multiples of 1024 frames (4800 in the probe), WebKit emits AAC packets with irregular timestamps (deltas of 704 and 1728 samples). In ffmpeg this gave a +55 to +61 ms offset drifting about 2 ms/s. With 1024-aligned input the deltas were uniform 1024 and the offset was a constant 44 ms. Chrome's timestamps were uniform either way.

Safari 26.5 on macOS reported the following. VideoEncoder isConfigSupported is true for avc1 (Baseline, Main, High), hvc1, vp8, vp09 and av01 at 540p through 1080p. It is even true for Baseline 3.1 at 1920x1080, which Chrome rejects. AudioEncoder supports mp4a.40.2, mp4a.40.5 and opus. MediaRecorder supports video/mp4 but emits 'avc1.42000a' Constrained Baseline. OPFS works on the main thread including createWritable (new in Safari 26), and SyncAccessHandle works in a worker. canShare is true for mp4, webm, mov, png and even a .bin name. userActivation.isActive is false at load. AudioContext is 'suspended' without a gesture. Storage quota is 78,643 MB. hardwareConcurrency is reported as 8 (the machine has 10). Missing APIs: ImageDecoder, MediaStreamTrackProcessor, SharedArrayBuffer (not cross-origin isolated). The worker encode, the mediabunny MP4 and the MediaRecorder MP4 all pass ffprobe and AVFoundation isPlayable.

iOS 27 and Safari 27 shipped with Xcode 27 in September 2026. Safari 27 notes include a WebCodecs VideoDecoder B-frame ordering fix and color-space overrides for hardware decoders. There are no new MediaRecorder or Web Share items. The matrix must cover iOS 27, iOS 26 (first with AudioEncoder) and at least one pre-26 iOS for the no-AudioEncoder fallback.

Playwright's default Chromium switches include --disable-background-timer-throttling, --disable-renderer-backgrounding, --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows and --disable-back-forward-cache. In Playwright Chrome, userActivation.isActive was true and AudioContext was 'running' at page load. Real Safari showed false and 'suspended'. Tests of backgrounding and codec reclamation must use ignoreDefaultArgs to remove those switches. Tests of the activation window must not trust automation-granted activation.

findings.topic: Validators must run outside the producing browser
findings.claim: Each browser's own <video> reported a finite duration for its own files, and files that pass in-browser can still be broken elsewhere (#173's 'audio object type 0' passed backend checks). Validation in this plan is off-device: ffprobe/ffmpeg (structure, frame count, decode, sync), plus a Swift AVFoundation checker built with the CLT (isPlayable, isExportable, track formats, sync as iOS decodes it). Both ran on every probe output. Separately, WebKit returns a black frame from drawImage(video) unless the frame has been presented; this was fixed by attaching the element, calling play() muted, and waiting for requestVideoFrameCallback.

findings.topic: WASM AAC fallback works under the production CSP
findings.claim: @mediabunny/aac-encoder 1.60.0 (a 972 KB min.mjs that imports the bare specifier 'mediabunny', so it needs an import map or bundler) encodes and muxes under a CSP identical to apps/web/next.config.ts:33-35 (script-src 'unsafe-eval', worker-src 'self' blob:). It produced valid AAC-LC (extradata 5 B) with 1024-sample priming. Every probed desktop browser has native AAC, so this path runs only on browsers without an AAC AudioEncoder (Firefox, iOS before 26, probably Linux/ChromeOS Chrome), or when forced with ?forceWasmAac=1 in the lab.

findings.topic: Chrome AAC encoder is OS-backed; ChromeOS/Linux unverified
findings.claim: Chromium's AAC AudioEncoder uses platform encoders (Media Foundation on Windows, AudioToolbox on macOS; issue text: 'only on Windows and Mac'). Whether ChromeOS or Android Chrome exposes native AAC encode is not established. The Chromebook and Android device rows decide whether the WASM AAC path is the common path on school Chromebooks. Priming also differs per OS encoder.

In the upscaler.video codec dataset (about 320k sessions per codec, a desktop-heavy adult audience, not kids), VideoEncoder support for avc1.42001f was: iOS Safari 100.0% (31,155/31,156), Chrome Android 99.79%, Chrome ChromeOS/Linux 98.9%, Firefox Android 0%. For avc1.640028: Chrome Android 96.22%, iOS Safari 99.99%. Encoder availability is close to universal on the target browsers, but this data says nothing about realtime throughput, file correctness or share behavior. Those are what device testing must prove.

On iOS Safari 26.x, VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported throws a native TypeError ('Type error') for some configs instead of returning {supported:false}. mediabunny fixed its own call sites after 1.52.3. The probe and the production capability check must wrap every isConfigSupported call and record a 'throw' outcome separately from 'false'.

pymobiledevice3 11.19.4 (pip wheel 1.3 MB) provides `webinspector opened-tabs`, `js-shell` (also `--automation`), `launch URL`, and a `cdp` bridge on 127.0.0.1:9222 that is documented for VS Code, Playwright and Puppeteer. `--native` on macOS rides Apple's remoted tunnel with no root, entitlement or Xcode. The device needs Settings > Apps > Safari > Advanced > Web Inspector (plus Remote Automation for launch/automation) on iOS 18+. Safari's Develop menu can inspect Home Screen web apps while they are in the foreground, and it supports inspection over the network after one cabled pairing.

Playwright's experimental _android (Node only) needs Chrome 87+ on the device, a running adb, and 'Enable command line on non-rooted devices' in chrome://flags. It supports Chrome and WebView and works with devices or AVDs. A lighter path: `adb forward tcp:9333 localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote` then chromium.connectOverCDP (use the default context). `adb reverse tcp:3200 tcp:3200` makes http://localhost:3200 on the phone a secure context, so no HTTPS is needed over USB. Emulator stack sizes, from Google's repository XML: emulator 37.3.1 aarch64 419.8 MB, cmdline-tools 23.0 155.4 MB, system image android-36 google_apis_playstore arm64 1.89 GB zip (android-37.0 is 2.26 GB). A JDK is also needed because none is installed.

WebCodecs, OPFS and Web Share require a secure context, so a LAN IP over http:// is useless. Options, all zero cost: (1) `tailscale serve --bg 3200` gives https://jackmb.tail463ffa.ts.net with a real certificate for tailnet devices (tailnet HTTPS is already enabled and Jack's iPhone is a tailnet node). (2) A cloudflared quick tunnel (2026.9.3, 19.8 MB tgz, no account) gives a random trycloudflare.com URL for devices off the tailnet, with a 200 in-flight request limit, no SSE, no SLA, and testing use only. (3) Android over USB via adb reverse to localhost. (4) The iOS Simulator reaches the Mac's localhost. Next.js blocks cross-origin requests to dev-only assets (allowedDevOrigins), so tunnel a `next build && next start` production build rather than `next dev`. auth.ts already sets trustHost: true (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:118).

iOS Simulator VideoToolbox encoding runs on the host and can diverge from real hardware: an Apple Developer Forums VideoToolbox report says encoding 'still works fine on the iOS 26 simulator, it only fails on real hardware'. Simulator (and Android emulator) codec, performance and thermal results are informational only. They are still valuable for API surface, UI flows, standalone web-app storage and share-sheet invocation.

(1) Safari Advanced Fingerprinting Protection (on by default in Private Browsing, optional for all browsing) injects noise into 2D canvas and WebGL readback and into AudioBuffer and AudioWorklet sample reads. (2) Low Power Mode caps requestAnimationFrame at 30 fps in iOS Safari. (3) Since iOS 26, every site added to the Home Screen opens as a web app. WebKit grants persist() heuristically (for example to Home Screen web apps) and evicts best-effort storage. Each of these is a separate matrix mode.

Desktop Chrome 153 and Safari 26.5 on macOS both return canShare true for webm, mov and mismatched extensions. Share acceptance on iPhone (Save Video, Messages) and on Android targets can therefore only be proven on devices with a human tap. Automation can prove only the call shape: one File of type video/mp4 named *.mp4, called while userActivation.isActive is true.

findings.topic: Repo facts relevant to the harness
findings.claim: The repo is PUBLIC (jackneil/hanks-hits). vitest only includes src/**/*.{test,spec}.*, so Playwright specs under apps/web/e2e/ will not collide. The local gate is .githooks/pre-push (install, lint, typecheck, test, build). No Playwright dependency exists in the repo yet. Production CSP and headers live in apps/web/next.config.ts:13-56.

research.designSpec:
CLIPS DEVICE-VERIFICATION PLAN (Hank's Hits). Concrete, reproducible, no paid device clouds.

0. PRINCIPLES
- Prove each clip property at the cheapest tier that can observe it, and escalate only what that tier cannot see. Every tier writes the same verdict JSON into one results table.
- The producing browser never judges its own output. Every MP4 made on any device is pulled back to this Mac and judged by two independent decoder families: ffmpeg/ffprobe (the family Chrome, Android and web players use) and a Swift AVFoundation checker (the family iOS Photos, Messages and Safari use). Today's probes showed these two disagree on A/V sync by up to 44 ms for the same file.
- Test the branded browsers kids run, not stand-ins. The Playwright headless shell has no share and uses a software encoder. Bundled Chromium hid the Chrome 153 realtime-encoder stall.
- "Works" is decided on a real iPhone, a real Android phone and a real Chromebook, on the real surface: a tunnel to a production build before merge, then hankshits.com after deploy.

1. TIERS
T0 Unit (vitest, jsdom, part of the existing `pnpm --filter web test`). Pure logic in src/shared/clips/**/__tests__:
- ring-buffer eviction trims only at keyframes and keeps the last N seconds;
- audio PCM ring index math;
- timestamp rebasing, including AAC re-stamping to exact 1024-sample steps;
- the priming table (AudioToolbox 2112, libavcodec 1024) and the "elst + roll group" box writer;
- the share decision table (canShare files -> share; else download; else hosted link);
- brag-event debounce with pre/post-roll windows;
- filename and metadata PII scrub (only the leaderboard handle is allowed);
- the clip-size budget calculator.
T1 Mac automated browsers (Playwright 1.62 + safaridriver). Full functional suite against a production build with the lab enabled.
T2 Simulators (Xcode iOS Simulator, Android emulator). Covers the API surface, UI flows, standalone web-app storage and share-sheet invocation. Codec, performance and thermal numbers from simulators are informational only.
T3 Real devices. Scripted where possible (adb+CDP on Android; pymobiledevice3/safaridriver on iPhone), with a human checklist for the steps that need a real tap: share sheet, Save Video, Messages, lock screen, Low Power Mode, thermal.
T4 Field health, in production and privacy-safe. Anonymous counters with no identifiers and no raw user agent: a UA-family bucket, the capture path used, a TTFC bucket, fallback reason, and share outcome. Posted with navigator.sendBeacon to /api/clips/health, which only increments counters. This covers the device long tail no lab can hold. Enabling it needs Jack's privacy sign-off (see open questions).

2. THE CLIPS LAB (the fixture every tier drives)
- Route: apps/web/src/app/dev/clips-lab/page.tsx. It renders the REAL <GameShell> + ClipProvider with a TestPatternSource, so the true pipeline runs end to end. Gate: `if (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLIPS_LAB !== '1') notFound()`. The flag is set only for local and tunnel builds, never in Railway.
- TestPatternSource (src/shared/clips/testing/TestPatternSource.ts) is a canvas source registered like any game. Each frame draws:
  (a) a 16-cell black/white binary barcode of the frame index, 20 px cells at top-left, inside the safe area;
  (b) a full-white frame on the first frame of every whole second;
  (c) a moving bar;
  (d) the HUD overlay painter showing a test handle, so overlay presence can be asserted.
  Audio: a 1 kHz, 60 ms beep at every whole second, played through the shared game-audio bus. This proves the AudioWorklet tap path, not a side channel.
  Query knobs: ?mode=replay|highlight|record, ?secs=, ?orient=portrait|landscape, ?forceWasmAac=1, ?forceMediaRecorder=1, ?ablock=N (non-1024 audio chunking regression), ?brag=t1,t2.
- Probe module (src/shared/clips/testing/probe.ts). It is a port of /tmp/hh-clips/probe/probe.js and is reused by the lab and by T4. It records:
  - typeof for about 30 APIs;
  - a VideoEncoder isConfigSupported matrix (avc1 42001f/4d401f/640028, hvc1, vp8, vp09, av01 at 540p-1080p, both orientations, prefer-hardware and prefer-software), with 'throw' recorded separately from false (mediabunny #456);
  - an AudioEncoder matrix (mp4a.40.2 and .5, opus, flac, mp3);
  - the MediaRecorder type list;
  - a canShare matrix;
  - OPFS main-thread createWritable and worker SyncAccessHandle round trips, plus estimate() and persisted();
  - TTFC, max encodeQueueSize and throughput for the first and second encoders, in the main thread and in a worker;
  - the AAC description parse (detects WebKit 302253 ESDS);
  - AudioWorklet on an OfflineAudioContext;
  - whether a live AudioContext is suspended before a gesture;
  - a full mediabunny mux, with playback checked via play(), requestVideoFrameCallback and drawImage.
- Ingest: no ingest code ships in the app. scripts/clips/lab-server.mjs is a small reverse proxy on :3200. It serves POST /__lab/result and POST /__lab/clip itself and proxies everything else to `next start -p 3100`. The page posts same-origin, which fits the production CSP connect-src 'self'. The prototype is /tmp/hh-clips/probe/server.mjs, which already mirrors the production CSP and Permissions-Policy.

3. VALIDATORS (run on the Mac for every clip, from every tier)
apps/web/e2e/clips/lib/verify-mp4.ts, a wrapper over ffprobe/ffmpeg:
- ffprobe reports no errors;
- atoms are ftyp then moov before mdat (fast start). Long-record files may be fragmented (moof) and must be finalized or recoverable;
- video is avc1 (High, Main or Constrained Baseline) at level 4.0 or below, dimensions even, long side 1280 or less;
- audio is AAC-LC (objectType 2) at 48000 or 44100 Hz with 1-2 channels whenever the game has sound;
- the container has no metadata tags beyond encoder and handle title. No location, no real name. The filename matches hanks-hits-<game>-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>.mp4.
apps/web/e2e/clips/lib/frame-index.ts: runs ffmpeg -vf crop,scale=16:1:flags=neighbor -f rawvideo -pix_fmt gray and decodes the barcode per frame. From the decoded indices it computes:
- dropped frames (gaps) and duplicated frames (repeats);
- the effective fps;
- the first index, which must fall on a keyframe;
- the last index, which must be within 2 frames of the index the page logged at the "Clip it" tap. This proves the ring holds the LAST N seconds.
apps/web/e2e/clips/lib/av-sync.ts (a port of /tmp/hh-clips/probe/analyze_sync.py, calibrated at 0.0 ms on an ffmpeg reference): white-flash times against beep onsets, giving audio-minus-video in ms.
apps/web/tools/clips/avsync.swift and avcheck.swift (built with `swiftc -O`, which needs only the CLT; prototypes are in /tmp/hh-clips/avcheck/): measure the same sync through AVAssetReader, and check isPlayable, isExportable and track formats.
Pass thresholds:
- A/V offset within [-45, +45] ms at every beep, in BOTH decoder families (ITU-R BT.1359 detectability). Drift is 10 ms/min or less.
- Effective fps is at least 90% of target on desktop and at least 80% on phones. The largest frame gap is 100 ms or less outside documented pauses.
- Instant replay duration is between N-1.0 s (1 s GOP) and N+0.1 s. Auto-highlight windows include the brag timestamp with the configured pre/post-roll.
- The game's own fps drops by 15% or less with clips on (median over 20 s; the feasibility baseline was 15%).
- TTFC is 1000 ms or less at p95, in every row. This flags the Chrome 153 realtime stall.
- JS heap and process RSS grow 50 MB or less over a 10-minute always-on session.
- Tap-to-share-ready time for a 30 s clip is 2 s or less on the reference iPhone (a target to measure and tighten).

4. AUTOMATION INSTRUMENTATION (apps/web/e2e/clips/lib/instrument.ts via page.addInitScript)
- Wrap navigator.share to record: file count, type, name, size, whether title/text/url were also passed (must be files only), userActivation.isActive at call time, and ms since the last pointerup.
- Wrap getUserMedia and getDisplayMedia to throw and record the call. The test fails on any call (no mic, camera or screen, ever).
- Expose window.__clipsDiag: TTFC, queue depth, frames dropped by the bounded queue, audio underruns, and which path was chosen (webcodecs, mediarecorder or wasm-aac).
- Playwright projects that test backgrounding use `ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--disable-background-timer-throttling','--disable-renderer-backgrounding','--disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows','--disable-back-forward-cache']` so real throttling and codec reclamation happen. Hidden, frozen and resumed states are driven with CDP Page.setWebLifecycleState.
- Performance runs use CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate at 1x and 4x as a low-end proxy (a proxy only, never the verdict).

5. VERIFICATION MATRIX. Format: row, then tier and automation level, then scope and human steps.
M1 Chrome stable 153 on macOS. T1, AUTOMATED (channel 'chrome', headless-new plus one headed run). Everything: lab (replay 15/30/60, highlight, 10-min record, both orientations, forced WASM AAC, forced MediaRecorder), game contract (all games), share stub, download fallback, OPFS library, lifecycle, performance, hosted link, privacy.
M2 Chrome Beta on macOS. T1, AUTOMATED after install. Same suite. Early warning for regressions like the 153 stall.
M3 Bundled Chromium (CfT 151). T1, AUTOMATED. Smoke only. Recorded for contrast, never used as a proxy.
M4 Playwright WebKit 26.5 on macOS. T1, AUTOMATED after the 81 MB install. Functional suite with a share stub. Engine proxy for WebKit timestamp and description quirks.
M5 Desktop Safari (26.5, then 27 after update) via safaridriver. T1, AUTOMATED after a one-time `safaridriver --enable`. Lab, game contract (representative 6), OPFS, performance. The share sheet is not automated.
M6 Playwright Firefox 153. T1, AUTOMATED after the 106 MB install. Fallback paths: no AAC encoder so WASM AAC, no file share so the download path (page.waitForEvent('download'), then verify the file). Records whether H.264 VideoEncoder is available.
M7 Windows Chrome and Edge on JACKS-ML-DESKTOP (tailnet). T1-remote, SEMI (run the same Playwright suite there). Media Foundation H.264 and AAC, whose priming may differ. Human: Windows share UI once.
M8 Chrome device emulation (Pixel 7, iPhone 15 descriptors). T1, AUTOMATED. Clip UI layout at 375 px with 6 header controls, touch targets of 44 px or more, read-aloud contract. Codec results are not truth here.
M9 iOS Simulator Safari tab: iOS 26.5 now (Xcode 26.6); iOS 27 after the macOS 26.7 update (Xcode 27); an iOS 18.x runtime for the no-AudioEncoder path. T2, AUTOMATED (safaridriver `platformName:'iOS', 'safari:useSimulator':true`, plus `xcrun simctl openurl`). API surface, lab flows, OPFS, iPad size classes (iPad reports a desktop-class UA). Codec numbers are informational.
M10 iOS Simulator Home Screen web app. T2, SEMI (Add to Home Screen by hand once). Standalone storage separation, persist(), clip library survives relaunch.
M11 Android emulator (API 36 Play image, arm64). T2, AUTOMATED (adb reverse + forward, connectOverCDP). UI flows, share-sheet invocation (dismissed with `adb shell input keyevent BACK`), backgrounding via `input keyevent HOME`. Codec informational.
M12 Jack's iPhone 17, Safari tab (iOS 26 or 27). T3, SCRIPTED + HUMAN. `pymobiledevice3 webinspector launch <tunnel URL>/dev/clips-lab --native`, or a QR code opened by hand; the page posts results to the lab server. Run the lab plus 6 representative games: breakout (canvas2D), monster-truck (R3F, also the performance worst case), four-wheeler-adventure (srcdoc iframe), retro-arcade (EmulatorJS iframe), 2048 (DOM replay), oregon-trail (mixed). Human: Share, then Save Video, then open Photos and confirm it plays with sound and the handle overlay. Send it in Messages. Lock the screen mid-record, then unlock. Switch apps during a replay. Repeat with Low Power Mode on. Do a 10-minute always-on thermal run; the lab page logs fps, TTFC and drops.
M13 Same iPhone, Home Screen web app. T3, HUMAN + Web Inspector. The M12 flows, plus: My Clips persists across relaunch, storage is separate from the Safari tab, and the share sheet works in standalone mode.
M14 Same iPhone, Private Browsing tab. T3, HUMAN. AFP noise: the clip looks and sounds clean, nothing throws, the ephemeral-library notice appears.
M15 Same iPhone, Chrome for iOS (WKWebView). T3, HUMAN. Capture plus share.
M16 An older iOS device (iOS 18 or earlier, or an older iPad), if the household has one. T3, HUMAN. Fallback path (MediaRecorder or WASM AAC) and performance floor.
M17 A real Android phone with Chrome. T3, AUTOMATED + HUMAN (scripts/clips/android-device.mjs: adb reverse tcp:3200 tcp:3200; adb forward tcp:9333 localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote; connectOverCDP; the full T1 suite on-device with trusted CDP taps). Human: pick a share target (Photos/Gallery, Messages). Automated telemetry: `dumpsys battery`, `dumpsys thermalservice`, `dumpsys meminfo com.android.chrome`, `dumpsys gfxinfo`.
M18 Samsung Internet on a Samsung device (the SM-X230 if Jack frees it). T3, HUMAN + lab ingest. Capture, share, OPFS on an old Chromium base and a MediaTek SoC. The SM-X230's Chrome 140 is also the "stale Chrome" row.
M19 Android installed PWA. T3, HUMAN. Standalone share and storage.
M20 A school Chromebook. T3, HUMAN (lab over a cloudflared quick tunnel; ingest). Native AAC present or not (decides the WASM path), VA-API H.264 TTFC and throughput, performance on a low-end CPU.
M21 Recipient views of the hosted link /c/<slug>. T1 AUTOMATED + T3 HUMAN. Automated: curl with Twitterbot/facebookexternalhit/Slackbot user agents returns og:video, og:video:type=video/mp4, width and height, and og:image; the video URL returns 206 for `Range: bytes=0-1` with Content-Type video/mp4 and Accept-Ranges bytes (iOS AVFoundation needs byte ranges); expiry returns 410; report and takedown remove the object. Human: iMessage preview, WhatsApp preview, and playback in iOS Safari and Android Chrome.
M22 Production live smoke after every deploy that touches clips. T3, HUMAN. M12 and M17 flows against https://hankshits.com, following the rule that verification happens on the live surface.

6. HARNESS FILES (under apps/web/) AND COMMANDS
- e2e/clips/playwright.config.ts. Projects: chrome (channel 'chrome'), chrome-beta, chromium, webkit, firefox, mobile-ui (devices['Pixel 7'] and devices['iPhone 15'] on chrome), plus lifecycle variants with ignoreDefaultArgs. webServer: `node scripts/clips/lab-server.mjs --build` (runs next build with NEXT_PUBLIC_CLIPS_LAB=1, next start on :3100, proxy on :3200). globalSetup checks that ffmpeg, ffprobe and swiftc exist and compiles tools/clips/*.swift. It fails loudly if any is missing, and never skips silently.
- e2e/clips/lib/{verify-mp4,frame-index,av-sync,instrument,pull-clip}.ts. pull-clip moves the Blob to Node in 1 MB base64 chunks through page.evaluate.
- e2e/clips/lab-pattern.spec.ts: replay 15/30/60 after 75 s of play; highlight at scripted brag times; 10-minute record (reload mid-record, then recover); portrait and landscape; forced WASM AAC; forced MediaRecorder; ablock=4800 regression.
- e2e/clips/game-contract.spec.ts. It auto-discovers every game from the metadata.ts registry (the same scan the home page uses), so kid-built games are covered on arrival. Per game: open the route, dismiss GameStartOverlay, drive generic input (arrows, space, center taps) for 8 s, press the shell "Clip it" control, pull the clip, and verify: valid MP4, frames non-black with temporal variance, overlay handle region present, audio RMS above -50 dBFS unless the game metadata says silent, and fps impact within budget. DOM-replay games are verified the same way.
- e2e/clips/share-and-save.spec.ts: share stub shape and activation checks, canShare false leads to download, the hosted-link fallback.
- e2e/clips/storage.spec.ts: OPFS library across reload and browser restart (launchPersistentContext), quota-exceeded handling (fill OPFS to force it), persist() request.
- e2e/clips/lifecycle.spec.ts: hidden, frozen and resumed during replay and record; AudioContext interruption; encoder error recovery (close the encoder from the test hook).
- e2e/clips/perf.spec.ts: fps with clips off vs on at 1x and 4x CPU; TTFC first vs second encoder; memory over 10 minutes (CDP SystemInfo.getProcessInfo and Performance.getMetrics).
- e2e/clips/hosted-link.spec.ts: presign, PUT, finalize, serve against local MinIO (Docker.app is installed) plus a single real-bucket smoke with a 1-day lifecycle test prefix.
- e2e/clips/privacy.spec.ts: container tags, filenames, card text, and no getUserMedia/getDisplayMedia calls. Also that the production headers still carry Permissions-Policy camera=(), microphone=().
- tools/clips/avcheck.swift and avsync.swift (AVFoundation, CLT-buildable).
- scripts/clips/lab-server.mjs: ingest proxy, validators, a PASS/FAIL table printed per device, results written to test-results/clips-matrix/<date>/<device>.json, and a QR code of the tunnel URL in the terminal.
- scripts/clips/tunnel.mjs --via tailscale|cloudflared|none. It prints the command it would run (for example `tailscale serve --bg 3200` or `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3200`) and runs it only with --yes, because it changes tailnet serve config. On --stop it runs `tailscale serve reset` or kills cloudflared.
- scripts/clips/android-device.mjs --serial <id> [--no-kiosk-check]. It refuses to run if the device foreground is a kiosk app (de.ozerov.fully) unless --no-kiosk-check is given.
- scripts/clips/ios-device.mjs: pymobiledevice3 webinspector launch/js-shell --native; reads window.__probe; lists results.
- scripts/clips/ios-sim.mjs --runtime iOS-26-5: simctl create/boot, safaridriver session with useSimulator, run the lab URL on http://localhost:3200 (the simulator's localhost is the Mac).
- scripts/clips/safari-desktop.mjs: safaridriver on port 4444 with W3C WebDriver JSON over fetch, executeAsyncScript to wait for window.__probe.
- scripts/clips/matrix.mjs: runs every available tier and prints the PASS/FAIL table. It writes test-results/clips-matrix/<date>/report.html. Human rows are "PENDING" until someone taps "I checked it" in the lab page's checklist panel, which posts an evidence row with the device, timestamp, clip SHA-256 and a free-text note. It refuses a release-ready verdict while any required human row is pending.
- package.json scripts: "clips:e2e" (playwright test -c e2e/clips/playwright.config.ts), "clips:e2e:gate" (project chrome, lab-pattern plus game-contract limited to the 6 representative games and games changed in the diff, target under 4 minutes), "clips:lab", "clips:android", "clips:ios-sim", "clips:ios-device", "clips:safari", "clips:verify <file>", "clips:matrix".
- Add test-results/ and playwright-report/ to .gitignore.

7. WHEN EACH TIER RUNS
- Every push: .githooks/pre-push adds `pnpm --filter web clips:e2e:gate` after build, using `cmd > log 2>&1; rc=$?`, never piped.
- Every PR touching src/shared/clips, GameShell or any game's clip registration: `pnpm --filter web clips:matrix` covering T1 (all projects) and T2 (when installed).
- Before the first release to kids and before each clips-feature release: required T3 rows M12, M13, M17 and M20 with evidence, plus M14 and M19. M16 and M18 when a device is available.
- After deploy: M22 on hankshits.com.
- Weekly or on browser updates: M2 and M5 re-run (Chrome Beta, Safari updates). The probe records browser versions so drift is attributable.
- make-a-game, remix-a-game and change-a-game skills: add "run clips:e2e:gate for my game" to their verification steps. mobile-playability: add "Clip it works by tap".

8. INSTALLS NEEDED (none performed; all free; sizes measured)
- repo devDependency @playwright/test@1.62.0, then `cd apps/web && pnpm exec playwright install webkit firefox` (81.2 MB + 106.5 MB zips). Chrome Beta is optional (a system install).
- `safaridriver --enable` (admin password, once). Enables M5 and real-iPhone WebDriver.
- iOS Simulator, option A today: Xcode 26.6 (needs macOS 26.2 or later; xip about 2 GB, about 3.6 GiB installed) plus the iOS 26.5 runtime (about 7-8 GB) via `xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS`. Option B: install macOS Tahoe 26.7 first (3.85 GB, restart), then Xcode 27.0 plus the iOS 27 runtime (about 7.85 GB). Optional iOS 18.x runtime for the fallback path.
- Android emulator: JDK 21 (`brew install --cask temurin@21`), cmdline-tools 155 MB, emulator 37.3.1 aarch64 420 MB, system-images;android-36;google_apis_playstore;arm64-v8a 1.89 GB zip. About 2.6 GB download. platform-tools is already installed.
- pymobiledevice3 11.19.4 via pipx (1.3 MB wheel plus dependencies).
- cloudflared 2026.9.3 via brew (19.8 MB), only for devices off the tailnet (Chromebook, friends' phones).
- On-device toggles: iPhone Settings > Apps > Safari > Advanced > Web Inspector and Remote Automation. Android Developer options > USB debugging. chrome://flags "Enable command line on non-rooted devices" only if using Playwright _android.

9. REGRESSION LOCKS FROM TODAY'S PROBES (each must be a named test)
(a) Dual-decoder A/V sync. AudioToolbox AAC without signalling reads +44 ms in ffmpeg and 0 ms in AVFoundation. With elst only it reads 0 and -44.
