The ffmpeg-style elst plus sgpd/sbgp roll group reads 0 in both. Test: lab clip within +/-45 ms in ffmpeg AND AVFoundation for the native and WASM AAC paths, on every row.
(b) WebKit non-1024 AudioData chunking. Test with ?ablock=4800: packet deltas all exactly 1024, and drift of 10 ms/min or less.
(c) WebKit 302253 ESDS description. Test: the muxed ASC is 2 bytes with objectType 2.
(d) Chrome realtime TTFC stall. Test: TTFC of 1000 ms or less and a bounded encode queue (frames dropped and counted, never queued without limit).
(e) isConfigSupported throws on iOS. Test: the capability check survives injected throws.
(f) WebKit black video readback. The lab's playback check must present the frame first.
(g) Headless shell is banned from the gate. Config test: the gate project uses channel 'chrome'.
risksAndMitigations: Human-tap rows (Share sheet, Save Video, Messages, lock screen, thermal) get skipped. Mitigation: matrix.mjs cannot report release-ready while required human rows are PENDING. Evidence rows carry the device, timestamp and SHA-256 of the pulled clip.

The lab's test pattern drifts from what real games do. Mitigation: game-contract.spec.ts auto-discovers every registered game, including future kid-built ones, and runs the same validators on each. The lab covers only timing and sync, where a fixture is required.

Browser updates silently change encoder behavior (the Chrome 153 realtime stall is the proof). Mitigation: Chrome Beta and Safari rows re-run weekly. The probe records browser versions and TTFC, and the gate fails on TTFC above 1 s.

A/V sync regresses on one decoder family while the other looks fine. Mitigation: every clip is checked by ffmpeg AND AVFoundation. Priming is measured per platform from the probe instead of hard-coded.

Simulator or emulator results get mistaken for device truth. Mitigation: the T2 rows mark codec, performance and thermal fields as informational in the report schema. Only T3 or T1-branded rows can satisfy a codec or performance requirement.

Automation flags hide background throttling and activation rules. Mitigation: lifecycle and share specs use ignoreDefaultArgs and never rely on automation-granted activation. The real activation window is proven only in T3.

Tunnels expose the dev lab publicly. Mitigation: the lab exists only in builds with NEXT_PUBLIC_CLIPS_LAB=1 (never set on Railway). Prefer tailscale serve (tailnet-only). cloudflared quick tunnels are per session and torn down by `tunnel.mjs --stop`. Ingest lives in lab-server, never in the app.

Changing tailnet serve config or macOS/Xcode updates disrupt Jack's machine (a restart for macOS 26.7). Mitigation: tunnel.mjs prints the command and needs --yes. OS and Xcode installs are scheduled with Jack. Xcode 26.6 avoids the OS update entirely.
The attached SM-X230 is a house kiosk dashboard. Mitigation: android-device.mjs refuses to drive a device whose foreground is de.ozerov.fully unless explicitly overridden with Jack's permission.

Few real devices (unknown kid device mix, no old iOS or Chromebook in hand). Mitigation: field health counters (T4) measure the long tail in production. Optional free BrowserStack OSS access for old iOS versions if Jack approves a free outside account.

Hosted-link tests could leave objects in the real bucket and cost money. Mitigation: local MinIO for the suite. The single real-bucket smoke uses a test prefix with a 1-day lifecycle rule and deletes its objects in teardown.

Encoder timing is noisy and makes tests flaky. Mitigation: thresholds are set on medians and p95 over repeated runs with warm and cold variants reported separately. No silent retries: a retry is logged in the results row.
openQuestions: Which devices do Hank and his friends actually use: iPhone/iPad models and iOS versions, Android phones, school Chromebook models? This decides M16, M17, M18 and M20 and whether an old-iOS row needs BrowserStack's free open-source program.
May the SM-X230 kiosk tablet (Android 16, Chrome 140, Samsung Internet 29) be taken off dashboard duty for scheduled test windows? It covers the stale-Chrome and Samsung Internet rows.

Approve the one-time installs and toggles: `safaridriver --enable` (admin password), Playwright webkit and firefox (188 MB), pymobiledevice3, cloudflared, the Android emulator stack (about 2.6 GB plus a JDK), and Xcode 26.6 now or the macOS 26.7 update followed by Xcode 27.
Are privacy-safe field health counters (no identifiers, UA-family bucket only) acceptable for a kids' site? This is the only way to prove behavior across the device long tail.
Chrome 153 realtime-latency stall: file a Chromium bug with /tmp/hh-clips/probe/ttfc2.mjs as the repro? Does it reproduce on Windows and ChromeOS Chrome 153?

Do iOS devices show the same WebKit quirks as desktop Safari 26.5 (ESDS AAC description, irregular AAC timestamps with non-1024 input), and what AAC priming does iOS AudioEncoder use? The first M12 run answers this.
Do ChromeOS Chrome and Android Chrome expose a native AAC AudioEncoder, or is WASM AAC (972 KB, 1024-sample priming) the common path there?

Does the iOS Simulator's Safari expose VideoEncoder/AudioEncoder/MediaRecorder with working H.264 encode, and does Android emulator Chrome accept avc1 in VideoEncoder on the goldfish software codec? Verify on first install; the plan treats both as informational either way.

Architecture decision (owned by another track, but the tests must follow it): write AAC priming as elst plus sgpd/sbgp roll group (the only form that measured 0 ms in both ffmpeg and AVFoundation), either upstream in mediabunny (#444) or as a post-finalize moov patch.

For iOS Home Screen web apps: is OPFS storage fully separate from the Safari tab on iOS 26/27, and is persist() granted there? The M10 and M13 rows verify this. The WebKit storage-policy post implies heuristic grants for Home Screen apps.
rejectedAlternatives: Paid device clouds (BrowserStack/Sauce/LambdaTest paid tiers): excluded by the constraint. BrowserStack's free open-source program exists and the repo is public, but it adds an outside account and still cannot do Photos or Messages human verification. It is kept as an open question, not the default.

Treating Playwright WebKit or Chrome mobile emulation as iOS/Android proof: both run the Mac's codec stack (VideoToolbox/AudioToolbox) with desktop policies, and emulation changes only the viewport and UA.

Gating on the Playwright headless shell or bundled Chromium: the headless shell has no navigator.share and uses SwiftShader and a software encoder. Bundled CfT Chromium 151 did not show the Chrome 153 realtime stall that branded Chrome shows.

Validating clips only in the browser that made them: in-browser playback and duration checks miss decoder-family sync differences (44 ms) and malformed AAC configs (mediabunny #173). Validation happens on the Mac with ffmpeg plus AVFoundation.
Serving `next dev` to phones: Next.js blocks cross-origin dev assets (allowedDevOrigins), and dev-mode performance numbers mean nothing. A production build behind the lab proxy is used instead.
Plain http:// on the LAN IP: not a secure context, so WebCodecs, OPFS and Web Share are unavailable. It would test a different product.

mkcert or self-signed HTTPS on phones: every phone, including kids' devices, would need a trusted root CA installed. Tailscale serve (real certificates) and cloudflared quick tunnels need nothing on the phone.

A Railway PR environment for every device session: each one spins up a service and database copy and costs money per PR. Local tunnels cover device testing for free. A PR environment is reserved, if ever, for a remote tester who cannot reach a tunnel.

Pixel-exact screenshot comparison of clips: Safari's fingerprinting protection noise and encoder differences make it flaky by design. The barcode frame index plus luma and RMS thresholds are exact where it matters.

Automating the iOS share sheet or Photos app from WebDriver: WebDriver cannot reach native share UI, and tapping through it with system automation needs Xcode UI testing of Apple apps, which is brittle and unsupported. A human does this step, with the evidence recorded.
Driving the attached Samsung tablet now: it is a Fully Kiosk house dashboard, so read-only getprop/dumpsys commands were the limit without Jack's permission.

verdicts.claim: Chrome 153 first-encoder stall with latencyMode 'realtime' (TTFC 8.7-38 s; frames queue without limit, encodeQueueSize reached 150)
verdicts.correction: The stall is real, and it is worse than the track reported. The evidence offered for the queue was an artifact: ttfc.mjs and ttfc2.mjs submit 30 or 150 frames in one synchronous loop, so encodeQueueSize must equal the submitted count before any output callback can run. I re-ran it with rAF-paced 30 fps input, the way real capture feeds frames. The first realtime encoder emitted NOTHING for 11.4-16.7 s. In a 30 s run the first output arrived at 14.3 s, and the queue peaked at 357 frames, which is hundreds of MB of 720p frames. With a 4-frame bounded queue, 315 of 337 frames were dropped, so the replay is blind for that whole window. It reproduces in a Chrome 153 launched normally with no Playwright switches and a fresh profile (11,451 ms). Chromium's realtime path sets kVTVideoEncoderSpecification_EnableLowLatencyRateControl, which selects Apple's 'rtvc' encoder (vt_video_encode_accelerator_mac.mm:143-151, 476-479). Mitigation measured: latencyMode 'quality' gave TTFC 26 ms in raw Chrome and 372 ms under Playwright, maxQ 1-9, no frame reordering, and keyFrame requests honored. prefer-software realtime gave 78 ms. CfT 151 realtime gave 839 ms. The design should default to 'quality' on Chromium or add a TTFC watchdog that reconfigures, and the gate should test that watchdog.

verdicts.claim: AAC priming breaks A/V sync differently per decoder family; only elst + sgpd/sbgp roll group reads 0 ms in both
verdicts.correction: Independent community evidence agrees (mediabunny #444, comment of 2026-09-18). Edit list alone over-trims in Audition (an Apple/Adobe-style implicit delay applied on top). Edit list + roll_distance -1 is correct in Audition, Audacity and ffmpeg. The track MISSED a second defect in the same thread: Safari's AudioEncoder consumes the first 1024 frames of REAL audio as priming (kAudioConverterPrimeMethod left at default). The fix is to pre-pad 1024 silent frames and set the elst media_time to 2112+1024=3136. Also, mediabunny PR #485 (negative timestamps, so the edit list is written automatically) merged 2026-09-08. Roll-group writing is still not in mediabunny, so a moov patch is required.

verdicts.claim: WebKit bug 302253 (AAC AudioEncoder ESDS description) still present
verdicts.correction: bugs.webkit.org REST reports status NEW, last changed 2025-11-17.

verdicts.claim: Chrome AAC encoder is OS-backed; ChromeOS/Linux unverified (open question: is WASM AAC the common Chromebook path?)
verdicts.correction: Chromium source answers the open question. kPlatformAudioEncoder is FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT only on Windows, Mac and Android. MojoAudioEncoder::IsSupported(kAAC) falls to the disabled default on ChromeOS and Linux, and Windows N SKUs are excluded. Android uses NdkAudioEncoder (MediaCodec), so its priming is a third, unmeasured value. The conclusion: WASM AAC (972 KB, 1024-sample priming) IS the school-Chromebook path. It must be a first-class, performance-gated row, not a fallback curiosity.

verdicts.claim: WASM AAC fallback runs on browsers without an AAC AudioEncoder (Firefox, iOS before 26); verified via ?forceWasmAac=1 on Chrome
verdicts.correction: It works under the production CSP. However, MDN BCD 8.1.3 lists AudioData itself as Safari/iOS 26+, not only AudioEncoder. Forcing the WASM path on Chrome or Safari 26 leaves the AudioData, AudioEncoder and AudioDecoder globals defined, so it does not reproduce the iOS 16.4-18 API surface. mediabunny guards some uses (sample.js:88, 2371) but also calls `new AudioData` (sample.js:2168-2201). The lab knob must delete these globals in both window and worker scopes. An iOS 18 simulator row is still required.

verdicts.claim: Desktop Safari 26.5 capability surface: MediaStreamTrackProcessor missing
verdicts.correction: probe.js:41 tests typeof only on the main thread. BCD lists MediaStreamTrackProcessor (and .readable) as Safari/iOS 18+, and per spec it is exposed in dedicated workers. The 'missing' reading is a main-thread-only probe artifact. The production probe must test the worker scope too.

verdicts.claim: Automation masks real-user policies (Playwright disables background throttling etc.)
verdicts.correction: It is broader than the track stated. The same chromiumSwitches list also has --disable-field-trial-config, so branded Chrome under Playwright runs with NO Finch experiments, unlike every real user. It also has --disable-ipc-flooding-protection and --disable-hang-monitor, and headless adds --mute-audio. So 'channel chrome' is still not 'the browser kids run'. Add one CDP-attach run against a normally launched Chrome (the pattern is in /tmp/hh-clips/rev-dti/rawchrome.mjs). Measurements also differ: quality-mode TTFC was 372 ms under Playwright vs 26 ms raw.

verdicts.claim: Headless shell is not a valid stand-in; gate must use channel 'chrome'
verdicts.correction: Agreed. Note that headless channel 'chrome' also gets --mute-audio. The audio-tap assertions must therefore be validated against a headed run or the raw-Chrome run, so a fake or muted output device cannot mask audio-clock behavior.

verdicts.claim: Mac inventory: CLT only, no Xcode/simctl, safaridriver 26.5, macOS 26.5.1; Playwright caches chromium-1234/headless-1234, no webkit/firefox
verdicts.correction: Re-checked locally. One addendum: @playwright/test 1.63.0 shipped 2026-09-04, so the spec's pin of 1.62.0 (2026-07-24) is a release behind.
sources: local: xcode-select -p; xcrun simctl; safaridriver --version; sw_vers; ls ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright

verdicts.claim: Xcode 27.0 needs macOS 26.6; Xcode 26.6 needs macOS 26.2 and ships iOS 26.5 SDK
Real iPhone automation without Xcode via pymobiledevice3 11.19.4 --native
verdicts.correction: PyPI shows 11.19.4 uploaded 2026-09-27 11:29 (today). The docs state that --native piggybacks on remoted with no root, entitlement or Xcode. The cdp bridge targets WebViews and JSContexts. Keep js-shell as the primary path and treat Playwright-over-that-CDP as unproven.

verdicts.claim: HTTPS to phones via tailscale serve / cloudflared
verdicts.correction: `tailscale serve status` currently reports 'No serve config', so `serve --bg 3200` will not clobber anything. For devices off the tailnet, Tailscale Funnel needs no new install, unlike cloudflared. Either domain may be blocked by school web filters, so run the Chromebook row on the home network.
sources: local: tailscale serve status; tailscale funnel status

verdicts.claim: iOS modes: Advanced Fingerprinting Protection noise is Private-Browsing default, optional for all browsing
verdicts.correction: Safari 26's 'all browsing by default' protections apply only to KNOWN fingerprinting scripts (an Apple engineer, quoted by lapcat). Noise on first-party canvas and audio readback still needs Private Browsing or the opt-in setting, so M14 is correctly a separate row.

verdicts.claim: Desktop canShare cannot predict iOS/Android share acceptance
verdicts.correction: This is stronger than stated. Chromium's browser process rejects shares that canShare would accept: when the tab is not foreground and visible (PERMISSION_DENIED), when there are more than 10 files, and on Android when the total exceeds MAX_SHARED_FILE_BYTES = 50 MiB. None of these show in canShare.

verdicts.claim: designSpec: hosted-link tests against local MinIO plus a real-bucket smoke with a 1-day lifecycle test prefix
verdicts.correction: Two problems. First, MinIO community stopped publishing binaries and images in October 2025, and the repo was archived on 2026-04-25. Second, Railway Buckets list 'Bucket lifecycle configuration' as NOT supported, and the endpoint is Tigris-style t3.storageapi.dev. A lifecycle-based expiry or test prefix is impossible. Expiry must be an app-side reaper, and the test must exercise that reaper plus explicit teardown deletes. Use a maintained emulator (Garage, SeaweedFS, RustFS, versitygw) or a dedicated Railway test bucket (storage $0.015/GB-month, API ops and egress free).

verdicts.claim: designSpec: A/V pass threshold [-45,+45] ms at every beep (ITU-R BT.1359) locks the priming regressions
verdicts.correction: BT.1359's +45/-125 ms is the END-TO-END detectability limit for the whole chain (+ = sound advanced). The spec's own regression lock (a) cites elst-only reading -44 ms in AVFoundation and WASM reading +21/-22 ms. Both PASS a ±45 ms threshold, so the lock cannot fail on the bug it names. The container/decoder stage needs about |offset| <= 5 ms on synthetic-timestamp files, and the ±45 budget should be reserved for the whole live chain including recipient transcodes.

verdicts.claim: designSpec: the lab posts same-origin, which fits production CSP connect-src 'self'
verdicts.correction: Production connect-src is actually "'self' https:" (next.config.ts:33-35), so ingest works either way. The CSP line that matters and was missed is media-src 'self' blob:. It blocks in-page playback of presigned bucket URLs on /c/<slug>.

designSpecProblems: A/V threshold is toothless. ±45 ms passes the exact -44 ms (elst-only, AVFoundation) and ±22 ms (WASM priming) defects that regression lock 9(a) exists to catch. Split it into (1) a container/decoder test on synthetic-timestamp files with |offset| <= 5 ms in BOTH ffmpeg and AVFoundation, and (2) an end-to-end live budget using the asymmetric ITU +45/-125 ms limit.

The live-lab sync fixture confounds sources of error. It draws the white frame 'on the first frame of every whole second' (rAF-quantized: up to 16.7-33 ms late, more under jank) and schedules the beep on the AudioContext clock (a separate clock, mapped through getOutputTimestamp). The measured offset therefore mixes pipeline clock-mapping error with frame quantization. Log each flash frame's VideoFrame.timestamp and each beep's scheduled time converted to the pipeline timeline, then judge the measured offset against that logged ground truth.
The drift limit of '10 ms/min' allows 100 ms of drift by the end of a 10-minute record, which is past ITU detectability. Make it an absolute bound at every beep across the whole clip.

The TTFC gate is necessary but the spec gives no remedy. On Chrome 153/mac the first realtime encoder emits nothing for 11-17 s even with paced 30 fps input. A bounded queue then drops about 94% of frames, so the replay is blind. Default latencyMode to 'quality' on Chromium (measured 26-372 ms, no B-frames, keyframes honored), or ship a TTFC watchdog that reconfigures. Add a named test that the watchdog fires, and run TTFC against a normally launched Chrome (CDP attach), not only Playwright.

The pre-push integration breaks the kid workflow. Adding clips:e2e:gate to .githooks/pre-push, with a globalSetup that 'fails loudly' when swiftc, ffmpeg or branded Chrome is missing, blocks EVERY push from a kid's Windows, Linux or Chromebook clone (CLAUDE.md: kids clone this onto fresh computers; guardrail 9 says never make the kid debug). It also contradicts the hook's own 'tool missing -> skip' stance (.githooks/pre-push:21-25). Instead, run the AVFoundation checker on darwin only with a visible 'SKIPPED (not macOS)' row, and use ffmpeg-static or a vendored ffprobe.

The pre-push gate puts perf thresholds (TTFC, fps impact) on a busy dev machine. lessons.md:15 records that gates must run on a quiet machine, because a concurrent Playwright sweep caused false timeouts. Keep pre-push functional-only and move the perf thresholds to the quiet clips:matrix run.

NEXT_PUBLIC_CLIPS_LAB is inlined at build time. This forces a SECOND `next build` in the gate (more minutes, and it overwrites the first build's .next output), and every device row tests a different bundle than the one Railway ships. Gate the lab on a runtime server env read in a dynamic server component (notFound unless CLIPS_LAB=1 at `next start`), reuse the single build, and add a privacy test that production returns 404 for /dev/clips-lab.

'Local MinIO' is a dead dependency: repo archived 2026-04-25, no community images since October 2025. The '1-day lifecycle test prefix' cannot exist on Railway Buckets, which do not support lifecycle configuration. Clip expiry must be an app-side reaper, and the suite must test the reaper, not bucket lifecycle.

M21 checks unfurls with curl but never plays the clip in-page under the real CSP. The media-src 'self' blob: directive blocks a presigned bucket URL (private Tigris-backed t3.storageapi.dev) on /c/<slug>. Test real playback in iOS Safari and Android Chrome through the production headers.

M21 runs against the origin, not the Cloudflare edge. Cloudflare caches .mp4 by extension by default (200/206 for 120 min, 302 for 20 min). A takedown or expiry can keep serving from the edge, and a cached 302 can outlive a short-lived presigned URL and break playback. Test through hankshits.com: assert cf-cache-status, 410 after expiry, and 404 after takedown within a stated SLA. Also assert that zero video bytes transit the Railway service (a 302 to the bucket, where egress is free), because that is the server-cost promise.

There is no test at the share-size ceiling. Chrome (desktop and Android) caps shared files at 50 MiB (MAX_SHARED_FILE_BYTES), while a 10-minute Record clip at about 3 Mbps is about 225 MB. Add per-platform 'largest clip a kid can make' share tests, plus the trim, split or download path the UI offers when a clip is over the cap.

The Safari AudioEncoder eats the first 1024 real samples (mediabunny #444). Offset-only checks miss this. Add a 't=0 beep present at full 60 ms' lock and a pre-pad-1024 requirement for every encoder start, including restarts after reclamation.
The forced-WASM lab mode does not simulate iOS < 26, because AudioData is also 26+ per BCD. The knob must delete AudioEncoder, AudioDecoder and AudioData in the window and worker scopes.

The game contract's generic input ('arrows, space, center taps for 8 s') cannot produce gameplay in chess, checkers, quoridor, wordle, memory-match, oregon-trail or math-attack. The 'temporal variance' and 'audio RMS > -50 dBFS' assertions will then false-fail or get watered down. Each island needs its own clip driver (for example src/games/<id>/__clips__/drive.ts) that make-a-game, remix-a-game and change-a-game scaffold. The 9 apps (drawing-app, drum-machine, virtual-pet...) are not covered at all. Require an explicit literal opt-out in metadata instead of a silent skip.

The retro-arcade contract run depends on cdn.emulatorjs.org (allowed by the /emulator CSP) and on ROMs from the storage sidecar, so it is network-flaky. Use a vendored homebrew or public-domain ROM fixture.

Memory is gated only on desktop CDP RSS. On iPhone the clip-loss failure is a WebContent jetsam kill, which loses the game AND the ring. M12 and M13 need an iOS memory measurement (Web Inspector Timelines, or pymobiledevice3 syslog/crash reports for jetsam events) on the oldest supported iPhone running monster-truck with a 60 s ring.

The tunnel and lab builds never say which DATABASE_URL and AUTH env `next start` uses. Force a local Docker Postgres with seeded test users, and fail if the host is not local, so device sessions can never write to production.

OPFS 'My Clips' in a Safari tab is subject to WebKit's 7-days-of-browser-use proactive eviction unless persisted, and persist() is granted heuristically (mainly Home Screen apps). Test persisted() per surface, and test that the UI tells kids 'Save Video' is the durable copy. Without this, clips silently vanish.

No test covers an encoder reset inside the ring window: Chrome reclaiming a backgrounded codec under pressure, a GPU-process crash, or WebGL context loss. A clip that spans two encoder sessions (possibly different avcC/SPS) must still mux, or must be cut cleanly at the reset.

The device rows use Jack's adult iPhone. They miss the actual users' configurations: a Child Apple Account with Screen Time content restrictions, a Family Link supervised Android, and a managed school Chromebook (download restrictions, filtered networks).

Missing surfaces: Android WebView and in-app browsers, where BCD lists navigator.share as unsupported on webview_android. This is where kids land from WhatsApp, Discord, Instagram, Snapchat and Google app links. Firefox Android is also missing (no VideoEncoder or AudioEncoder per BCD).

Missing iPhone human steps: ringer silent switch, an AirPods route change mid-replay, a call, Siri or alarm interruption (AudioContext 'interrupted'), device rotation mid-replay, share cancel (AbortError) and double-tap share (InvalidStateError), iPad share popover anchoring, and a real iPad row (desktop-class UA breaks UA sniffing).

Hosted-link testing covers only the happy path, expiry and takedown, even though sharing is open to everyone. A presigned-upload endpoint is otherwise anonymous video hosting on a kids' domain. Required abuse tests: signed Content-Length and Content-Type on the PUT; server-side validation of the uploaded object (box parse, duration and size caps); per-account and per-IP rate limits; slug enumeration resistance; report-to-takedown latency through Cloudflare; and the CSAM/NCMEC handling path.

The T4 /api/clips/health counter endpoint is unauthenticated. If it writes to Postgres per beacon, it becomes a spam and DB-write-amplification vector against the 'low server cost' constraint. Aggregate counts in memory, flush periodically, and rate-limit.
The spec pins @playwright/test 1.62.0. 1.63.0 shipped 2026-09-04; pin the current release.
missedIssues: There is no per-OS priming table source for Android. Chrome Android AAC goes through NdkAudioEncoder (MediaCodec), whose encoder delay is neither the 2112 (AudioToolbox) nor the 1024 (WASM) the spec tabulates. M17 must measure it and derive the elst/roll values from the encoder in use, never from the UA.

Recipients recompress shared files: WhatsApp transcodes, iMessage may transcode, and Android Gallery handles VFR poorly. Variable-frame-rate game capture needs a receive-side check in M12 and M17 (sync and playback after the recipient app recompresses), not only a check of the sender's file.

Playwright headless adds --mute-audio, and automation uses fake or muted outputs. Audio-tap timing and audio-clock drift therefore need at least one headed or raw-Chrome run, or the audio ring may be validated against a clock no real device has.

The M8 layout check is at 375 px only. The header already holds up to 6 controls at 375 px, and a Clip control makes 7. Test at 320 px as well (iPhone SE 1st gen, small Androids); a 320 px screenshot already exists at /tmp/hh-clips/header-320-snake-playing.png.
The lab's 16-cell barcode frame index wraps at 65,536 frames (about 18 minutes at 60 fps). Record mode needs a maximum duration that is both enforced and tested, or a wider code.

Kids are not in scope for Web Inspector or Remote Automation toggles, and cannot 'tap I checked it' reliably. The human-row evidence protocol should state that Jack or a grown-up executes the rows, and the kid-facing skills must not attempt device automation.

Tunnel exposure: Tailscale Funnel or a cloudflared quick tunnel makes the lab build (with test pattern and handle) reachable publicly for the session. lab-server should require a per-session random token path in addition to the build flag.
verify.summary:
The device-test-infra inventory and most load-bearing platform claims hold up: the local toolchain, Xcode requirements, pymobiledevice3 --native, the WebKit 302253 status, and the AAC priming behavior across decoder families (independently backed by the latest mediabunny #444 comments). The Chrome 153 realtime-encoder stall is real and worse than reported. The track's evidence for the queue was an artifact of burst submission, but my rAF-paced re-run shows the first realtime encoder emits nothing for 11-17 s, reproduced in a normally launched Chrome. latencyMode 'quality' starts in 26-372 ms with no B-frames, so the design needs a default change or a watchdog, not just a gate. Chromium source resolves an open question: native AAC AudioEncoder is off by default on ChromeOS and Linux, so WASM AAC is the school-Chromebook path. The track missed that Safari's AudioEncoder drops the first 1024 real samples and that AudioData is also iOS 26+.

The designSpec has real holes:
- Its ±45 ms A/V threshold passes the very -44 ms and ±22 ms bugs its regression lock names.
- The live sync fixture confounds rAF quantization with clock mapping.
- Wiring a macOS-only, fail-loud, perf-threshold gate into pre-push would block every kid's non-Mac clone and flake on busy machines.
- The build-time lab flag forces a second build and tests a different bundle than production.
- MinIO is archived, and Railway Buckets cannot do lifecycle rules.
- M21 ignores CSP media-src and Cloudflare edge caching of .mp4.
- Nothing tests the 50 MiB Chrome share cap, iOS jetsam, 7-day OPFS eviction, encoder resets mid-ring, child-account or school-managed devices, in-app WebViews, or hosted-link abuse, even though sharing is open to everyone.

Scratch evidence is in /tmp/hh-clips/rev-dti/ (paced.log, paced2.log, rawchrome.log, reorder.log, vtvea.mm, blink_audio_encoder.cc, media_switches.cc, minio.md).

findings.claim: Railway buckets cost $0.015 per GB-month. The usage is the average of daily usage across all bucket instances in the workspace, rounded UP to the next whole GB-month. All S3 API operations are free and unlimited. Bucket egress is free, both through presigned URLs and through the S3 API. Service egress costs $0.05/GB. This covers a Railway service sending bytes to users, and a service uploading to a bucket over the public network, because buckets are not on the private network. RAM costs $10/GB-month and CPU costs $20/vCPU-month.

Hobby workspaces have a combined 1 TB bucket cap, and uploads beyond it fail. Pro is unlimited. Jack (PERSONAL) looks like it is on Pro: `railway usage limit status` on 2026-09-27 showed the Agent hard limit at $20.00, which is the Pro default ($5 on Hobby). The same output showed $16.68 compute usage 8 days into the period, with NO soft or hard compute limit set. If the Hard Usage Limit is exceeded, Railway suspends bucket reads and uploads and takes workloads offline. So a Railway hard limit is a site-killer, not a clips cost control.

Railway buckets are private only. They support presigned URLs (per Railway docs, valid up to 90 days), multipart, tagging and copy. They do NOT support lifecycle configuration, versioning, object lock or SSE configuration. Railway's own docs show browser uploads using createPresignedPost with ['content-length-range', min, max] and ['starts-with','$Content-Type', ...] conditions, plus aws s3api put-bucket-cors on https://t3.storageapi.dev. New buckets use virtual-hosted URLs (<bucket>.t3.storageapi.dev), so the CSP host is bucket-specific. Every environment gets its own bucket instance with its own credentials.

Railway buckets run on Tigris: the earlier live probe of the ROM bucket returned 'Server: Tigris OS'. Tigris's published compatibility matrix supports PutObject with a SHA256 checksum, PutBucketCors, presigned GET/PUT/HEAD/DELETE/UploadPart, range GET and multipart. Tigris's CEO stated in 2024 that there is no request-rate limit and that the max object size is 5 TB. PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration works on raw Tigris but is not exposed by Railway, so expiry must be app-driven.

findings.topic: Serving model: 302 to presign vs proxy vs Cloudflare
findings.claim: Cloudflare's Service-Specific Terms (page dated Sept 28, 2026) still require Free/Pro/Business zones to use paid services (Stream, Developer Platform, Images) to serve video or other large files via the CDN. hankshits.com is orange-clouded (server: cloudflare, cf-ray, x-railway-edge). Video bytes must therefore never be served through the hankshits.com hostname. A 302 from our route to a presigned t3.storageapi.dev URL keeps the bytes off the CF zone and off Railway service egress. At 100k clips/month with 25 plays of ~9 MB each, that is about 22.5 TB/month: $0 via bucket egress, versus about $1,125/month if proxied through Next.js at $0.05/GB.

Cloudflare caches by file extension, and MP4 is in the default list. With no Cache-Control header, a 302 is edge-cached for 20 minutes by default. HTML is not cached by default. Cloudflare will not cache a response that carries Set-Cookie or Cache-Control private/no-store/max-age=0. So /c/<slug>/v.mp4 redirects WILL be edge-cached unless we send Cache-Control. We must send an explicit max-age that is much shorter than the presign TTL, and 'no-store' on 404/410.

findings.topic: Prior art: Streamable uses exactly this pattern
findings.claim: Streamable, the canonical clip host, serves og:video as a CloudFront-signed URL with about a 3-day Expires. og:video:secure_url is a stable API URL (api-f.streamable.com/api/v1/videos/<id>/mp4). That URL answers 302 to a freshly signed CDN URL with cache-control: no-cache. The page also sets og:type video.other, twitter:card player, twitter:player (a /t/<id> player page) and 852x480 dims.

findings.topic: iMessage unfurl: verified live with LinkPresentation
findings.claim: LIVE TEST, macOS 26.5.1 LinkPresentation (the framework Messages uses; test in /tmp/hh-clips/lp). The page is fetched with UA 'facebookexternalhit/1.1 Facebot Twitterbot/1.0'. og:image and og:video BOTH follow a server 302 to a signed-URL-shaped target. The video is fetched by AppleCoreMedia: first a Range: bytes=0-1 probe, then the full range. It never sends HEAD. It also probes /apple-touch-icon-precomposed.png, /apple-touch-icon.png and /favicon.ico. Size threshold (41 KB poster): 8,758,322 / 9,471,755 / 9,802,597 / 10,104,561 byte videos were downloaded inline (videoProvider=true). 10,472,855 and 12,365,173 were NOT (only remoteVideoURL set, so tap-to-play). This matches TN3156's 10 MB associated-resource budget (about 10 MiB total). Each unfurl costs about 9 origin hits.

On prod, /apple-touch-icon.png and /apple-touch-icon-precomposed.png return 404. The layout advertises <link rel=apple-touch-icon href=/icon.svg>, and iOS does not use SVG touch icons. LinkPresentation requested both PNG paths during the unfurl test, so iMessage previews of hankshits.com links have no icon today. TN3156 asks for a square icon of at least 108 px.

findings.topic: Discord and Telegram follow a 302 for og:video
findings.claim: FxEmbed (fxtwitter), which exists to make Discord and Telegram play video inline, deliberately points og:video and twitter:player:stream at its own /2/go?url= endpoint for Discordbot/TelegramBot. That endpoint is a bare c.redirect(url, 302). Its tag set is og:video, og:video:secure_url, og:video:type, og:video:width/height, twitter:player:stream(+content_type) and og:image. It halves dims above 1920 and doubles them below 400 for Discord. So both platforms play a direct MP4 reached through a 302.

findings.topic: WhatsApp, Google Messages, Slack, X, Messenger unfurls
findings.claim: WhatsApp (official doc updated 2026-05-21): og:title, og:description and og:url must be in the <head> within the first 300 KB. og:image should be under 600 KB, at least 300 px wide, with aspect ratio no wider than 4:1. The crawl is a GET made by the SENDER's device with UA WhatsApp/2.x. There is no documented og:video playback, so the preview is an image card. Google Messages crops images taller than about 1.91:1, so the card should be landscape 1200x630. Slack only plays inline video from app-posted video blocks or allow-listed providers; others get an image card, and Slack follows up to 5 redirects. X player cards have been unreliable since 2023/2024, and X users must be 13+. Messenger: image card; inline og:video playback is not relied on.

findings.topic: Unfurl bots are not blocked at the edge
findings.claim: GETs with Discordbot, facebookexternalhit, WhatsApp, TelegramBot, Slackbot-LinkExpanding, Twitterbot and Google snippet UAs all returned 200 with the full 14 KB page from Cloudflare. That is true even though the zone serves a Cloudflare-managed content-signals robots.txt. The /c/ path must stay out of any bot-block or challenge rule.

PROTOTYPE /tmp/hh-clips/node/validate-clip.mjs, using mediabunny 1.60.0 (latest, published 2026-09-25) in Node through a CustomSource range reader. It does a top-level box walk (ftyp,moov,mdat only; exact byte accounting to EOF; moov size cap; brand allowlist), then parses moov only and walks packet metadata (no decode). The run used 9-10 range reads totalling 1.7-25 KB (0.03-0.56% of each file) in 3-62 ms. It ACCEPTED mediabunny's own in-memory fast-start output (ftyp, moov with udta/meta/ilst, mdat) and ffmpeg faststart files. It REJECTED fragmented (both ffmpeg and mediabunny), non-faststart, QuickTime, WebM, HEVC, 4K, truncated, HTML-appended polyglot and 8.3 s-GOP files. Production collapses the reads into one 64 KB Range GET, since fast-start moov is small (about 0.8 KB per second of video).

findings.topic: Visual prescreen is cheap and separates real faces from game frames (prototyped)
findings.claim: PROTOTYPE /tmp/hh-clips/node/screen.mjs: ffmpeg -skip_frame nokey decodes only keyframes into 640x640 letterboxed frames, then YuNet runs (OpenCV Zoo, MIT, 232 KB ONNX) on onnxruntime-node with 1 thread. A public-domain adult portrait scored 0.934, and 0.911 when shrunk to a 23x29 px face. Six real Hank's Hits screenshots (monster-truck, four-wheeler-3d, four-wheeler-adventure, retro-arcade, snake, four-wheeler) and synthetic test patterns scored 0.018-0.078. Cost on Apple silicon: 73-229 ms decode plus 15-21 ms per frame of inference. This is only 6 real game frames, so production thresholds MUST be calibrated on real captures from every game before launch.

Silero VAD is MIT-licensed, ships an ONNX model and processes a 30 ms chunk in under 1 ms on one CPU thread. Our capture pipeline can never contain speech: mic is blocked by Permissions-Policy, and speechSynthesis cannot be routed into a MediaStream. So detected speech in a hosted clip is a strong forged-upload or PI signal. The exception is retro-arcade ROM voice samples. For nudity: OpenNSFW2 is MIT and maintained (weights from Yahoo open_nsfw, BSD-2-Clause). NudeNet is AGPL-3.0, which is unsuitable.
sources: /tmp/hh-rec/feasibility-result.json (crossCutting: speechSynthesis cannot be routed into a MediaStream)

findings.topic: COPPA: hosting = 'enabling a child to make PI publicly available'
findings.claim: eCFR 16 CFR 312.2 (current, amended 2025-06-23; compliance required from 2026-04-22) defines collection to include '(2) Enabling a child to make personal information publicly available in identifiable form'. The operator is not considered to have collected 'if it takes reasonable measures to delete all or virtually all personal information from a child's postings before they are made public AND ALSO to delete such information from its records'. So held or rejected clips containing PI must be DELETED, not kept in quarantine (the 18 U.S.C. 2258A legal-hold exception still applies). PI item (8) is a photo/video/audio file containing a child's image or voice. Item (11) is information combined with an identifier. Item (7) is a persistent identifier, including an IP address or a cookie ID.

findings.topic: COPPA: FTC's own recipe for a no-consent upload service
findings.claim: FTC COPPA FAQ F.2 addresses a child-directed app where children upload photos and no other PI is requested. To run it without parental notice and consent, the operator must: (1) pre-screen uploads and delete any that depict children, and also delete other PI 'for example, geolocation metadata'; and (2) use persistent identifiers only for support for internal operations. It adds that an operator who does not pre-screen 'may be subject to civil penalties'. F.3 says blurring facial features is acceptable. F.4 says a site primarily directed to children must assume the uploader is a child. That maps one-to-one onto the design: face/voice/NSFW prescreen, metadata rejection, identifiers used only for rate limiting.

312.5(c)(7) exempts collecting a persistent identifier and NO OTHER PI when it is used solely for support for internal operations. The definition covers (v) 'protect the security or integrity of the user, website, or online service' and (vi) 'ensure legal or regulatory compliance'. Relying on it requires the 312.4(d)(3) notice: the specific internal operations and how we prevent the identifier being used to contact a specific individual or build a profile. 312.4(d)(2) requires the notice to say whether the service 'enables a child to make personal information publicly available' and to include the retention policy. Caveat: the site already collects a child's email at signup, which is online contact information and therefore PI, so the 'no other PI' condition is clean only for guests. That signup practice is a pre-existing COPPA gap outside clips.

findings.topic: COPPA: written retention policy and security program
findings.claim: 312.10: PI may not be retained indefinitely. The operator needs a WRITTEN retention policy (purposes, business need, deletion timeframe), and it must be published in the online notice. 312.8(b): a WRITTEN information security program that designates a coordinator, runs a risk assessment at least annually, keeps safeguards sized to the data, regularly tests and monitors them, and gets an annual evaluation. 312.8(c) requires written assurances from service providers (here Railway/Tigris and Cloudflare).

The FTC has enforced TIDA Section 3 since May 19, 2026. 'Covered platform' expressly includes image/video sharing and gaming platforms that primarily provide a forum for UGC. Duties: a clear and conspicuous notice-and-removal process (usable without an account); removal of the content AND known identical copies within 48 hours of a valid request; request IDs and status are recommended; hashing to prevent reappearance is recommended. Civil penalty: $53,088 per violation. The design's SHA-256 dedupe/blocklist implements 'known identical copies' directly.

Under 18 U.S.C. 2258A, a provider with actual knowledge of apparent CSAM must report to NCMEC's CyberTipline as soon as reasonably possible. A completed report counts as a request to preserve the reported content and related context for 1 YEAR (changed from 90 days by the REPORT Act, Pub. L. 118-59, 2024). Preserved material must be stored securely with limited access, consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework. So the takedown tool needs a legal-hold path that never deletes, separate from normal deletion.

The Copyright Office fee is $6 per designation, amendment or resubmission (current fee schedule). A designation expires after 3 years unless renewed, and the Office sends email reminders at 90/60/30/7 days. The service provider's full legal name and PHYSICAL STREET ADDRESS are published. A PO box is allowed only with prior written approval in exceptional circumstances such as a personal-safety threat. The agent's own address may be a PO box. The safe harbor also needs agent info on the site, expeditious removal, 512(g) counter-notice, and a 512(i) repeat-infringer policy.

The ICO Children's Code (15 standards) requires a DPIA, high-privacy defaults, data minimisation, geolocation and profiling off, no nudge techniques, and parental-controls transparency. It applies to services likely to be accessed by UK children even when the service is outside the UK. Hosted links make the site a 'user-to-user service' under the Online Safety Act, but only if it has UK links (a significant number of UK users or a UK target market). A link-only, opt-in-per-clip design with no feed, profile or comments is the minimal-risk shape.

Steam's 'Create a Share Link' hosts a clip on a link that expires after 2 days. Xbox deletes network-uploaded captures after 90 days. A 30-day default with creator renewal up to 90 days sits between those and meets 312.10's no-indefinite-retention rule.

findings.topic: Railway serverless and cron for the worker
findings.claim: Railway Serverless puts a service to sleep 5-10 min after its last OUTBOUND packet. Open DB pools, telemetry and private-network calls all count as outbound and keep it awake. A request from the internet or over the private network wakes it, and the first request may get a 502. Cron services must exit, run at least 5 minutes apart in UTC, and are skipped if the previous run is still active. So the screener must close its DB pool when idle, and the web app must retry the wake call.

lib/rate-limit.ts is an in-memory Map, so it resets on every deploy and is per-process. That is unusable as a cost guarantee, and clips need durable Postgres counters. getClientIP already prefers x-real-ip and the rightmost X-Forwarded-For hop (reuse it). The site CSP has media-src 'self' blob:, so it will block a /c/ <video> that loads from the bucket host. connect-src 'self' https: already allows a browser POST to Tigris. Permissions-Policy lacks display-capture=(). public/sw.js has a no-op fetch listener, which is fine but must never intercept /c/* or media. There is no admin role and no email sender. railway.toml is config-as-code, which the Railway CLI warns is deprecated and stops working on 2026-12-01.
sources: railway usage limit status CLI warning (2026-09-27)

research.designSpec:
HOSTED CLIP LINKS: DESIGN SPEC (track: hosting at near-zero cost + legal duties)
Evidence base: live LinkPresentation test (/tmp/hh-clips/lp), validator prototype (/tmp/hh-clips/node/validate-clip.mjs), prescreen prototype (/tmp/hh-clips/node/screen.mjs), plus the sources in findings.

0. PRINCIPLES (each follows from evidence, none are taste)
- Local share never depends on the server. A hosted link is an explicit per-clip tap ("Get a link"), never automatic. This is the AADC high-privacy default and COPPA minimisation.
- Video bytes never cross hankshits.com. Browser uploads go straight to the bucket via presigned POST. Views get a 302 to a presigned GET. This is required by the Cloudflare SST and keeps service egress at $0.
- Every stored identifier is either a keyed HMAC (for rate limits) or encrypted (for security and legal duties). Clips carry no FK to users. The only person-facing label is the server-issued handle snapshot, or 'a Hank's Hits player' for guests.
- Page text comes only from structured fields: registry game name, a numeric score, the handle, and a curated caption id. There is no free text, so no text moderation is needed and no PI can appear in page text.
- Every hosted clip passes structural validation plus an automated face/voice/nudity prescreen before its link is revealed (FTC FAQ F.1/F.2). Flagged clips are HELD. Held clips with PI are DELETED (312.2 'delete ... from its records').
- Hard caps in the app (Postgres) bound the worst-case bill. A Railway hard limit is NOT used, because it takes the whole site and the buckets offline.

1. INFRA LAYOUT
- New bucket 'hanks-hits-clips' in the SIDECAR project hanks-hits-storage. This follows the memory file: buckets block projectTransfer and carry a 52 h purge gate. Credentials are copied into the web, screener and sweeper services as variables CLIPS_S3_ENDPOINT, CLIPS_BUCKET, CLIPS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, CLIPS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and CLIPS_BUCKET_HOST (<bucket>.t3.storageapi.dev, virtual-hosted). Staging gets its own bucket instance; never point staging at prod.
- Bucket CORS (aws s3api put-bucket-cors --endpoint-url https://t3.storageapi.dev): [{AllowedOrigins:["https://hankshits.com"], AllowedMethods:["POST","GET","HEAD"], AllowedHeaders:["*"], ExposeHeaders:["ETag","Content-Length","Content-Range"], MaxAgeSeconds:3600}]. No wildcard origin for POST.
- New Railway service 'clip-screener' (main project; Node 22 bookworm-slim + apt ffmpeg + onnxruntime-node + models: YuNet 232 KB, OpenNSFW2 ONNX ~23 MB, Silero VAD ~2 MB). Serverless ON. It listens on the private network at :8080. Its DB pool closes after 30 s idle so it can sleep.
- New Railway cron service 'clip-sweeper' (same image, different start command), schedule '*/15 * * * *'. It must exit and close all connections.
- Cloudflare: one Cache Rule, 'hankshits.com/c/*' eligible for cache, respect origin TTL. Keep /c/* out of bot-fight/challenge rules. A CF API token (zone.cache_purge only) is optional, for purge-on-takedown.
- Railway soft usage alert (email, not a hard limit) at about current run-rate + $25. For example $85, since the workspace showed $16.68 after 8 days.

2. BUCKET KEY LAYOUT (clipId = UUIDv4; slug is separate, so keys never reveal slugs)
- c/<clipId>/v.mp4 (hosted video), c/<clipId>/card.jpg (1200x630 unfurl card), c/<clipId>/poster.jpg (video-aspect poster)
- q/<clipId>/... quarantine for held or reported clips. It is never served publicly; admin sees it only through a 5-min presign.
- lh/<clipId>/... 18 U.S.C. 2258A legal hold. It holds the object plus a JSON context file for 1 year. The sweeper never touches it; access is logged.
- 'Hide' = CopyObject c/->q/, then DeleteObject c/. Every outstanding presigned URL dies at once with a 404. This is the reason presign TTLs can be hours long.

3. SIZE / FORMAT TIERS (each cap is justified by a real constraint)
- standard: duration <= 60.5 s, video object <= 9,000,000 bytes. LinkPresentation downloaded and inline-played 10,104,561 B but not 10,472,855 B (41 KB poster), which matches TN3156's 10 MB associated-resource budget. 9.0 MB + card <= 300,000 B + poster <= 200,000 B + icon leaves about 1 MB of margin for 'limits may change'. The client encodes to fit: kbps_video = min(3500, floor((9e6*8*0.97/dur_s - 96000)/1000)). The resolution ladder is 720x1280 / 1280x720 for <= 30 s and 540x960 / 960x540 for 30-60 s. H.264 High/Main/Baseline, AAC 48 kHz, 30 fps (<= 60 allowed), 1 s keyframes (validator max gap 2.5 s), mediabunny fastStart:'in-memory' (ftyp, moov, mdat). NO metadata tags (the validator rejects udta). Rotation is 0.
- long (the Record mode): duration <= 300.5 s, video <= 52,428,800 B (50 MiB). That is Chromium's navigator.share kMaxSharedFileBytes, so any hosted clip is also shareable as a file. iMessage shows these as tap-to-play (remoteVideoURL).
- card.jpg: exactly 1200x630 baseline JPEG, <= 300,000 B. It fits WhatsApp (< 600 KB, >= 300 px, <= 4:1) and Google Messages (<= 1.91:1). The portrait frame is pillarboxed over a blurred fill with NO text (TN3156). poster.jpg: video dims, <= 200,000 B. Both must contain APP0/JFIF only: no APP1-APP15 (EXIF/XMP/GPS) and no COM segments.
- Long clips from the fragmented OPFS recorder are remuxed client-side (mediabunny Conversion, no re-encode) to in-memory fast-start before upload.

4. DATA MODEL (packages/db/src/schema/clips.ts, Drizzle; register the table, no FK to users)
clips: id uuid pk; slug text unique (12 chars base62, crypto random, ~71 bits); status enum(pending_upload, screening, live, held, hidden, rejected, expired, deleted); tier enum(standard, long); game_id text (must be in the generated registry); layout enum(portrait, landscape); width int; height int; duration_ms int; bytes bigint; card_bytes int; poster_bytes int; sha256 bytea; dhash64 bigint[] (keyframe dHashes, filled by the screener); score bigint null; score_label_key text null (from the registry); caption_id text null (curated list); handle_snapshot text null (server-issued gaming_profiles.handle or null for guest); owner_key_hash bytea (sha256 of a client-held 32-byte delete key); uploader_dev_hmac bytea; uploader_ip_enc bytea (AES-256-GCM, key CLIPS_IP_KEY); legal_hold bool default false; screen jsonb (scores and reasons only, never frames); report_count int; hidden_reason text; views int; created_at; finalized_at; live_at; expires_at; renew_count smallint; deleted_at. Indexes: partial unique (sha256) WHERE status IN ('screening','live','held','hidden'); (status, expires_at); (handle_snapshot) for account-deletion sweeps.
clip_reports: id text pk (human request id 'HHR-XXXXXX'); clip_id; reason enum(real_person, private_info, intimate_tida, mean_scary, copyright, other); details text <= 1000; reporter_contact text null (DMCA/TIDA only); reporter_hmac bytea; status; created_at; due_at (created_at + 48 h for intimate_tida); resolved_at; action.
clip_hash_blocklist: sha256 bytea pk, reason, added_at. clip_dhash_blocklist: dhash64 bigint, clip_id, added_at.
clip_quota: key text, win text, count int, bytes bigint, pk(key, win). Keys: 'ip:'+hmac(ip, K_day) | 'dev:'+hmac(hh_did) | 'acct:'+hmac(user_id) | 'global'. Windows: 'h:YYYYMMDDHH', 'd:YYYYMMDD'.
clip_settings (single row, DB-editable kill switch; the DB value beats env): mode enum(on, uploads_paused, off); live_bytes_cap bigint default 400 GB; live_bytes bigint (maintained in the same transaction); daily_bytes_cap default 60 GB; daily_count_cap default 5000; default_ttl_days 30; max_lifetime_days 90; screener_thresholds jsonb.
clip_admin_audit: id, admin_user_id, action, clip_id, at, note.

5. ROUTES (App Router; every /api/clips route returns Cache-Control: no-store; POSTs require Origin == https://hankshits.com and a JSON body validated by a zod .strict() schema)
5.1 POST /api/clips (grant). Body: {gameId, tier, durationMs, width, height, bytes, cardBytes, posterBytes, sha256Hex, ownerKeyHashHex, score?, captionId?}. Session is optional: handle_snapshot comes from the session's gaming profile when signed in and the handle is shown on leaderboards, otherwise null. It sets cookie hh_did (128-bit random, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 1 y) if absent; this is the only Set-Cookie in the flow and it lives on /api only. One SERIALIZABLE transaction:
  a) settings.mode must be 'on', else 503 {state:'resting'}.
  b) The registry policy for gameId must not be 'off'. For retro-arcade the ROM must be on the kid-safe allowlist (the core/rom id is sent as a structured field; the title is never stored or rendered publicly). Dims, tier, bytes and duration must be inside the tier caps. captionId must be in the curated list. Score must be 0 <= score <= MAX_CURRENCY.
  c) If sha256 is in the blocklist, return 422 with generic kid copy.
  d) If sha256 is already live, return 200 {slug, url} with no upload. This is dedupe, and a double tap costs nothing.
  e) Quota upserts: INSERT INTO clip_quota(key,win,count,bytes) VALUES(...) ON CONFLICT (key,win) DO UPDATE SET count=clip_quota.count+1, bytes=clip_quota.bytes+EXCLUDED.bytes RETURNING count, bytes. Roll back if any cap is exceeded (section 7). A separate lightweight 'attempt' counter per IP-hmac is committed even on failure, to throttle hammering.
  f) Reserve bytes: UPDATE clip_settings SET live_bytes=live_bytes+$total WHERE live_bytes+$total<=live_bytes_cap RETURNING. If no row returns, set mode 'uploads_paused' (auto-trip) and return 503.
  g) Insert the clips row with status pending_upload.
  h) Build 3 presigned POST policies with @aws-sdk/s3-presigned-post, Expires 900 s (1800 s for long). Conditions: {bucket}, ['eq','$key',key], ['content-length-range', n, n] (EXACT size), ['eq','$Content-Type','video/mp4' | 'image/jpeg'], ['eq','$Cache-Control','public, max-age=43200'], ['eq','$x-amz-meta-clip', clipId], ['eq','$success_action_status','204']. Also send x-amz-checksum-sha256 as a field; it is best-effort because Tigris POST checksum support is unverified, and the screener re-hashes regardless.
  i) Fire-and-forget POST http://clip-screener.railway.internal:8080/wake, so the worker warms while the upload runs.
  Response: {clipId, uploads:[{url, fields}x3]}.
5.2 The client uploads the 3 files with XHR multipart POST straight to Tigris (upload.onprogress drives a named-step progress bar). It retries each file up to 3 times with backoff; after 15 min it gets a fresh grant for the same clip (idempotent on ownerKeyHash+sha256).
5.3 POST /api/clips/:id/finalize, header X-Clip-Key (the raw key; the server compares sha256). Steps: HeadObject x3 (ContentLength must equal the declared size; ContentType must match); one Range GET bytes=0-65535 of v.mp4 plus the rest of moov if it is larger; box-walk and mediabunny moov validation (validate-clip.mjs rules: layout ftyp,moov,mdat; brands; moov <= 4 MB; exactly 1 avc video + <= 1 aac audio; no other tracks; no udta; profile 0x42/0x4d/0x64; dims <= 1280x720 long/short with short >= 180 and even; rotation 0; duration and fps caps; first packet key; key gap <= 2.5 s; sample bytes <= mdat payload). On failure: status rejected, DeleteObjects, release reserved bytes, 422. On success: status screening, then POST /screen to the screener with retries at 1 s, 2 s, 4 s (the first call to a slept service may 502). If still unreachable, the sweeper re-pings.
5.4 GET /api/clips/:id/status (X-Clip-Key) returns {status, slug?, url?, expiresAt?}. The client polls every 1 s for up to 60 s, then every 5 s. The link is revealed ONLY when the status is live. It is never pre-shared, because an unfurl generated before the clip is live is frozen into the recipient's message forever.
5.5 DELETE /api/clips/:id (X-Clip-Key): immediate DeleteObjects, status deleted, PI columns nulled, bytes released. POST /api/clips/:id/renew (X-Clip-Key): expires_at = min(now+30 d, created_at+90 d); allowed only while live.
5.6 GET /c/:slug (server component, reads NO cookies so it stays cacheable). Headers: Cache-Control public, max-age=60, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60; X-Robots-Tag noindex, nofollow, noarchive; plus <meta name=robots content=noindex,nofollow>. Do NOT Disallow /c/ in robots.txt, because some unfurlers honor it. Body: <video controls playsinline preload=metadata poster=<presigned poster> src=<presigned v.mp4, 12 h TTL>>, the game name, score, handle or 'a Hank's Hits player', the curated caption, 'This link disappears on <date>', a big 'Play <Game> free' CTA to /games/<id>, and a 'Report' button. No view counts, comments, likes, feed or related-clips rail. Tombstoned slugs get a 410 page ('This clip has expired. Play <Game>!') with generic og tags. Unknown slugs get a 404. Both send no-store.
  og/twitter tags (identical for every UA, per TN3156): og:site_name "Hank's Hits"; og:type video.other; og:title "<Game>: <score label> <score>" (no site name); og:description "A <N>-second clip by <handle|a Hank's Hits player>. Play free at hankshits.com" (80 chars max); og:url canonical; og:image https://hankshits.com/c/<slug>/card.jpg + :width 1200 :height 630 :type image/jpeg :alt; og:video and og:video:secure_url https://hankshits.com/c/<slug>/v.mp4 + :type video/mp4 + :width/:height (actual); twitter:card player; twitter:player https://hankshits.com/c/<slug>/embed + :width/:height; twitter:player:stream = the v.mp4 URL + :content_type video/mp4; twitter:image = card; theme-color. The head must be in the first 300 KB (WhatsApp). og tags always point at the STABLE hankshits.com URLs and never at presigned URLs, so presign expiry can never break an unfurl.
5.7 GET|HEAD /c/:slug/v.mp4, /card.jpg, /poster.jpg. Look up the live clip (in-process LRU, 30 s). GET returns 302 Location = getSignedUrl(GetObjectCommand{Key, ResponseContentType fixed, ResponseContentDisposition 'inline; filename="hankshits-<gameId>.mp4"'}, expiresIn 43200). HEAD returns 302 to a presigned HeadObject, because a GET-signed URL fails HEAD; LinkPresentation never sent HEAD, but other crawlers may. Use NextResponse.redirect(url, 302) explicitly (Next's default redirect is 307). Headers: Cache-Control public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300 (explicit, otherwise Cloudflare caches 302s for 20 min); Referrer-Policy no-referrer; X-Robots-Tag noindex. Not live: 404/410 with no-store. Per-IP limit 600/min (section 7).
5.8 GET /c/:slug/embed: minimal HTML with a <video> and a 'Watch on Hank's Hits' link (target=_blank). CSP frame-ancestors https:, with no X-Frame-Options for this path only. No report button inside the frame (it links out instead).
5.9 POST /api/clips/report {slug, reason, details?, contact?}. No account needed. It returns {requestId}. real_person, private_info and intimate_tida HIDE the clip IMMEDIATELY on the first report (asymmetric risk). mean_scary hides at 2 distinct reporter hmacs. copyright goes to the DMCA form. Report caps: 30/day per IP-hmac; a reporter hmac with more than 10 reports that admins overturned loses auto-hide power.
5.10 Legal pages (plain words, kid-readable summary first): /privacy (the full 312.4(d) notice), /legal/clips (how links work, rules, retention, 'messaging apps may keep a copy of the preview'), /legal/report (TIDA notice-and-removal form, conspicuous, linked from every /c/ page footer and the home footer), /legal/dmca (agent info plus the 512(c)(3) notice form and the 512(g) counter-notice form).
5.11 Admin /admin/clips: next-auth session + ADMIN_USER_IDS allowlist + re-auth within 12 h; every action goes to clip_admin_audit. Queues: held, reported (a TIDA countdown is shown), screening-stuck. Actions: approve (q/->c/, live), remove (delete + blocklist sha256 + dHash), legal-hold + NCMEC (move to lh/, mark legal_hold, export the context JSON, never delete), purge by uploader_dev_hmac or IP-hmac cluster, mode toggle (on/uploads_paused/off), cap editing, budget meter (live_bytes vs cap, daily counts, screener p95, hold rate). Frames are shown blurred until the admin clicks.

6. SCREENER PIPELINE (clip-screener; queue = clips WHERE status='screening' ORDER BY finalized_at FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; concurrency 2)
  1) Stream GetObject v.mp4 ONCE (bucket egress free, service ingress free). Tee it into SHA-256 (must equal the declared hash, else reject) and into ffmpeg stdin, which works because the file is fast-start. ffmpeg has two outputs: '-skip_frame nokey' video scaled/padded to 640x640 bgr24 on pipe:3 (every keyframe, i.e. 1/s; stride down to 120 frames max for the long tier), and audio resampled to 16 kHz mono s16le on pipe:4. A decode error means reject; this caught a corrupted file in the prototype.
  2) YuNet on every keyframe. max score >= T_face means HOLD. The prototype saw real faces at 0.91-0.93 and game frames at 0.02-0.08. Set T_face on the calibration corpus (default 0.60 until then).
  3) OpenNSFW2 (224x224) on the same frames. max >= T_nsfw means HOLD.
  4) Brand-band check. The compositor paints a fixed logo sub-rectangle in its branding strip. The mean absolute difference against the reference render for that layout must be below T_band on at least 80% of keyframes, else HOLD. This proves the clip came from our compositor (or from a forger who copied the band) and costs about 0.1 ms per frame.
  5) Silero VAD on the audio. Speech ratio >= 2% means HOLD for every game except where the registry says voice:'ignore' (retro-arcade, where ROMs have digitized voices); faces are still screened there.
  6) card.jpg and poster.jpg: JPEG marker walk (SOI; APP0 only; SOF dims exact; EOI; no trailing bytes), decode, then YuNet + NSFW.
  7) dHash64 per keyframe. More than 3 matches at Hamming distance <= 6 against clip_dhash_blocklist means HOLD. This catches re-encoded re-uploads of removed content (FTC TIDA guidance recommends hashing).
  Decision: all pass means LIVE (live_at=now, expires_at=now+default_ttl). Any HOLD signal means HELD (copy to q/, delete c/, alert the admin). Structural or decode failure means REJECTED (delete objects, release bytes). Only scores are written to clips.screen. Measured prototype cost is 0.16-0.44 s on Apple silicon for 6-12 keyframes. Budget 2 vCPU-s per 30 s clip on Railway x86. Targets: p95 under 5 s warm, under 15 s from sleep; the wake at grant time hides the cold start behind the upload.

7. RATE LIMITS AND CAPS (durable Postgres, never the in-memory lib/rate-limit.ts; reuse getClientIP())
Per identity (grants): guest device 6/h, 20/day; signed-in account 10/h, 40/day; per IP-hmac 60/h, 300/day (school NAT); live links per device or account <= 60; bytes per device <= 600 MB/day. Global: daily_count_cap 5,000; daily_bytes_cap 60 GB; live_bytes_cap 400 GB. Attempts (including failures) per IP-hmac 120/h. Finalize/status/renew/delete per clip 120/min. /c/* pages and redirects per IP 600/min at origin; Cloudflare absorbs repeats (the HTML is edge-cached for 5 min, and so are the 302s). Reports: 30/day per IP-hmac. HMAC keys: K_day is derived from a CLIPS_HMAC_SECRET plus the UTC date, so stored hashes cannot be joined across days. Counters are deleted after 48 h.
Auto-trips (checked at every grant; alert the admin): live_bytes >= cap means uploads_paused; the daily count or bytes cap means paused until 00:00 UTC; a screener error rate > 20% over 15 min means new grants are refused ('links are resting'); a hold rate > 25% over the last 50 clips means paused plus an alert (a calibration regression or an attack). The kid UX when paused: 'Links are taking a nap. You can still share your video!' The local share button is always available.

8. EXPIRY AND SWEEPER (clip-sweeper, every 15 min; idempotent; every destructive step verified)
 a) live/hidden with expires_at < now: DeleteObjects (up to 1000 keys per call), then HeadObject a sample of 20 and FAIL LOUD if any still exists, then status expired, null the PI columns (owner_key_hash, uploader_dev_hmac, uploader_ip_enc, handle_snapshot), release bytes, and optionally purge the Cloudflare URLs.
 b) pending_upload older than 1 h: delete any partial objects, release bytes, status deleted.
 c) screening older than 2 min: re-ping the screener. Older than 30 min: HELD with reason screen_timeout.
 d) held older than 7 days without an admin decision: DELETE (312.2 delete-from-records), unless legal_hold.
 e) intimate_tida reports unresolved at 44 h: auto-remove plus blocklist. The content was already hidden at report time, so this is a guaranteed 48 h backstop.
 f) clip_quota windows older than 48 h are deleted. Tombstones (slug, game_id, status, removed_at with no PI) older than 12 months are deleted.
 g) Daily at 03:00 UTC: ListObjectsV2 on c/ and q/ against the DB, deleting orphan objects (keys with no live/held/hidden row); ListMultipartUploads, aborting anything older than 1 h; recompute live_bytes from the listing and fail loud if drift > 1%; write a budget summary to the admin dashboard.
 h) Account deletion (existing flow): also delete clips WHERE handle_snapshot = the user's handle.

9. HEADERS / CSP (next.config.ts headers(), last match wins, so order the rules: global, /emulator, /c/:path*, /c/:slug/embed)
- Global: add display-capture=() to Permissions-Policy (camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), display-capture=()).
- /c/:path*: CSP "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://static.cloudflareinsights.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; media-src 'self' https://${CLIPS_BUCKET_HOST}; connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self' data:; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'". Also X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Robots-Tag noindex. CSP3 does not ignore the host after a redirect, so media-src must name the bucket host.
- /c/:slug/embed: the same, but frame-ancestors https: and no X-Frame-Options.
- CLIPS_BUCKET_HOST is read at BUILD time. Add ARG CLIPS_BUCKET_HOST to the Dockerfile builder stage. A boot-time assertion must check that the presigner's host equals the CSP host and crash loudly otherwise.
- Game pages keep connect-src 'self' https: (it already allows the POST to Tigris).
- sw.js must never call respondWith for /c/*, /api/clips* or cross-origin media.
- Add a real 180x180 /apple-touch-icon.png (prod returns 404 today, and LinkPresentation requests it).

10. PER-GAME HOSTING POLICY (literal fields in each metadata.ts, e.g. clips: { hosted: 'on' | 'off' | 'allowlist', voice: 'hold' | 'ignore' }; read by the server from the build-time generated registry)
- Built-in canvas, R3F and iframe games: on/hold. Oregon Trail: on. Leader and party names live only in the DOM and must never be rasterized; add a unit test that the capture registration never reads name fields.
- Wordle: on, but hosted renders use colour-only tiles (maskLetters). The dictionary accepts rude words.
- DOM-replay games (2048, chess, checkers, cookie-clicker, memory-match, quoridor, snake): on. Renderers draw state only, never user strings. Brag cards show the handle at most, NEVER a first name (this overrides the feasibility suggestion of a 'first-name watermark').
- retro-arcade: 'allowlist' (kid-rated titles only), voice:'ignore'. The public page and og tags say 'Retro Arcade', never the ROM title (copyright visibility).
- Kid-built (madeByKid) games: on only after the put-it-online scrub. The make-a-game skill must add the rule 'no real photos, no recorded voices, no typed names drawn into the canvas'. A game that draws runtime-typed text into the canvas must set hosted:'off'.
- Captions come from a curated list of about 20 kid lines plus emoji, with no typing. The handle comes from the server, and the compositor draws it; the server cannot verify pixels, and that residual risk is covered by the prescreen and reports.

11. COST MODEL (assumptions stated; all numbers are per month)
Assumptions: 95% standard clips averaging 8.45 MB (8.0 video + 0.3 card + 0.15 poster); 5% long clips averaging 30.45 MB; blended 9.6 MB. Retention: 80% expire at 30 d, 10% renewed to 90 d, 10% deleted by the owner at about 5 d, giving a mean lifetime of 33.5 d (factor 1.12). Views: 20 human views plus 5 unfurls per clip. HTML is 16 KB, a 302 is 0.7 KB, and each unfurl makes about 5 redirects. The page <video> uses a presigned src directly (no extra hop). Screener: 2 vCPU-s per clip; 0.45 GB RAM while awake; it sleeps 5-10 min after idle.
- 1k clips: storage 10.75 GB-mo, billed 11 = $0.17; service egress 0.42 GB = $0.02; screener CPU $0.02 + RAM (about 12 min awake per clip, so about 12k min) $1.25; sweeper $0.05; web CPU ~$0. TOTAL about $1.50.
- 10k clips: storage 108 GB-mo = $1.62; egress 4.2 GB = $0.21; screener CPU $0.15 + RAM (awake about 24/7) $4.49; sweeper $0.05; web $0.02. TOTAL about $6.55.
- 100k clips: storage 1,075 GB-mo = $16.13 (over the Hobby 1 TB cap; fine on Pro; the default live_bytes_cap of 400 GB would bind first, so either raise the cap deliberately or shorten default_ttl to 14 d, which gives about $7); egress 42 GB = $2.10 (about $0.30 with the CF HTML cache rule); screener CPU $1.54 + RAM $4.49; sweeper $0.05; web $0.21. TOTAL about $24.50.
- Video bytes delivered (25 plays x about 9 MB): 225 GB / 2.25 TB / 22.5 TB, all at $0 (bucket egress). If proxied through the Next.js service instead, the same bytes would cost $11 / $112 / $1,125. That is the single biggest reason for the 302 design.
WORST-CASE ABUSE (default caps, attacker with unlimited IPs and devices): storage <= 400 GB live = $6.00. Screener <= 5,000 clips/day x 2 s gives $2.31 CPU + $4.49 RAM. Origin egress is bounded by per-IP limits and CF edge caching of HTML and 302s; a generous ceiling of 100 GB is $5. Upload ingress, API operations and bucket egress are all $0. CEILING about $18/month. Beyond that, uploads auto-pause. POST policies bind the exact key and exact size, so a leaked policy can only overwrite its own object within 15 min. Nobody can write to the bucket without a policy we signed, and every grant passes caps and reservation in one SERIALIZABLE transaction. Stored bytes are counted in the same transaction that reserves them, and the nightly reconcile against the bucket listing fails loud on drift.

12. LEGAL CHECKLIST (must be complete before the hosted-link flag turns on; local sharing needs none of it)
COPPA (16 CFR 312, as amended; compliance from 2026-04-22):

13. VERIFICATION GATES (must pass before launch; each checks a claim that current evidence cannot settle)
 1. Bucket spike (needs Jack's write grant to create the bucket): POST content-length-range rejects n+1 and n-1 bytes; eq Content-Type is enforced; the x-amz-checksum-sha256 POST field is honoured or ignored (the screener re-hash covers either case); presigned GET response-content-type/disposition overrides work; presigned HEAD works; GET after DELETE returns 404 immediately (so takedown is instant); the CORS preflight/response for https://hankshits.com works; the virtual-hosted host is confirmed for the CSP.
 2. Real-device unfurls against a staging /c/ page: iMessage (iOS 26; also rerun /tmp/hh-clips/lp/lp against the real URL), WhatsApp, Discord, Telegram, Google Messages, Messenger, Slack. Record each result in a table.
 3. Screener calibration on REAL captures: at least 50 clips per game across all 26 games, plus allowlisted retro titles and brag cards. Record the distributions of max face, NSFW, speech and band scores. Set thresholds for zero holds on the corpus and at least 0.9 detection on a forged set built from public-domain ADULT portraits and voices (never real child imagery). Re-run whenever a game is added. Never tune thresholds against self-made fixtures.
 4. Load: 200 grants in 60 s from one IP must stay within the caps with no double-reservation (SERIALIZABLE retry loop); sweeper deletions are verified by HeadObject.
risksAndMitigations: False holds on cartoon faces (emoji, drawn characters, kid-built art) would degrade instant sharing. Mitigation: calibrate T_face on a real multi-game corpus before launch; a hold is soft (the kid keeps local share, and the admin approves with one click); auto-pause triggers if the hold rate exceeds 25% (a sign of calibration regression).

A forged upload (hand-crafted H.264 via the API) could carry a child's face, voice or name. Mitigation: FTC FAQ F.2-style prescreen on EVERY keyframe (faces), audio (Silero VAD) and posters; brand-band verification; metadata rejection; the report button hides instantly on real_person/private_info; held PI is deleted, not stored. Residual: text-only PI drawn into a forged frame is not OCR-screened (rejected on cost and recall grounds) and is covered by report + 30-day expiry.

Takedown latency. A presigned URL issued before a report stays valid. Mitigation: 'hide' moves the object out of c/ (CopyObject to q/, then DeleteObject), which kills every outstanding presign; the 302 and HTML edge caches are at most 5 min and point at a deleted object. Gate: verify GET-after-DELETE returns 404 immediately on Tigris (spike).

Copies outside our control. iMessage and WhatsApp previews are generated on the sender's device, and the downloaded media travels with the message, so an expired or removed clip can persist in recipients' chats. Mitigation: disclose this in /privacy and /legal/clips in kid language; keep the prescreen strict because removal is not total.

Cloudflare SST violation if anyone later 'optimises' by proxying video through hankshits.com. Mitigation: a code comment plus a unit test asserting that /c/*/v.mp4 only ever returns 302/404/410; never add a CNAME for the bucket under the orange-clouded zone.

The Cloudflare default 20-min caching of 302s on .mp4 paths could serve redirects to expired presigns if Cache-Control is ever dropped. Mitigation: explicit Cache-Control max-age=300 (much less than the 12 h presign TTL) and a test on the headers.

The in-memory rate limiter in lib/rate-limit.ts cannot bound cost: it resets on every deploy and is per-replica. Mitigation: durable Postgres quota counters and byte reservation in one SERIALIZABLE transaction; nightly reconciliation against the bucket listing that fails loud.

A Railway hard usage limit would suspend BUCKETS and take the site offline (the ROMs are in the same workspace). Mitigation: never set a hard limit for clips cost; use app-level caps (worst case about $18/month) plus a Railway soft email alert.

Serverless screener cold start and 502 on first wake. Mitigation: wake at grant time so it warms during the upload; finalize retries at 1/2/4 s; the sweeper re-pings rows stuck in screening; the DB pool closes when idle so the service can actually sleep.

Single full-access bucket key shared by the web, screener and sweeper (Railway exposes one credential pair per bucket). Mitigation: server envs only, never sent to the client; rotation runbook; audit admin actions. If Tigris IAM scoped keys ever become reachable for Railway buckets, split them into read-only (screener) and write (web) keys.

Retro-arcade clips publicise commercial ROMs, which invites DMCA notices aimed at the ROM library itself. Mitigation: allowlist of titles, no ROM titles in page text or og tags, a working DMCA agent and process. Flag the ROM-licensing exposure to Jack separately; it is outside this track.

Legal-address exposure: DMCA agent designation publishes the service provider's street address. Mitigation: operate through an entity with a business address, or request the PO-box exception. Jack must decide before launch.

Pre-existing, outside the clips scope, found during this research: (a) signup collects a child's email without parental notice or consent (COPPA); (b) the prod /apple-touch-icon.png returns 404, which degrades every iMessage unfurl today; (c) the railway.toml config-as-code format is deprecated and stops working on 2026-12-01, per the Railway CLI warning. Mitigation: fix (b) inside the clips PR because unfurls depend on it; file (a) and (c) as issues with this evidence.

Hobby 1 TB cap, if the workspace is ever downgraded (it currently appears to be on Pro, inferred from the $20 Agent-limit default). Mitigation: live_bytes_cap defaults to 400 GB, and the admin budget meter shows headroom against the plan cap.

Discord, X and Messenger embed behaviour changes without notice. Mitigation: the tag set mirrors FxEmbed and Streamable (the widest-compatible prior art); a real-device unfurl table is re-run quarterly; the image card fallback always exists.
rejectedAlternatives: Streaming clip bytes through the Next.js service (backend proxy): $0.05/GB service egress means about $1,125/month at 100k clips, plus memory and latency on the single web instance.

Serving video through the Cloudflare-proxied hankshits.com zone (cache rule on mp4, or a CNAME for the bucket): prohibited for Free/Pro/Business zones by Cloudflare's Service-Specific Terms unless a paid service is used.
Cloudflare Stream/R2, Mux, YouTube or Vimeo hosting: new paid or outside services, and a disclosure of kids' content to third parties.

Server-side transcoding of every upload with ffmpeg: about 10-30 vCPU-s per clip for no gain, since the client already encodes H.264/AAC with WebCodecs. The server only decodes keyframes for screening.

Putting presigned URLs directly in og tags: they cannot be refreshed once a platform caches them, and they cannot be revoked except by deleting the object. Stable hankshits.com URLs that 302 to fresh presigns (the Streamable pattern) avoid both problems.
Bucket lifecycle rules for expiry: not supported by Railway, even though Tigris supports them. An app-driven sweeper with verified deletes is used instead.
Presigned PUT without size binding: the size cannot be enforced. A presigned POST with an exact content-length-range is the Railway-documented pattern.
Multipart uploads for the standard tier: unnecessary at 9 MB or less, and presigned UploadPart does not bind part size, which leaves a storage-burst window.
Reusing the in-memory lib/rate-limit.ts for clips: it resets on deploy and is per-process, so it cannot guarantee a cost ceiling.
A foreign key from clips to users or gaming_profiles: it would combine the clip with an email-bearing account (PI item 11). A handle snapshot plus a device-held delete key is used instead.
