It comes from Safari itself through the private WKWebsiteDataStore._persistedSites SPI (macOS 15.2 / iOS 18.2), so Safari can grant tab origins by a closed heuristic. 'Always false in a tab' is plausible but has to be tested on a device. The 7*24h constant is only the CHECK interval of a separate time-based eviction. That eviction was enabled in WebKit in May 2026, uses a 180-day wall-clock threshold, skips persisted, active and push-subscribed origins, and WebsiteDataStore::timeBasedEvictionMode returns Disabled unless tracking prevention is OFF. ITP's 7-day rule is still the operative one in default Safari.
sources: GitHub commit log for WebsiteDataStoreConfiguration.cpp: 2026-05-28 'Enable time-based data eviction'

verdicts.claim: ITP's 7-day script-writable deletion includes WebsiteDataType::FileSystem (OPFS); Home Screen web apps are exempt.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed on WebKit main: monitoredDataTypes includes FileSystem and LocalStorage, and the standalone domain is in the exempt set. A consequence the track missed: the same sweep also deletes the spec's device-learning localStorage keys (hanks-hits-clips-device, the crash marker, the nudge timers). After a 7-day gap the tier learning resets together with the clips.

verdicts.claim: OPFS is unavailable in Safari Private Browsing; fall back to IndexedDB Blob storage.
verdicts.correction: OPFS: confirmed, getDirectory rejects with 'unknown transient reason'. For the IDB fallback: current WebKit writes IDB Blobs to disk even in ephemeral sessions (IDBTransaction writeBlobsToDiskForIndexedDB(isEphemeral)). Older Safari threw 'are not yet supported' on Blob puts in private mode, so the fallback chain must catch that and drop to memory.

verdicts.claim: OPFS support matrix: createSyncAccessHandle Safari 15.2/Chrome 102/Chrome Android 109/Firefox 111; createWritable Safari 26+; move Safari 15.2; remove Chrome-only; estimate Safari 17.
iPhone WebContent process limit is about 1.5 GB; typed arrays and wasm are capped at about 2 GB by the Gigacage.
verdicts.correction: The 1.5 GB statement is confirmed, from a WebKit engineer on bug 268816. The 2 GB Gigacage figure is stale: a later comment on the same bug says 277124@main increased the iOS Gigacage. For budgeting, the spec's '~2% of 1.5 GB' framing is misleading. Headroom is 1.5 GB minus the game's own footprint (R3F scenes, EmulatorJS), which nobody has measured.

verdicts.claim: EmulatorJS #1220: iPhone Safari jetsams EmulatorJS after 60-90 s; page memory grows ~14 MB/s (framebuffer x fps), so per-frame compositor work must be soak-tested.
verdicts.correction: #1220 exists (2026-05-25), but the maintainer closed it as a duplicate of #1143. That thread shows repeated jetsams on iOS 26.1-26.6 through 2026-08-05, on EmulatorJS 4.2.3, with no recording involved. Reporters attribute it to WASM ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH / low INITIAL_HEAP; the maintainer attributes it to WebKit (bug 284752). The page-memory = framebuffer x fps theory is one user's guess, and other reporters contradict it. The repo loads cdn.emulatorjs.org/stable, which currently resolves to 4.2.3 and is unpinned. So retro-arcade on iPhone is a pre-existing crash, independent of this feature.

verdicts.claim: Device signals: deviceMemory Chrome-only with Chrome 147+ buckets 1/2/4/8 (Android) and 2-32 (desktop); Safari 26 freezes the iOS UA version at 18_6 while Version/26 increments.
verdicts.correction: The deviceMemory buckets are confirmed by BCD notes. The UA part is incomplete. The frozen OS token has since moved (Version/26.6 ships 'iPhone OS 18_7'). Chrome for iOS (CriOS), Firefox for iOS (FxiOS) and in-app WKWebViews send NO Version/ token at all, and Chrome iOS even reports a real '26_0_0'. iPadOS sends a Macintosh UA by default. A tier table keyed on 'Safari Version token' misclassifies all of these.
sources: gh issue view 1143 -R EmulatorJS/EmulatorJS (2026-08-05 comment: Version/26.6, 'iPhone OS 18_7')

verdicts.claim: iOS 26/27 support iPhone 11/SE 2 and later (A13); XS/XR stop at iOS 18.
iOS Low Power Mode throttles rAF to 30 fps (WebKit bug 168837).
AudioContext 'interrupted' is in Safari 9+ and Chrome 136+; getOutputTimestamp is in Safari 14.1, Chrome 57 and Firefox 70.
WebCodecs reclamation: a UA MAY reclaim inactive codecs (no output for 10 s) even in the foreground; hence close idle encoders after 8 s.
verdicts.correction: The spec text is confirmed. No shipping engine actually does this in the foreground. Chromium starts its idle timer only when is_applying_pressure_ (hardware codec) AND global_pressure_exceeded_ AND is_backgrounded_ all hold. Its threshold is 90 s, and it needs two consecutive inactive 45 s ticks. WebKit's Modules/webcodecs has no reclamation code at all. So a visible, paused encoder is never reclaimed, and the 8 s foreground close only adds avoidable re-creates.

verdicts.claim: WebKit exposes VideoEncoder/AudioEncoder/VideoFrame to DedicatedWorker and a main-thread VideoFrame can be transferred to a worker.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed: the IDLs say Exposed=(Window,DedicatedWorker), and SerializedScriptValue::create accepts a WebCodecsVideoFrame in the transfer list. Separately, WebKit ignores hardwareAcceleration for encoders (it always uses VideoToolbox), so there is no prefer-software rung on iOS.

verdicts.claim: Chromium web share is limited to 50 MB total and needs type video/mp4 with a .mp4 name.
verdicts.correction: The limit is 50 MiB (52,428,800 bytes) on both Android (ShareServiceImpl.java MAX_SHARED_FILE_BYTES) and desktop (kMaxSharedFileBytes), with at most 10 files; mp4 is in the permitted extension and MIME lists.

verdicts.claim: mediabunny 1.60.0 fastStart accepts false/'in-memory'/'reserve'/'fragmented'; 'reserve' needs maximumPacketCount; fragmented exposes onMoof/onMdat.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed in output-format.ts. It also backs the spec's configKey segmentation: IsobmffMuxer.getVideoTrackData builds the track's decoder config once, from the first packet, and ignores later meta.decoderConfig. Packets from a re-created encoder with a different avcC would silently corrupt the track.

verdicts.claim: Repo: signOutAndClear clears registered/suffixed localStorage keys and broadcasts a reload; credentials signIn uses redirect:false, so the account can change without a reload.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed. Two consequences the track missed. First, nextAuthSignOut({callbackUrl}) navigates, so the signing-out tab reloads anyway; the real leak paths are the redirect:false sign-in and a bfcache Back restore. Second, storage-keys.ts already documents the guest-then-first-sign-in edge, and purging the ring on ANY user-id change would destroy the replay a guest just played when they sign in to save it.

verdicts.claim: Repo: sw.js fetch handler is a no-op; manifest is standalone + landscape; useGameShell pauses on visibilitychange only when canPause.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed. The visibility pause also requires pauseOnBlur (`if (!canPause || !pauseOnBlur) return`).

verdicts.claim: Iframe rAF timestamps must be shifted by the timeOrigin delta.
verdicts.correction: Correct per the HTML spec. The same applies to AudioTimestamp.performanceTime from getOutputTimestamp() on an AudioContext created inside the four-wheeler-adventure srcdoc iframe or the EmulatorJS iframe. The spec only converts rAF times, so audio anchors from iframe contexts would be offset by the iframe's load delay.

verdicts.claim: Design (e): a DOM-attached canvas is needed for the MediaRecorder/captureStream fallback because of WebKit bug 240380.
verdicts.correction: Bug 240380 was RESOLVED FIXED on 2022-05-25 (r294864 / 250996@main), which shipped in Safari 16. Only iOS 15 needs an attached canvas.

verdicts.claim: Design section 5: the CaptureClock gives about 30 fps at any source cadence with no judder; 'at 60 Hz and 120 Hz the cadence comes out exactly regular' (and synthetic CFR was rejected for judder at 144 Hz).
verdicts.correction: The average is 30.0 fps at every rate, and cadence is regular only when Hz is a multiple of 30. My simulation of the exact algorithm gives alternating gaps at 48 Hz (20.8/41.7 ms), 50 Hz (20/40), 72 Hz (27.8/41.7), 75 Hz (26.7/40), 100 Hz (30/40), 144 Hz (27.8/34.7) and 165 Hz (30.3/36.4). That is visible judder in the clip. An integer vsync stride (fps = Hz / ceil(Hz/31)) gives constant spacing: 25 fps at 50/75 Hz, 28.8 at 144 Hz.

verdicts.claim: @mediabunny/aac-encoder is the Safari < 26 AAC fallback.
verdicts.correction: Workable. The 1.60.0 bundle is ~1 MB (inline WASM, MPL-2.0 wrapper around libavcodec). It runs the encode in its OWN blob-URL worker (new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(blob))), so it does not block the clips worker. It needs worker-src blob: plus unsafe-eval or wasm-unsafe-eval, and the current site CSP allows both.

designSpecProblems: iPhone capture path (sections 0e, 1): the spec composites into an OffscreenCanvas 'never in the DOM' because of layer cost. That is exactly the path WebKit implements as a synchronous getPixelBuffer readback plus copy on every captured frame. ImageBitmap goes the same way, so calibrating between OffscreenCanvas and createImageBitmap picks between two equally slow paths. A detached HTMLCanvasElement has no composited layer, so the layer rationale does not hold. The only zero-readback VideoFrame source in WebKit is an HTMLCanvasElement with a WebGL context. The WebGL texImage2D fast path accepts only I420/NV12 VideoFrames, and texImage2D(canvas) uses getImageData/copyNativeImage. So WebKit has no zero-readback way to overlay a HUD. Required: benchmark on a real iPhone, before any defaults ship, (a) the 2D compositor readback at T1/T2 dims and (b) new VideoFrame(webglGameCanvas) passed straight to an encoder configured at the tier size (encoder-side scaling, HUD moved to the end card). Test that WebKit's encoder accepts frames whose size differs from the config. Pick the path per engine from that data, not from Chrome-desktop numbers. Sources: WebCodecsVideoFrame.cpp ~215-275, HTMLCanvasElement.cpp 831-862, GraphicsContextGLCocoa.mm 863-881, WebGLRenderingContextBase.cpp 3231-3240 and 3431-3452.

Cold start (sections 0a, 6): the pre-warm only removes the stall if it starts 10-17 s before the game encoder. The stall recurs on every Chrome process launch (measured, reused profile), so a kid who opens Chrome and taps a game straight away still hits it. The watchdog rule 'if the pre-warm is still pending, stay WARMING and drop frames' is wrong for desktop. I measured that a prefer-software encoder started during the pending hardware warm-up outputs within ~90 ms, so bridge at 2.5 s regardless of the pre-warm, then hand over to hardware at the next keyframe once the warm-up finishes. That hand-over is a configKey segment boundary, so the clip assembler must accept it.

Error ladder assumes a software rung everywhere: Chromium builds OpenH264 only when !(is_ios || (is_android && current_cpu == 'arm')). 32-bit Chrome on Android therefore has no software H.264. Google historically shipped 64-bit Chrome only to Android 10+ phones with 8 GB+ RAM, which excludes most kids' phones. WebKit ignores hardwareAcceleration for encoders, so iOS has no software rung either. Drive every rung from isConfigSupported probes, never from an assumed ladder. On an Android phone with no H.264 at all, fall back to MediaRecorder if it offers mp4, otherwise to a WebM/VP8 path with a hosted-link share.

Section 6, foreground encoder close after 8 s idle (pause menu, start overlay): no engine reclaims a visible encoder (Chromium needs backgrounded + global pressure + 90 s; WebKit has no reclamation). Each close/re-create risks an avcC change, and mediabunny freezes the track config at the first packet. The latest-segment rule then silently shortens 'Clip it!' after every pause of 8 s or more. Keep the encoder alive through visible pauses. On iOS, close IMMEDIATELY on visibilitychange:hidden: the WebContent process is suspended within seconds, so an 8 s timer fires only after resume, against a possibly invalidated VideoToolbox session. Also exclude errors in the first few seconds after resume from the 4-failures-in-60-s disable counter.

Section 1 topology, one 'clips-engine' worker doing encoder callbacks, ring, mediabunny muxing and synchronous OPFS SyncAccessHandle I/O: I measured a 60 s packet-copy remux (1800 video + 2814 audio packets, 17.5 MB) at 14-31 ms on an M5 in Node. The event-loop gap equals the mux time, so the job never yields. On a phone, add sync writes of 20-46 MB and an fsync flush and the stall is likely 100s of ms. During that time encoder outputs and incoming frames queue, the main thread hits inFlight >= 2 and drops frames. That punches holes in the ring exactly during auto-highlight post-roll and when kids spam Clip. Split into an encode/ring worker and a mux/IO worker (copy the GOP ArrayBuffers across at clip time, ~10-20 ms for 22 MB), or yield to a macrotask every ~100 packets and flush in chunks. (The WASM AAC fallback already runs in its own blob worker, so it is not the blocker.)

Section 5 CaptureClock produces judder at 48/50/72/75/100/144/165 Hz (simulated, alternating 20/40 ms gaps at 50 Hz), which contradicts the spec's own claim. When the game hits vsync, use an integer vsync stride (fps = Hz/ceil(Hz/31)) and set the encoder framerate to match. Keep slot pacing only for irregular game cadences. Section 4's L1 rule ('24 fps where Hz divides by 24, else 20') should use the same stride logic, and L0 should be 25 fps at 50/75 Hz.

Section 2 tier table keys iPhone class off the Safari 'Version/' token. Chrome iOS (CriOS), Firefox iOS (FxiOS) and in-app WKWebViews (Instagram, TikTok, Discord, Snapchat, Google app) have no Version token, and iPadOS sends a Macintosh UA by default. Detect the engine by features instead: on iOS, `'AudioEncoder' in self` means WebKit 26+, which means A13+. Detect iPad as Macintosh UA with maxTouchPoints > 1.

Section 2/4 defaults hit a big share of real users. Apple's June 7, 2026 numbers: 79% of iPhones on iOS 26, 14% on iOS 18, 7% earlier. The 'Version 16.4-25.x: heavy T0' row therefore puts roughly one iPhone in five, including many A13-A18 phones that simply haven't updated, into 'no replay' for Monster Truck, four-wheeler and similar games. T0 'no ring' is not a memory decision (30 s at 1 Mbps is ~3.75 MB video + ~5.8 MB PCM). It is a performance decision the governor already makes adaptively. For 'no limitations', default replay ON everywhere and let calibration plus the governor step down. Keep static OFF only for the crash breaker and the known pre-existing retro-arcade iOS jetsam.

Section 4 governor: V1 (fps < 0.90 x baseline) with a baseline from 'the first 2 s of active play' confuses scene complexity with capture cost. The first 2 s is usually the lightest scene (spawn area or menu), so open-world games will fire V1 whenever the kid drives somewhere busy, then step down and go to RESTING for no capture-caused reason. Make capture-attributed signals primary: capture cost p95 against the frame budget, encoder queue and latency, and frames where frameWork < budget < frameWork + captureCost. On Chrome, add LoAF script attribution. Use fps-vs-baseline only as the SEVERE backstop.

RESTING UX promises 'Clip it still works on the ring it already has'. That clip ends when resting began, so it silently leaves out the play the kid just saw and tapped for, which reads as broken. Either label it honestly ('Your clip is from before replay rested') or keep a minimal capture running for the last 15 s instead of stopping completely.

Crash-loop breaker uses a single localStorage marker. With two tabs, a tab that loads while another tab is capturing and visible reads capturing:true/visible:true and records a false unclean exit. Three device-wide false exits then disable replay everywhere. Use Web Locks for liveness: each tab holds navigator.locks 'hh-clips-live-<sid>' for its lifetime, and on load a marker counts only if navigator.locks.query() shows its lock is gone. Web Locks are released when a tab dies.

Owner purge ('session user id change: purge') wipes the ring when a guest signs in via credentials (redirect:false). That is the same kid saving the run they just played, and storage-keys.ts already notes the guest-then-first-sign-in edge. Keep the ring on guest-to-user. Purge on user-to-other-user and user-to-guest. On pageshow persisted=true (bfcache Back after sign-out), compare the ring owner to the current session and purge on mismatch.

Section 7 Record cap (180 s / 46 MB) turns a SHARE-path limit (Chromium's 50 MiB) into a RECORDING limit, which contradicts the owner's 'no limitations'. OPFS fMP4 streaming already keeps RAM flat. Record longer, and at share time offer: trim; auto-split into parts of 48 MiB or less; a lower-bitrate transcode to fit; Download (no cap); or the hosted link.

Section 8 reconcile treats 'row with no file' as eviction. WebKit and Chromium evict whole origins (performEvictionForOrigin deletes allManagedTypes; ITP deletes IDB, OPFS and localStorage together), so after a real eviction there are no rows left to find. The local eviction notice can never fire; only the server hint cookie can detect it. Also, the device-learning keys, the crash marker and the install-nudge timers are wiped in the same sweep.

Section 7 journal ordering is unspecified. SyncAccessHandle.flush() of the media bytes must complete BEFORE the journal's lastGoodEnd is rewritten and flushed. Otherwise a crash can leave the journal pointing past bytes that never became durable, and recovery truncates to a corrupt tail.

Section 3 memory budget: 'a clip job adds <5 MB' holds only for packet-copy clips. The editor's trims at non-keyframes, title/end cards and portrait re-framing need decode plus re-encode. That means NV12 decoder output frames (~1.4 MB each at 720p) plus a SECOND hardware encoder and a hardware decoder while the live ring encoder is still running. On Android that is three concurrent MediaCodec sessions, which some SoCs cannot provide. Close or pause the live encoder while exporting (or export only outside gameplay) and budget the export memory explicitly.

'Save my last run' keeps the old ring in worker memory for 5 min while the kid starts another game. On an iPhone moving from one heavy game to another, that is two rings live at once. Persist the last run to OPFS tmp right away (with a 5-min TTL), or free it when the next session starts.

CSP interplay (next.config.ts): the main-site script-src has no blob:, so audioWorklet.addModule(blobURL) fails. clip-tap.worklet has to be a same-origin static file, also for the srcdoc iframe and the /emulator iframe. connect-src has no blob:, so there can be no fetch(objectURL) (UrlSource on blob URLs). media-src is 'self' blob:, which blocks playing bucket-hosted clips on site pages unless they are proxied same-origin or the CSP is extended. worker-src blob: is present, so the AAC encoder's blob worker works.

Audio timing: each AudioContext needs its own getOutputTimestamp anchors, and a context created inside the srcdoc or EmulatorJS iframe reports performanceTime against the iframe's timeOrigin. That needs the same offset as rAF. With several contexts (the game bus plus an iframe context), the worker has to mix streams whose clocks are mapped separately.

Section 8 persistence UX ignores in-app browsers. WKWebView hosts get the smaller 'other apps' quota (15% origin / 20% overall per WebKit's storage policy), may use non-persistent data stores, and lack the Version token. A kid who opens a shared hankshits.com link inside Discord, Instagram or Snapchat and records there can lose everything. Detect this and nudge 'Open in Safari/Chrome to keep your clips' before the first save.

T0 fallback 'MediaRecorder with a DOM compositor' assumes MP4 output. Chrome and Safari produce MP4, but Firefox MediaRecorder MP4 support is unverified (Firefox Android has no WebCodecs at all). Gate on MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported('video/mp4;codecs=avc1'), and give WebM output a separate share path (the 'video/mp4' file-share contract does not apply to it).
missedIssues: WebKit per-frame readback: every 2D/OffscreenCanvas/ImageBitmap VideoFrame in WebKit is a synchronous getPixelBuffer readback. This is the single biggest unknown for iPhone performance, and the track's cost numbers are Chrome-only (WebCodecsVideoFrame.cpp, HTMLCanvasElement.cpp FIXME).

Retro-arcade already jetsams on iPhone (EmulatorJS #1143, iOS 26.1-26.6, EmulatorJS 4.2.3), with no recording involved. The repo loads the unpinned cdn.emulatorjs.org/stable channel (public/emulator/index.html:169,239), so any soak-test verdict can go stale without notice. Under the PR-scope rule this is a pre-existing defect: file it with that evidence (or fix it: pin the version, test the INITIAL_HEAP / no-memory-growth builds). Do not blame it on clips.

Enforce 'never screen capture' at the platform level: next.config.ts already sets Permissions-Policy camera=(), microphone=(). Add display-capture=() and a test that asserts the header, so the no-mic/camera/screen constraint cannot regress.

The Chrome encoder cold start happens on every browser process start, not just fresh profiles (10.5-17 s measured, reused profile). Android and ChromeOS behaviour is still unmeasured and needs a device run before the mobile watchdog timings (30 s wait) are fixed.

Safari can grant persist() to tab origins through the private _persistedSites SPI (iOS 18.2+). A real-device test of navigator.storage.persist() in a Safari tab, in a Home Screen app and in iOS 26 'Open as Web App' should decide the nag copy instead of an assumption.
WebKit added (May 2026) a 180-day wall-clock storage eviction that applies when the user turns tracking prevention OFF. Clip storage is not durable in that configuration either.

There is no Web-Locks-based liveness anywhere in the design (crash marker, tmp-file cleanup, recovery ownership). The multi-tab false positives and the 'tmp older than 1 h deleted' race with a live writer in another tab both need lock checks.

Editor exports that need re-encoding compete for hardware codec sessions with the always-on ring encoder. On Android that can trip Chromium's global-pressure reclamation of a backgrounded tab's codecs, or MediaCodec instance limits. It is not budgeted anywhere.

The first 2 s baseline, WARMING calibration and the cold-start bridge all happen at session start, so the start of every run (often the moment kids want to clip, e.g. a crazy first jump) is not in the ring. Consider starting buffering immediately on the software bridge and sampling the baseline from game frames that the encoder is not blocking.
In-app browsers and non-Safari iOS browsers (CriOS/FxiOS) are absent from the tier, persistence and nudge logic entirely.
Integer-stride capture cadence and the matching encoder framerate hint for 50/75/100/144/165 Hz displays (Chromebooks, gaming monitors, 90/120/144 Hz Android) are missing.
verify.summary:
Most of the track's research holds up against fresh primary sources, but the design has one big blind spot and about a dozen fixable defects.

**What held up:**
- **Storage and ITP (WebKit main):** the quota numbers are right. ITP's 7-day sweep does include OPFS (FileSystem), and Home Screen apps are exempt.
- **Compat data (fresh MDN BCD):** the OPFS and AudioContext support versions check out.
- **Chromium share limit:** 50 MiB for `video/mp4` / `.mp4` on Android and desktop.
- **mediabunny options:** confirmed. mediabunny also freezes a track's decoder config at the first packet, so the configKey segment split is genuinely required.
- **Repo sign-out and PWA claims:** confirmed.

**The encoder cold start is real, and wider than reported.** I launched Chrome 153 directly (no Playwright flags) and the first hardware encoder took 10.5-17 s. It happens on every browser launch, even with a reused profile and after 30 s idle. It's Chrome's pipeline, not VideoToolbox, which encodes its first frame in 0.3-0.4 s through ffmpeg.
- A pre-warm only helps if it starts 10-17 s before a game needs the encoder.
- The software bridge works: started 2.5 s into the stall, it produced output about 90 ms later.

**Corrections to the track's findings:**
- `persist()` is also granted through a Safari-only private list of "persisted sites" (iOS 18.2+). The track's "7×24h" figure is the check interval of a new 180-day eviction that only runs when tracking prevention is off.
- Codec reclamation: Chromium only reclaims hidden hardware codecs under global pressure after 90 s, and WebKit never reclaims. So closing a paused, visible encoder after 8 s buys nothing and risks shortened clips.
- The captureStream "needs an attached canvas" bug (240380) was fixed in 2022 (Safari 16).
- EmulatorJS #1220 was closed as a duplicate of #1143. That thread shows retro-arcade jetsams on iOS 26.1-26.6 with EmulatorJS 4.2.3, the version the repo loads from an unpinned CDN channel. This is a pre-existing crash that has nothing to do with recording.
- The frozen iOS version in Safari's user agent has moved to 18_7. Chrome and Firefox on iOS, and in-app browsers, send no `Version/` token at all.

**Biggest miss: the iPhone capture path.** In WebKit, a VideoFrame made from an OffscreenCanvas, ImageBitmap, or 2D canvas is a synchronous full pixel readback on every captured frame. Only a WebGL `<canvas>` gets a GPU-only copy, and WebKit has no GPU route for compositing a HUD over the game. The spec's "OffscreenCanvas compositor" choice lands on the slow path, and every cost number in the track comes from Chrome on desktop. This has to be benchmarked on a real iPhone before any defaults ship.

**Measured or simulated design defects:**
- **Single worker:** a 60 s remux runs 14-31 ms with no break on an M5, before the synchronous OPFS writes. On a phone that drops frames from the replay buffer while a clip is being saved, exactly during auto-highlight post-roll. Split encoding and saving into two workers.
- **Frame pacing:** the CaptureClock judders at 48/50/72/75/100/144/165 Hz (20/40 ms alternating gaps at 50 Hz). Capturing every Nth screen refresh fixes it.

**Other design problems:**
- **Device tiers:** the table keys off the Safari `Version/` token, which fails for Chrome and Firefox on iOS, in-app browsers, and iPads. On Apple's June 2026 numbers (79% of iPhones on iOS 26, 14% iOS 18, 7% earlier), about one iPhone in five gets no replay on heavy games.
- **Governor:** its baseline comes from the first, easiest 2 s of play, so busy scenes will trip it for reasons that aren't recording.
- **Resting mode:** "Clip it" there silently misses the play the kid just saw.
- **Crash detector:** a single marker gives false crash reports with two tabs open; Web Locks fix this.
- **Guest sign-in:** purging on sign-in destroys the run a guest just played.
- **Record cap:** 180 s turns a sharing limit into a recording limit.
- **Missed eviction:** the reconcile step can never detect eviction, because browsers wipe the whole site's storage at once.
- **CSP:** the audio tap module has to be a same-origin file, and hosted-clip playback is blocked unless proxied.
- **Editor codecs:** exports that re-encode compete for hardware encoders with the always-on replay encoder.

All of these are fixable. The fixes are in the design problems list.

findings.claim: Steam offers three recording modes (Off, Record in Background, Record on Demand). Background recordings are temporary, overwritten when the disk budget fills, and only become permanent when the player makes a Clip. The Clip button drops an adjustable clip suggestion on a timeline (drag the end points, or use Start/End Clip buttons). Save/Share offers: Save in Steam, Export Video File (mp4), Copy to Clipboard, Send to Other Device (auto-downloads within 2 days), and Create a Share Link that Steam hosts and that expires after 2 days. The store page also lists 'Send an MP4 via the Steam Mobile App or a QR code'. Player markers drop with Ctrl+F12; achievements and screenshots auto-create markers.

Games emit markers with AddTimelineEvent(icon, title, description, priority, startOffset, duration, clipPriority). ClipPriority Featured makes Steam add a pre/post buffer around the event and pre-select it as an auto clip suggestion; Standard is a marker only. SetTimelineGameMode(Playing/Staging/Menus/LoadingScreen) shades the timeline bar by game state. This is the model for a shared markMoment() API with featured vs standard priority and for dimming menu/paused spans in the filmstrip.

Press the Capture button = screenshot; press and hold = save up to the last 30 seconds. Trim happens later in the Album ('Clip Video': slide the left marker, press A, slide the right marker, Save), the edit is saved as a NEW video (non-destructive), and 'Save as Screenshot' pulls a still from a video. Transfer to a phone is via 'Send to Smartphone' with a QR code (up to 10 screenshots or 1 video). The Nintendo Switch app states users under 13 cannot share screenshots or videos.

Xbox: press the Share button for a screenshot, hold it (or Guide + X) to 'Record what happened', default 30 s, configurable to 15/30/45/60 s. On Windows, background recording ('Record what happened') is a Game Bar setting. Xbox Support explicitly warns that on-screen notifications may get captured and says to review captures before sharing.

The Create button opens a create menu: Save Recent Gameplay (last 15 s up to 1 h, continuously buffered), Start New Recording (up to 1 h), Take Screenshot. The button can be remapped to 'Easy Screenshots' or 'Easy Video Clips'. PS5 auto-captures trophy screenshots and trophy videos (configurable duration), which is console precedent for auto-clips on achievements.

findings.topic: Auto-highlights on game events (Medal, NVIDIA, PostParty)
findings.claim: Medal: default clip key F8 saves the last 15 s to 10 min; auto-clipping saves the seconds around a game event without the player pressing anything, and each clip is named after the event and waits in the library under an Auto Clips filter until the player chooses to share ('When the match ends, the highlights are already in your library'). NVIDIA Highlights (now a legacy SDK) groups game-defined highlights and opens a summary at a natural break ('Show highlights summary after game win'). Rocket League's Postparty integration prompts the player to capture during the Goal Replay (dead time, not live play), saves the last 30 s, trims to a 3-second minimum, and awards a player title for the first share.

Rocket League .replay files are data, not video, and cannot be converted to video directly; they are re-simulated in a replay viewer with camera modes and an AI 'Director Mode'. Fortnite's replay system re-simulates matches with many camera modes. Brawl Stars keeps a Battle Log of the 25 latest games with replays that can be shared into Club Chat; players who want video outside the game screen-record (r/ClashRoyale). This supports rendering our 8 DOM games from a state log into video, and a 'recent games' list that can be turned into a clip at any time for almost no storage.

Roblox Moments lets a player capture a screenshot or a 30-second clip with an in-experience capture icon (a small indicator shows while recording), then trim, add music from a licensed catalog, add a description, and post (10 uploads/day). Every published video is auto-moderated and reportable. To protect identity, usernames above avatars and in-experience UI are removed from captures, and player voices are muted. Viewers react with emoji and tap 'Join' to jump into the game (the growth loop). Launched 13+ only (Sept 2025); on 2026-07-28 Baszucki announced its own tab and restricted it to age-checked 16+. Roblox users recorded 240M+ videos in July-Aug 2025.

findings.topic: Prior art on public sharing by age (contrast with the settled open-sharing policy)
findings.claim: Every major platform found restricts public posting of captures by young kids: Nintendo Switch app bars under-13 sharing; Xbox child defaults block sharing outside Xbox; Roblox Moments is 13+ then age-checked 16+; YouTube supervised experience disables uploads. Jack settled OPEN SHARING FOR EVERYONE on 2026-09-27; this spec does not reopen that. It compensates in the UX: clips are PII-free by construction (game canvas plus game audio only, no free text anywhere, pseudonymous handle or no name), links are unlisted and deletable, a one-tap self-check runs before a link is made, and every link page has Report.

Apple's own rolling-clip API (ReplayKit, iOS 15) keeps only 15 s of samples, lets apps export on a UI button or game-controller press, and explicitly encourages apps to export clips automatically on their own triggers. That matches a 'Clip it' button plus auto-highlights; our 60 s ring and 30 s default go beyond it.

Wordle's share button (added 2021-12-16) produces a spoiler-free emoji grid, an idea a player (@irihapeta) invented and Wardle adopted. Wardle says most sharing happens in group chats with friends and family, not in public feeds. Players were confused by clipboard-only sharing ('it's on a clip board. I have no idea where that is'). The grid's 'mystery squares' drove curiosity. So: one tap that does something visible, a mystery (letters hidden) style for Wordle clips, and assume the audience is a group chat.

Vertical 9:16 is the native short-form shape. YouTube counts square or vertical videos up to 3 minutes as Shorts (since 2024-10-15), and Reels allow 3 minutes. Hook viewers in the first seconds. Platform UI covers the top ~110-250 px and the bottom ~320-480 px of a 1080x1920 frame, plus ~120 px on the right; Meta says keep key text off all edges and, with disclaimers, leave the bottom 40% clear. So put score and branding inside the center safe zone, never add a pre-roll title card that delays the action, and put branding in an end card.

In Feb 2021 Instagram said it makes Reels 'visibly recycled from other apps (i.e. contains logos or watermarks)' less discoverable. It later said a creator's own logo is fine. So a big bouncing TikTok-style watermark can hurt a kid's clip on other platforms. Use a small, static corner bug plus a 1.5 s end card with 'Play free at hankshits.com'.

NN/g recommends touch targets of at least 2 cm x 2 cm for young children (4x the adult 1 cm). Dragging with a mouse or trackpad is hard for under-9s. Offer tap alternatives for every drag, because kids rarely discover hidden alternate interactions (none found PBS Kids' click-to-place). State the goal and next step clearly and literally. NN/g also saw audio instructions fail because the browser blocked sound. So the trim editor needs big handles plus 'Start here / End here' buttons plus length chips, every drag needs a tap path, and read-aloud must be tap-triggered.

On prod at a 390 px viewport (Playwright Chrome, guest, 2026-09-27), the header title already truncates: Flappy Bird's title gets 86 px of the 113 px it needs, and Bomberman's (which also shows a pause button) gets 38 px of 118 px. Adding one 44 px clip button plus its 4 px gap leaves the Flappy title 38 px and the Bomberman title 0 px. So the clip control needs a header width-budget rule. Note: the Playwright browser appears to be shared with a concurrent agent (an /games/asteroids navigation landed on /games/bomberman), so the Bomberman number is a pause-button game, not Asteroids.

For canPause games, PauseMenu already renders Leaderboard (children slot) and Restart. The header copies are duplicates, so hiding them in the header on narrow screens loses no function. 11 games plus 7 apps pass canPause={false} and have no pause menu. Those keep header Restart and Leaderboard and need the long-press capture menu or toast for the advanced capture actions.
sources: grep canPause={false} in apps/web/src (endless-runner, four-wheeler-3d, wordle, hill-climb, math-attack, dino-runner, monster-truck, flappy-bird, cookie-clicker, four-wheeler-adventure, retro-arcade + 7 apps)

findings.claim: Letter keys are game input: Wordle types every letter, and four-wheeler-3d binds C (camera), E, F, P, M, I, X. F-keys are unreliable: the Chromebook top row sends browser actions, and Mac laptop F-keys are media keys without fn. Google's Chromebook shortcut list reserves Alt+[ ] = - 1-9 d Space Backspace arrows plus Shift+Alt combos, but not Alt+C or Alt+R. Firefox's Alt menu accelerators are F/E/V/S/B/T/H. So use Alt+C (Option+C on Mac, matched by event.code 'KeyC' + altKey) for Clip it and Alt+R for Record, with F8 (Medal's default) as a PC alias. Every handler goes through keyBelongsToTarget().

The W3C Standard Gamepad mapping has buttons 0-16 and no Share or Capture button. Index 8 is the 'left button in center cluster' (Xbox View, PS Create, Switch Minus) and 16 is the center Home/Guide/PS button. Xbox's Share button is not exposed through XInput (RetroArch needs DInput to map it). No Hank's Hits game reads gamepads except retro-arcade's EmulatorJS iframe, where button 8 is the console's Select. So: hold button 8 for 1 s = Clip it in every game except retro-arcade.

On iPhone the only in-browser route into the Photos camera roll is the share sheet action 'Save Video', which the kid must tap. An a[download] lands in Files > Downloads. navigator.share must get files only, with exact type 'video/mp4' and a '.mp4' name, and must run synchronously in a fresh tap. Some users report 'Save video' silently doing nothing. Whether Safari shows a Photos permission prompt the first time is unverified, so the coaching includes a conditional 'If your iPhone asks, tap Allow'.

Chromium caps Web Share at 10 files / 50 MB on desktop and Android. iMessage rich previews autoplay an og:video that points directly at an MP4 only when page + image + video total 10 MB or less (TN3156), and og:image should be at least 900 px wide. So the link copy must be auto-sized to about 9 MB or less, and a local file over 50 MB needs an automatic 'smaller copy' before Share on Chromium.

WCAG 2.2.2 requires a pause/stop control for auto-starting moving content lasting more than 5 s, so the looping editor preview and the hosted page video need a visible pause. Flashes must stay under the 2.3.1 threshold, so there is no full-screen 'shutter flash' on save.

findings.topic: House style constraints for new clip UI
findings.claim: The house font is Nunito (layout.tsx), and the theme is primary blue-600 / secondary green-600 / accent orange-500 (globals.css). Modals use slate-900 surfaces with border-slate-700 (LeaderboardModal.tsx:63). Toasts go in a pointer-events-none lane at fixed top-14 z-[1100] with one ≥44 px button (AchievementCelebrations.tsx:73-113). The z-stack is header z-1000 < toast z-1100 < LeaderboardModal z-1500 < PauseMenu z-2000. Every menu surface has a ReadAloudButton whose text names every visible button (PauseMenu spokenExtras). Bottom sheets must hide while a start card is up (startOverlayPresence). Pre-existing AI-slop tells are present and must NOT be copied into clip UI: gradient-clip text headings (Header.tsx h1, HomeClient hero), the blue-to-purple page background (TrophiesPage.tsx), and the yellow-to-orange toast gradient.

findings.topic: Pre-existing defects found while reading (for filing, not in clip scope)
findings.claim: (1) IOSInstallPrompt's close button is w-8 h-8 (32 px), below the repo's 44 px kid-target rule (IOSInstallPrompt.tsx:58). (2) The GameShell title is already unreadable on 390 px phones for pause-button games (38 px for 118 px), independent of clips. (3) The slop tells above. The clip work fixes (2) as part of the width budget. (1) is a one-line fix to fold in. (3) should be filed with file:line evidence.

findings.topic: Brag moments already present per game
findings.claim: The feasibility study's per-game bragMoments already name featured triggers for all 26 games. Examples: flappy isNewHighScore computed before the write (store.ts:228), platformer best time (store.ts:586-592), breakout final-level clear, chess/checkers/quoridor recordWin, 2048 tile 2048, wordle 1-3 guess solve, monster-truck flips and big-air (no high score), four-wheeler-3d race win, cookie-clicker golden cookie frenzy. retro-arcade has none (manual only). These map one-to-one onto markMoment({priority:'featured'|'standard'}).

The achievements engine already detects per-app personal bests (BEST_ALIASES) from a 1 s poll and queues celebration toasts (useAuthSync.ts:418-437, achievements/store.ts:52-96). The global catalog has cross-game trophies ('Record Breaker!'). Clip trophies ('Director!', 'Film Crew!') slot into the same global catalog and toast queue, with no new celebration system.

research.designSpec:
HANK'S HITS CLIPS: UX SPEC (track: 10/10 kid clip experience)
Scope: every game under apps/web/src/games/* (26 today, plus every kid-built game later). Settled constraints are fixed inputs: open sharing for everyone with no grown-up gate, canvas + game audio only, no real names (at most the auto handle), no paid services, one game = one island.

=====================================================================
0. PRINCIPLES (each traced to prior art)
=====================================================================
P1 One tap, instant, no menu. This follows Switch hold-to-save, Xbox 'Record what happened', PS5 'Save Recent Gameplay', and Medal F8. Tapping the clip button SAVES the last N seconds right away. Editing and sharing come later, and are optional.
P2 Never interrupt play. Auto-highlights save silently. Any prompt waits for a natural break: run end, result screen, or pause. Precedent: Postparty's prompt during the goal replay, NVIDIA's summary after a win, and Medal's 'already in your library when the match ends'.
P3 Suggest, don't decide. The editor opens with a suggested trim (Steam's 'clip suggestion') that the kid can widen in one tap ('All').
P4 Every drag has a tap twin (NN/g). Targets are ≥44 px everywhere, and ≥2 cm (64 CSS px on phones) for the trim handles and the primary Share action.
P5 Two taps to share, with the file always prepared first. The Web Share activation rule forces this. The UX hides it by pre-rendering in the background.
P6 Local first. The clip lives on the device. A link is an explicit extra step with an honest one-line disclosure ('Anyone with the link can watch'). This keeps server cost at storage-only and keeps COPPA exposure minimal.
P7 PII-free by construction. There is no free-text field anywhere in the clip flow. The only name option is the pseudonymous handle or 'No name'. The compositor never rasterizes DOM (the Oregon Trail name inputs, the header avatar).
P8 Every game gets the button automatically. A new kid-built game shows the clip button with zero code. Brag markers are an easy opt-in.

=====================================================================
1. SURFACE MAP (entry points -> destinations)
=====================================================================
In-game:
- Header clip button (GameShell right cluster, first item). Tap = Clip it. Long-press (≥500 ms) or right-click = Capture menu.
- Keyboard Alt+C (Option+C on Mac) = Clip it. Alt+R = start/stop Record. F8 = alias for Clip it. Gamepad: hold button 8 for 1 s = Clip it (not in retro-arcade).
- Toast lane (shared with trophies): 'Clip saved! [Watch]', the auto-highlight chip, and errors.
- Pause menu (canPause games): one new full-width button '🎬 Clips', which opens the Capture menu. Add 'Clips' to spokenExtras.

=====================================================================
2. THE CAPTURE CONTROL (header)
=====================================================================
2.1 Render rule: the button renders ONLY when a clip source is registered and the device can capture. This matches ReadAloudButton, which renders nothing when unsupported, so a kid never sees a dead button. Capability detection uses the useSyncExternalStore 'mounted' pattern (useFullscreen.ts:69-85) so there is no hydration mismatch. Apps under GameShell (weather, jokes) do not register a source, so they show no button.
2.2 Position: the first child of the right cluster, before Leaderboard. That puts it closest to the center, away from the account control, and one slot from Restart (Restart's own confirmation dialog absorbs mis-taps). Never insert before the title: four-wheeler-3d styles `.fw-shell-header > div:nth-child(2)`.
2.3 Width budget. Measured on prod at 390 px: the title already truncates (38 px for 118 px on pause games). Apply these steps in order, stopping when everything fits. It is computed in JS from which controls are present (every control is 44 px, and the guest 'Sign In' is 92 px), so nothing is measured at runtime:
  step 1 (viewport < 480): cluster gap 4 px -> 0 (hit areas stay 44 px; the ~24 px glyphs give the visual spacing).
  step 2 (viewport < 480): the title text becomes the game's metadata emoji (28 px). The full name moves to the element's sr-only text / aria-label. The full name stays on the start card and the pause menu.
  step 3 (viewport < 400 AND canPause): hide the header Leaderboard and Restart. Both already exist in PauseMenu.
  step 4 (still over budget): LoginButton drops its label (showLabelOnMobile=false -> 44 px icon).
  Worst cases after the rule, guest, browser tab (not PWA):
   - canPause game at 360: 24 pad + 🏠44 + emoji 28 + [🎬 ⛶ ⏸ SignIn92] 224 = 320 ✓ (steps 1-3)
   - canPause=false game at 375: 24 + 44 + 28 + [🎬 🏆 ⛶ ↻ SignIn92] 268 = 364 ✓ (steps 1-2)
   - canPause=false game at 360: step 4 applies -> 316 ✓
  In a PWA (standalone) the fullscreen slot is already hidden (FullscreenButton.tsx:37), which frees 44 px. Landscape phones (≥ 667 px) get the full title and all controls.
2.4 Glyph: an inline SVG clapperboard in the same 2 px stroke style as the fullscreen icon (FullscreenButton.tsx:83-89). It is SVG, not emoji, because the states in 2.5 overlay a ring, dot, check or badge on the glyph, and emoji render differently per OS. In copy and buttons elsewhere, 🎬 is the clip emoji (house voice).
2.5 States (the button stays 44x44 in every state). Each row gives visual / aria-label / behavior:
  unavailable  | not rendered | n/a
  warming (<3 s of gameplay in the ring, or only menu frames) | glyph at 60% opacity | 'Save a clip (play a little first)' | tap -> hint toast 'Play a little first! Then tap 🎬 again.'
  ready (the ring is filling) | white glyph + a thin static orange ring (#f97316), never animated | 'Save a clip of the last 30 seconds' | tap -> saving
  saving (mux, or a replay render for DOM games) | the glyph becomes a determinate progress ring | 'Saving your clip' | extra taps are ignored; typically <1 s for canvas games, 1-4 s for replay games (toast 'Making your clip…')
  saved | ✓ check scales in (150 ms) for 1.2 s, then back to ready | 'Clip saved' (a live region announces it) | the toast shows
  recording (Record mode) | red #dc2626 rounded square with a white stop square. A non-interactive timer pill '● 0:42' (tabular-nums) sits just under the header at the left of the toast lane | 'Stop recording, 42 seconds' | tap -> stop + save
  resting (auto perf guard, or the setting is off) | glyph with a diagonal slash, 60% opacity | 'Clip camera is off. Tap for options' | tap -> Capture menu, with 'Turn clip camera on' first
  paused (tab hidden, pause menu open, editor open, start card up) | the ring is hidden (nothing is being kept) | unchanged label | tap still works on the pre-pause footage
  error | glyph + a small amber '!' badge for 3 s | 'Clip didn't save' | toast with the kid-word reason (section 12)
2.6 Feedback on save: the button-local check + the toast + a soft click sound. The sound plays through a UI-only audio node, NEVER through the capture bus, so it never lands in the next clip. On Android, navigator.vibrate(20). There is no full-screen flash (WCAG 2.3.1).
2.7 Desktop tooltip (native title plus a styled tooltip on hover/focus): 'Clip it! Saves the last 30 seconds (Alt+C)'. It uses aria-keyshortcuts='Alt+C'.
2.8 Gamepad: hold button 8 (Xbox View / PS Create / Switch Minus) for 1 s. The standard mapping has no Share button. Disabled in retro-arcade, where 8 is the console's Select. Shown only after a gamepadconnected event, as a one-time toast: '🎮 Hold the little ⧉ button to save a clip!'.
2.9 Escape: while the editor or Capture menu is open, GameShell passes suppressEscape (same mechanism as the restart dialog), so Esc closes the sheet and does not toggle pause.

=====================================================================
3. CAPTURE MODES AND CLIP UNITS
=====================================================================
3.1 Clip it (instant replay). The ring always holds 60 s. Clip it saves the last 30 s by default. The setting offers 15 / 30 / 60 s, following Xbox's 15/30/45/60 and Medal's 15 s+.
3.2 Auto-highlights. A game emits markMoment({kind, label, emoji, priority:'featured'|'standard', preSec?, postSec?}), modeled on Steam AddTimelineEvent. Featured events become an auto clip covering 8 s before to 3 s after (defaults). A standard event is a ⭐ marker on the filmstrip only. The zero-code fallback is the achievements personal-best poll (1 s latency, which the ring absorbs), so every game gets at least a 'new best' highlight with no edits.
3.3 Record (long video). Start from the Capture menu, Alt+R, or the pause menu. It runs until the kid stops it, or until the device is nearly out of space. There is no arbitrary cap (data-integrity rule). At about 2 minutes of space left: toast 'Almost out of space! Your video will stop soon.' It pauses when the game pauses or the tab hides, and resumes seamlessly. It stops and saves on route change.
3.4 Photo. Capture menu '📸 Take a photo' grabs the current composited frame as a PNG. The editor also has '📸 Save a photo' from any frame (Switch 'Save as Screenshot'). Photos live in My Clips with a 📸 badge.
3.5 Clip unit per game type (the kid-facing label changes, the flow does not):
  Real-time canvas / R3F / iframe (arkanoid, asteroids, blitz-bomber, bomberman, breakout, dino-runner, endless-runner, flappy-bird, hextris, hill-climb, math-attack, oregon-trail, platformer, space-invaders, monster-truck, four-wheeler-3d, four-wheeler-adventure, retro-arcade): time-based, 'the last 30 seconds'.
  Real-time DOM replay (snake, cookie-clicker): time-based, rendered from the state log. Toast: 'Making your clip…'. Cookie-clicker gets speed chips (2x / 4x) so number-go-up reads well.
  Turn-based DOM replay (chess, checkers, quoridor, memory-match, 2048, wordle): move-based. Clip it = 'your last 10 moves' (about 0.8 s per move plus capture animations). The editor offers 'Last 10 moves / Whole game (sped up to fit 60 s)'. Wordle: the whole puzzle with row reveals, plus a Style toggle 'Show letters / Mystery tiles' (Wordle-grid mystery). Because the log is tiny, the library keeps 'Recent games' (the last 10 per game) that can become a clip at any time (Supercell battle-log precedent).
3.6 Shape, 'Auto' default: Tall 9:16 (720x1280) when the game's surface aspect is < 1.2, and Wide 16:9 (1280x720) otherwise.
  Tall: arkanoid, asteroids, bomberman, breakout, flappy, hextris, math-attack, space-invaders, snake, all board/tile games, cookie-clicker.
  Wide: dino, endless, hill-climb, platformer, blitz-bomber, monster-truck, both four-wheelers, retro-arcade (4:3 pillarboxed), oregon-trail.
  The kid can switch in the editor (it re-renders with progress; see 5.6).
3.7 Composition inside the frame (compositor spec for the architecture track). All text sits inside the universal safe zone: ≥10% from the top, ≥20% from the bottom, ≥11% from the right, ≥6% from the left.
  Tall: top band (game emoji + name + live score, tabular-nums, painted from store state) | game area centered | a thin line under the game ('hankshits.com', 60% white). The lowest 20% is a plain brand-color field. No pre-roll title card: the action starts at frame 0 (first-second hook).
  Wide: game full-bleed, a small score chip top-left, a small 'hankshits.com' bug bottom-right.
  The name/handle is NEVER in the live frames. It appears only on the end card, so changing it is instant and a live capture can never leak it.
  End card (1.5 s, on by default): solid deep slate (#0f172a), large game emoji, game name, final score, a 'NEW BEST!' badge when earned, handle or nothing, the optional sticker, and 'Play free at hankshits.com'.

=====================================================================
4. TOASTS, PROMPTS, AND ANTI-NAG RULES
=====================================================================
4.1 One shared ToastLane (upgrade AchievementCelebrations into a shared queue). fixed top-14, z-[1100], pointer-events-none except its buttons, one toast visible at a time. Priority: error > trophy > clip-saved > highlight-chip > hints. Each shows for 4 s, and the queue collapses a burst the way the SUMMARY_THRESHOLD rule does. The toast surface is solid slate-900/95 + ring-1 white/15, with no gradient or glow.
4.2 Clip saved toast: [poster 56x56 with a '0:30' chip] 'Clip saved! 🎬' / 'The last 30 seconds.' [Watch] (≥44 px, btn-primary). role=status, aria-live=polite. Tapping Watch opens the editor. canPause games pause first. canPause=false games keep running under the modal sheet; input is blocked and the ring is paused.
4.3 Merge rule: if a trophy toast and a highlight fire within 2 s of the same moment (e.g. 'Record Breaker!' plus the new-best clip), show ONE trophy toast with two buttons, [Yay!] [🎬 Watch]. Never two stacked toasts.
4.4 Auto-highlight chip (shown only at run end, result screen, or pause, never mid-play): '🎬 We saved your new best! [Watch]'. If a run had several: '🎬 We saved 3 big moments! [Watch]', which opens the library filtered to Auto + this game.
4.5 Anti-nag caps:
  (a) At most 1 highlight chip per run, and at most 1 per 3 minutes per session.
  (b) If the kid tapped Clip it on a window that covers the event, no separate auto clip is saved (dedupe).
  (c) After 3 consecutive chips without a Watch tap, chips stop for that game for 7 days. Auto-saving continues silently into the Auto filter.
  (d) The setting 'Save my big moments by myself' turns both off.
  (e) Chips never appear while a start card, pause menu, or modal is up (startOverlayPresence).
4.6 Auto clip housekeeping: auto clips clean up after 7 days unless kept (⭐ Keep). The library says so ('Auto clips clean up after a week. Tap ⭐ Keep to keep one.') and shows 'Cleaned up 3 old auto clips' after a sweep. Nothing disappears silently. Manual clips, Record videos and photos stay until the kid deletes them.

=====================================================================
5. EDITOR SHEET
=====================================================================
5.1 Container: full-screen sheet on phones (100dvh, safe-area padding) and a centered dialog on desktop (max-w-5xl, two columns). z-[2100], above PauseMenu (z-2000). role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby 'Your clip'. Focus goes to the preview Play/Pause, is trapped, and returns to the invoker on close. Motion: open 250 ms / close 150 ms with cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), and no bounce on close. With reduced motion: opacity only.
5.2 Top bar: [✕ Close] 'Your clip' [🔊 Read it to me].
5.3 Preview: plays with sound, because the Watch tap is a gesture. It loops, and a big ▶/❚❚ control is always visible (WCAG 2.2.2). With reduced motion it does not autoplay (poster + ▶). A visually hidden description reads 'Monster Truck clip, 15 seconds, 12,400 points'.
5.4 Three big tabs under the preview, one panel at a time (reduces load). Default is Trim:
  [✂️ Trim] [🎨 Style] [🎵 Sound]
  TRIM
  - Filmstrip 64 px tall, 1 thumbnail per second.
  - Menu/paused spans are dimmed with a 'menu' tag (Steam game-mode shading).
  - ⭐ markers sit above the strip (28 px glyph, 44 px hit area). Tapping a marker centers the window with the moment at 70%.
  - Two handles: visual 20x64 px orange bar with a grip; touch area 48x72 px extending outward; desktop 16x56 px with a 44 px hit area.
  - Handles snap to 1-second steps. This matches the 1 s keyframes, so trimming is an instant remux. Minimum length 3 s (Postparty); a violation shows 'Clips need at least 3 seconds.'
  - Handles are role=slider with aria-valuetext 'Clip starts at 0:12'. Arrow keys move ±1 s, PageUp/PageDown ±5 s.
  - Tap twins: [Start here] [▶ from start] [End here] act at the playhead. Length chips: (5s) (10s) (15s) (30s) (All).
  - Default suggestion on open: 15 s with the newest featured marker at 70%. With no marker, the last 15 s. A hint line reads 'We picked the best 15 seconds. Tap All to use everything.'
  STYLE
  - Shape: [📱 Tall] [🖥️ Wide] (Auto preselected).
  - End card: on/off.
  - Name on clip: (TurboRacer42) (No name). The default mirrors the leaderboard choice: the handle if showOnLeaderboards, else No name. Guests see only 'No name', with the note 'Sign in to get a player name'. Never users.name or email.
  - Sticker (end card only, preset, no free text): none / 🔥 WOW! / ⭐ NEW BEST! / 😂 LOL / 🏆 GG / 🤯 NO WAY / 👑 CHAMP.
  - Speed: (1x) (Fast 2x) (Slow-mo).
  - Wordle only: Show letters / Mystery tiles.
  - [📸 Save a photo] (current frame).
  SOUND
  - Game sounds on/off.
  - Music: None / Arcade / Chill / Hype. These are in-house loops synthesized with the same Web Audio approach the games use, so they are licensing-free by construction. When music is on, game sounds duck to 50%.
  - Note at non-1x speed: 'Sounds get silly in slow-mo!' (pitch-shifted audio, not muted).
5.5 Actions footer (pinned):
  primary: [Share my clip] (56 px, btn-primary; on desktop the primary is [⬇ Save to computer])
  secondary row: [🔗 Make a link] [🗑 Delete]
  The iOS coaching line sits directly above the primary (see 6.3).
5.6 Instant vs re-render (UX contract for the architecture track):
  INSTANT: trim, end card on/off, name, sticker, music, game sounds, speed, photo grab. These are keyframe remux, concatenation of a pre-encoded end-card segment, and an audio-only re-encode.
  RE-RENDER with progress: shape change for canvas games. It shows 'Changing the shape… 40%' over the preview, and the kid can keep editing.
  DOM replay games: every edit is a re-render from the log, which is cheap and shows the same progress UI.
5.7 Non-destructive: the source clip + an edit recipe are stored, and the final MP4 is produced on demand. 'Reset' in the Trim tab restores the original. There is no double storage.
5.8 Keyboard in the editor: Space play/pause, ←/→ ±1 s playhead, [ and ] set start/end, Enter = primary action, Esc = close.

=====================================================================
6. SHARE STEP
=====================================================================
6.1 Two-tap mechanics hidden by pre-render. Whenever the editor settles (1 s after the last change), render the final file in the background. When the kid taps Share:
  if the File is ready -> navigator.share({files:[new File([blob], '<game>-clip.mp4', {type:'video/mp4'})]}) synchronously. Files only, no title/text on iOS.
  if not ready -> the button becomes 'Getting it ready… 70%' (disabled, determinate). When done it becomes 'Share it! ▶' with a single 150 ms scale pulse (no pulse with reduced motion). The kid taps again, which is a fresh activation.
  Pause the game before the share sheet opens. Windows Chrome drops fullscreen on share.
6.2 Platform decision table:
  iOS/iPadOS Safari + home-screen PWA: primary Share (share sheet). Coaching for 'Save Video'. Secondary: Make a link. No download button (it lands in Files and confuses kids).
  Android Chrome / Samsung: primary Share. Secondary: [⬇ Save to phone] (a[download] to Downloads, which appears in the gallery app) and Make a link.
  Desktop Chrome/Edge on Windows, macOS 128+, ChromeOS: primary [⬇ Save to computer]. Secondary: [Share] (OS share: Nearby Share/Drive on ChromeOS), [📲 Send to a phone] (QR, needs a link), Make a link.
  Firefox (desktop and Android), Linux Chrome, anywhere canShare({files}) is false: primary Save (download) + Send to a phone (QR) + Make a link. The Share button is not rendered.
  Chromium file over 50 MB: Share auto-offers 'This video is big! We'll make a smaller copy to share… 40%' and then re-arms.
6.3 iOS coaching (above the Share button). It shows on the first 3 shares on the device, then collapses into a small link 'How do I keep it in Photos?':
  An illustration of the bottom of the iOS share sheet with the 'Save Video' row outlined in orange (a real screenshot-style drawing, not an icon grid).
  Text: 'Want it in Photos? Tap Share, then tap Save Video.' Small: 'If your iPhone asks, tap Allow.'
  🔊 reads the text aloud.
  The wording matches the literal iOS label 'Save Video', because kids follow instructions literally (NN/g).
6.4 Results:
  resolve -> toast 'Shared! 🎉' (celebration, no confetti with reduced motion)
  AbortError (the kid closed the sheet) -> quiet line in the footer: 'No problem. Your clip is safe in My Clips.'
  NotAllowedError (activation expired) -> the button re-arms: 'Oops! Tap Share one more time.'
  a thrown TypeError/DataError (type rejected) -> fall back to the Save button, with 'Let's save it instead!'
6.5 Make a link (sheet over the editor):
  Screen 1:
  - Poster.
  - 'Anyone with the link can watch this clip.'
  - Quick check: 'No real names, schools, or towns in your clip?' This is the Xbox 'review your captures' idea, as a single tap, not a gate.
  - [👍 Looks good! Make my link] [Watch it again].
  Screen 2 (progress): 'Sending your clip… 60%'. The upload goes straight to the bucket (presigned); the page stays usable.
  Screen 3 (ready):
  - 'Your link is ready! 🎉'
  - The link text shown as 'hankshits.com/c/k7Qm2xZp'.
  - [Share link] uses navigator.share({url, text:'Watch my Monster Truck clip!'}) where URL share is supported.
  - [Copy link] -> 'Link copied! Paste it in a message.' (visible confirmation; the Wordle clipboard lesson).
  - QR code, 200 px, with 'Scan with a phone camera to watch it there.' (Steam/Switch QR precedent: moves a clip from a school Chromebook to a family phone).
  - 'Works for 90 days.' [Delete link]
  The link copy is auto-sized to ≤ ~9 MB so iMessage previews autoplay inline (TN3156). Longer Record videos still get a link that plays on the page, and they unfurl as a poster image.
  Guests can make links too (open sharing). Attribution is 'No name'. The device keeps the delete token.
  If link service is unconfigured (local pnpm dev with no bucket env), 'Make a link' is not rendered. Share and Save still work.
6.6 Send to a phone (desktop): the same as Make a link, opening straight to the QR. The phone lands on /c/<slug>. That page shows [⬇ Get the video]. After the file is fetched, it shows [Save to Photos] (navigator.share files). This is two taps because of activation.

11. ACCESSIBILITY AND KID-UX RULES
=====================================================================
- Targets: ≥44 px everywhere; primary Share 56 px; trim handles 64 px touch (≈2 cm on phones, NN/g); chips 48 px.
- Every sheet (Capture menu, editor, share coaching, Make a link, settings, library empty state, hosted page) has a ReadAloudButton whose text names every visible button, in on-screen order. Update PauseMenu spokenExtras with 'Clips' (and PauseMenu.test).

- Surfaces: slate-900 sheets with border-slate-700, matching LeaderboardModal. Toasts are solid slate-900/95. No backdrop-blur on new cards (the header's existing blur stays).
- One accent with a point of view: the clip orange (theme accent #f97316) marks only clip affordances (ring, handles, selected outline, the 'Save Video' highlight). Live recording uses red. Primary actions stay house blue (btn-primary).

- Type: Nunito (house). tabular-nums for every timer, duration and score. Headings are sentence case.

- Zero code: the shell auto-discovers the largest canvas in the play area (or the same-origin iframe canvas) and shows the button. The personal-best poll gives a 'new best' auto-highlight.
