16. ACCEPTANCE CHECKS (UX-level, for the QA plan)
=====================================================================
- Header at 360 / 375 / 390 / 430 px × {canPause, not} × {guest, signed in} × {tab, PWA}: no overflow, every target ≥44 px, the title rule applied. Test with the iPhone UA as well as touch emulation (lessons.md).
- For all 26 games: tap 🎬 after 10 s, and the clip contains the game plus the score band, with game audio and no DOM names.
- iOS real device: Share -> 'Save Video' lands in Photos. The coaching copy matches the real label.
- Android real device: Share and Save to phone. A 60 MB Record video triggers the smaller copy.
- Reduced motion on: no autoplay, no pulses. VoiceOver/TalkBack: every control is named, and saved is announced.
- Anti-nag: 3 ignored chips suppress the chips for that game. A dismissed chip never reappears in the same run.
- Pause menu read-aloud includes 'Clips' (update PauseMenu.test).
- Hosted page: iMessage unfurl autoplays a ≤9 MB clip, and 410 on delete.
- Storage: persist requested, the eviction note shown when denied, Tidy up lists what it keeps.
risksAndMitigations: Header crowding: the title is already unreadable at 390 px on pause-button games (measured 38 px for 118 px), and a 6th control removes it. Mitigation: the deterministic width-budget steps in 2.3, pinned by tests at 360/375/390/430 px across canPause x guest x PWA. GameShell.test indexes Restart by position, so update those tests deliberately.

Open sharing for all ages diverges from every major precedent (Nintendo under-13 share block, Xbox child defaults, Roblox Moments 13+ then 16+ age-checked). This is Jack's settled call, not reopened here. Mitigations are built into the UX: PII-free by construction (canvas + game audio only, no free text, handle or No name only, name only on the end card), unlisted links, a one-tap self-check before a link, Report with auto-hide on 2 reports, owner delete/renew, a 90-day default expiry, and per-device link rate limits.

Pixels can still carry kid-typed text: retro-arcade ROM name-entry screens, a kid-built game that paints a name, and the Oregon Trail inputs if a painter ever draws them. Mitigation: the compositor never rasterizes DOM, the Oregon painter excludes party names (feasibility capture map), the link self-check line names exactly this risk, and Report covers it. Automated OCR moderation is rejected (no paid services; heavy on-device), so this residual risk depends on review.

Transient activation on iOS: a share called after an async render throws NotAllowedError. Mitigation: background pre-render on every editor change, and the Share button turns into 'Getting it ready' then 'Share it!' (a fresh tap). NotAllowedError re-arms the button with kid copy.

The iOS 'Save Video' flow can fail silently for some users (Apple Community report), and a Photos permission prompt is unverified. Mitigation: conditional coaching ('If your iPhone asks, tap Allow'), the clip always remains in My Clips, and a real-iPhone check is in the acceptance list.

Nagging: auto-highlight prompts can become spam. Mitigation: chips only at natural breaks, at most 1 per run and 1 per 3 minutes, dedupe against manual clips, a 7-day per-game backoff after 3 ignored chips, and a settings kill switch. Silent saves always land in the Auto filter.

Silent data loss: browser storage eviction, private mode, and the 7-day auto-clip cleanup. Mitigation: navigator.storage.persist() on the first clip, visible notes when not persisted or in private mode, cleanup counts shown in the library, and Tidy up that lists what it keeps before deleting.

Performance on low-end Chromebooks and phones: always-on capture costs frame rate (feasibility: compositor about 15%; the raw DPR canvas tanked Monster Truck to 4-6 fps). Mitigation: Auto picture quality, an automatic downshift to Smooth, then resting the clip camera with one kid-word toast. Record stays available.

Toast collisions with game HUDs and the achievement toast. Mitigation: one shared ToastLane queue with priorities, a trophy + clip merge rule, pointer-events-none except the buttons, and a 4 s show window.
Growth watermark vs reach: a large watermark can get clips demoted on Instagram (Feb 2021 policy). Mitigation: a small static corner bug + a 1.5 s end card, and the end card can be turned off.

Instant-edit promise depends on the architecture: 1 s keyframes (trim by remux), an end card encoded with identical codec parameters (concatenation), and audio-only re-encode for music/speed. If the encoder track cannot guarantee identical SPS/PPS for the end card, fall back to re-encoding only the last GOP + card. The UX already has a progress state for this.
Kids may tap Share repeatedly or leave mid-upload. Mitigation: taps are ignored while saving, the link upload survives sheet navigation, and failures show 'Try again' with the clip kept locally.

Pre-existing defects seen during research: the IOSInstallPrompt close button is 32 px (below the 44 px rule); gradient-text headings and purple gradients are slop tells. Mitigation: fold the one-line close-button fix into the clip PR (it shares the bottom-sheet presence work), and file the slop sweep with file:line evidence (Header.tsx h1, HomeClient.tsx:195 hero, TrophiesPage.tsx:19, AchievementCelebrations.tsx:94).
rejectedAlternatives: Clip button only in the pause menu or on result screens: 11 games have no pause menu, and instant replay's value is one tap right after the moment (Switch/Xbox/PS5 all use a dedicated always-available button).

Floating in-canvas clip button: the corners are taken by game touch controls (monster-truck pedals, etc.), and the shell contract forbids per-game floating chrome (ARCHITECTURE.md 'the shell owns the chrome').
Tap opens a menu (PS5 Standard mode): it adds a decision at the worst moment. Tap saves instantly, and the menu goes on long-press/right-click, mirrored in the pause menu.
Long-press as the ONLY route to Record/Photo: kids rarely discover hidden gestures (NN/g PBS example), so the same menu is also in the pause menu, the Capture menu, and a one-time tip.
Single-letter keyboard shortcut (C): Wordle types letters and four-wheeler-3d binds C/E/F/P/M/I/X. F-key-only shortcuts fail on Chromebooks and Mac laptops.
Pre-roll title card before the action: it delays the first-second hook. The game name and score live in the top band from frame 0, and branding goes to the end card.
Big bouncing TikTok-style watermark: it risks demotion on Instagram and obscures gameplay.
Free-text titles, captions or descriptions (as in Roblox Moments): typed text is the main PII vector for kids. Preset stickers and score captions only.
Copy video to clipboard as a share path: clipboard confused Wordle players, and video clipboard support is patchy. Copy is offered only for links, with a visible 'Link copied!' confirmation.
Download on iOS: it lands in Files > Downloads, not Photos. Share sheet 'Save Video' is the only Photos path.
Cloud-synced clip library for signed-in kids: every clip would cost storage and would become PI when combined with the account. The explicit link + QR 'send to a phone' covers cross-device.
Public clip gallery or clips feed (Roblox Moments tab): it turns unlisted links into listed public content, beyond 'open sharing' of links. Left as an open question for Jack, not designed in.
Trophies for sharing or making links: they nudge kids toward publishing. Trophies reward making clips only.
Licensed music catalog (Roblox uses DistroKid): it would be a new outside service. The music beds are synthesized in-house.
Server-side OCR or video moderation: it needs a paid service or heavy compute. Report + auto-hide + review instead.
Full-screen shutter flash on save: a photosensitivity risk (WCAG 2.3.1). Button-local check + sound + toast instead.
openQuestions: Hosted link lifetime: this spec recommends 90 days, renewable by the owner, as the written COPPA 312.10 retention period. Jack has not settled a number. Confirm or pick one.

Default attribution: should the handle appear on the end card by default (mirroring showOnLeaderboards), or should 'No name' be the default for everyone? The spec mirrors the leaderboard choice. Confirm.

Should leaderboard rows be able to show a ▶ clip for top scores (a 'prove it' loop, Kidscreen's 'trackside billboard' idea)? That makes clips listed rather than unlisted, so it needs Jack's explicit OK before it is designed in.
Does Safari show a one-time Photos permission prompt when 'Save Video' is tapped from a web share sheet? This needs a real-iPhone check; the coaching copy is conditional until then.

Gamepad: is button 16 (Home/Guide) delivered to web pages on ChromeOS, macOS and Windows with Game Bar installed? If it is, it could be the retro-arcade clip trigger, where button 8 is Select. Device test needed.
Reactions on the hosted page (preset, anonymous, counts visible only to the owner): keep them in scope, or drop them to keep the link page strictly view-only?
Per-device link rate limit (proposed 20 links/day/device plus an IP ceiling): confirm the numbers against the expected class-share bursts (a whole class sharing on the same school IP).

verdicts.claim: Steam Game Recording: three modes; the Clip button makes an adjustable suggestion; export to MP4, Copy to Clipboard, Send to Other Device (within 2 days), and a Steam-hosted Share Link that expires after 2 days.
verdicts.correction: The claim is correct, but the spec ignores what it implies. Steam's hosted link lives 2 days. The spec's default is 90 days with unlimited 'Keep 90 more days' renewals, which is 45x longer, and storage and moderation exposure grow with that lifetime.

verdicts.claim: Steam Timeline API: AddTimelineEvent(icon, title, description, priority, startOffset, duration, clipPriority); Featured adds a pre/post buffer and pre-selects a clip; Standard is a marker only; SetTimelineGameMode shades the bar.
verdicts.correction: The signature is stale. The current API is AddInstantaneousTimelineEvent(title, description, icon, priority, startOffset, clipPriority), AddRangeTimelineEvent(..., duration, ...) and StartRangeTimelineEvent. 'Standard is a marker only' is wrong: None (1) means 'not appropriate as a clip', Standard (2) means 'the user may want to make a clip around this event', and Featured (3) is promoted ahead of Standard. The Featured buffer is only in Valve's overview video, not in the API reference. Two parts the track missed are load-bearing for this spec. (a) flStartOffsetSeconds can be negative, for events whose significance is only known later. (b) Game Phases (StartGamePhase/EndGamePhase/SetGamePhaseAttribute) are the run-boundary signal that the spec's 'natural break' rules need and do not have.

verdicts.claim: Switch: hold Capture saves the last 30 s, trim later in the Album, Send to Smartphone by QR; the Nintendo Switch app bars sharing by users under 13.
PS5 Create: Save Recent Gameplay from 15 s up to 1 h, plus auto trophy captures.
Auto-highlights: Medal F8 saves 15 s to 10 min and auto-clips; Postparty prompts during the Goal Replay, saves the last 30 s, enforces a 3 s minimum and gives a title for the first share.
verdicts.correction: Medal now offers 15/30/60 s 'or even up to 20 minutes', not 10 min. The track missed one Medal behavior: during a Long Recording, the clip hotkey becomes a Bookmark key. The spec instead turns the header clip button into Stop while recording (2.5), so a kid who taps it out of Clip-it habit ends the recording. The Postparty details are confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Data replays: Brawl Stars Battle Log keeps the 25 latest games with shareable replays (supports a 'Recent games' list for DOM games).
Roblox Moments: 30 s captures, trim/music/description, 10 uploads/day, auto-moderated and reportable, usernames/UI stripped, voices muted, 13+ at launch, 16+ age-checked from 2026-07-28.
verdicts.correction: Every fact is confirmed, including 'available to age-checked players 16+' (2026-07-28 post). The track left out the contrast that matters most. Roblox states 'Users cannot upload external files': only in-client captures can be posted, and every published video is auto-moderated. The spec's hosted links accept arbitrary client-uploaded bytes and have no moderation. Roblox's under-16 catalogs also exclude 'free-form drawing games' by default, which bears directly on this repo's drawing-app canvas.

verdicts.claim: Every major platform restricts public posting of captures by young kids (Nintendo under-13, Xbox child defaults, Roblox 13+/16+).
Short-form norms: 9:16, Shorts and Reels up to 3 min; keep text inside platform safe zones (top ~10%, bottom ~20-40%, right ~11%).
verdicts.correction: The numbers are fine, but the track applies them to the wrong channel. The safe zones protect against feed-app overlays on TikTok, Reels and Shorts, which are 13+ platforms. The track's own Wordle finding says the real audience is group chats, where nothing overlays the video. Leaving the bottom 20% of every Tall frame as a blank brand field (spec 3.7) spends game pixels to help a channel most of these kids cannot use.

verdicts.claim: NN/g: at least 2 cm x 2 cm touch targets for young children; the spec implements this as 64 CSS px on phones.
verdicts.correction: The 2 cm figure is confirmed. The conversion is wrong. iPhones run about 153-163 CSS px per inch and Android about 160 dp per inch, so 2 cm is about 120-126 CSS px. 64 CSS px is about 1 cm, which is NN/g's ADULT size. Two 2 cm handles do not fit usefully on a 390 px filmstrip, so the tap paths have to be the primary trim control.

verdicts.claim: GameShell header at 390 px already truncates the title; the width-budget steps fix every case (360 canPause=320 px, 375 canPause=false=364 px).
verdicts.correction: The problem is real, but the budget arithmetic leaves out the title div's px-2 (16 px, GameShell.tsx:88). A canPause=false guest game at 375 px needs 24+44+(28+16)+268 = 380 px, which overflows before step 4 runs. At 320 px (iOS Display Zoom on iPhone SE 2/3 and the minis) the same game still needs 332 px after step 4. The test matrix starts at 360 and never checks 320.

verdicts.claim: PauseMenu already carries Leaderboard + Restart; 11 games and 7 apps pass canPause={false}.
Chromium Web Share caps at 10 files / 50 MB; iMessage autoplays og:video only when page + image + video total <= 10 MB, so the link copy should be <= ~9 MB.
verdicts.correction: The 50 MB cap is confirmed on desktop AND Android. TN3156 splits the budget differently: the main resource (the page) is capped at 1 MB, and the associated resources (icons, images AND video together) are capped at 10 MB. Apple calls these 'guidelines only; limits may change'. So the ~9 MB target has to include the og:image poster and the icon.

verdicts.claim: House style: Nunito, primary #2563eb / secondary #16a34a / accent #f97316, toast lane fixed top-14 z-[1100].
The zero-code fallback (achievements personal-best 1 s poll) gives every game a 'new best' highlight; the ring absorbs the 1 s latency; auto clip = 8 s before to 3 s after.
verdicts.correction: The poll only sees the best when the store WRITES it. Flappy, for example, writes highScore in endGame(), at game over. The real delay is therefore 'moment the old best was passed' to 'crash', which can be minutes, not 1 s. The 8 s/3 s window catches the crash and the game-over screen, not the record-breaking moment. evaluate.ts also stays silent when prev.best is 0, so a kid's first-ever score never produces a highlight.

verdicts.claim: Gamepad: the Standard mapping has no Share/Capture button and Xbox Share is not exposed, so use hold button 8 for 1 s.
verdicts.correction: Chromium exposes an extra buttons[17] beyond the standard 17 buttons. On macOS it maps the Xbox Series X Share button there. On Windows, macOS and Linux it maps the Switch Pro Capture button there. XInput on Windows really does not expose Xbox Share. DualSense and DualShock also put their touchpad click on index 17, so the mapping must be chosen by gamepad.id: 17 = Clip it on Switch Pro and Xbox Series, with hold-8 as the fallback everywhere else.

verdicts.claim: Desktop shortcut: Alt+C (Option+C) / Alt+R / F8 via event.code + altKey, gated by keyBelongsToTarget.
verdicts.correction: No reserved-key conflict was found for Alt+C or Alt+R. The handler has two gaps. It must require !ctrlKey && !metaKey, because Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt (for example, Polish AltGr+C types 'ć'). It must also listen inside the same-origin iframes of retro-arcade and four-wheeler-adventure, because a keydown there never reaches the parent window once the kid clicks into the game.

verdicts.claim: iOS Photos path is share-sheet 'Save Video' only; share files-only with exact type 'video/mp4'.
verdicts.correction: No evidence against the iOS part. The hosted-page flow misses one gap: Android WebView has no navigator.share at all. Recipients usually open /c/<slug> inside in-app browsers (Messenger, Instagram, Discord on Android), so 'Save to Photos' on the hosted page fails there. That page needs an 'Open in Chrome' handoff.

verdicts.claim: Pre-existing defect: IOSInstallPrompt close button is w-8 h-8 (32 px).
verdicts.correction: Also missed in the same header: RestartGameButton.tsx:11-21 sets no text color, so the ↻ glyph renders dark on the bg-black/70 header (visible in /tmp/hh-clips/header-320-snake-playing.png). This is a one-line fix and belongs in the header rework. IOSInstallPrompt.tsx:54 also uses a blue gradient, which is a slop tell.

designSpecProblems: P7 'PII-free by construction' is FALSE in shipped code, and it breaks the settled 'no real name' constraint. four-wheeler-3d renders kid-typed free text (up to 10 chars) as a CanvasTexture on the front and back of the rider's shirt inside the WebGL scene (components/models/OutfitText.tsx:14-39, Player.tsx:303-304, RiderModel.tsx:118; typed in PropertyPanel.tsx:331-335). The default value is literally 'HANK' (lib/adventureTypes.ts:220). Any canvas capture records it, so every four-wheeler-3d clip shows a real first name out of the box. The class fix is a capture-safety contract: no free-text or free-draw content may render into a capturable surface. Here that means outfit text becomes preset words only (the panel already has preset buttons at PropertyPanel.tsx:341), or it is blanked while the clip camera is on. make-a-game needs a matching gate.

Sections 2.1 and 15 contradict each other on drawing-app. 2.1 says apps show no button. 15 says the shell auto-discovers 'the largest canvas in the play area'. apps/drawing-app is a free-draw canvas (components/Canvas.tsx:51), so auto-discovery would give it a clip button and public links of hand-drawn names, schools and addresses. Under COPPA 16 CFR 312.2, 'collects' includes enabling a child to make PI public, unless the operator takes reasonable measures to delete PI BEFORE it is public (/tmp/hh-clips/ecfr-312.txt:21). So excluding category 'apps' and free-draw surfaces is a compliance mechanism, not polish. Auto-discovery is also unreliable in real games: four-wheeler-3d mounts extra canvases (VehiclePreview R3F, PhonePanel 2D), oregon-trail swaps canvases in and out, and math-attack's canvas exists only while playing (feasibility games[].primarySurface).

Hosted links accept ARBITRARY client bytes. A presigned upload means the server never sees how the MP4 was produced. Any adult or script can host any video at hankshits.com/c/<slug> with og:video autoplay in iMessage, under a kids' brand. Roblox avoids this entirely ('Users cannot upload external files', and every video is auto-moderated). Railway's own guide says to treat uploads as untrusted and validate after upload (https://docs.railway.com/storage-buckets/uploading-serving). The spec needs all of the following. (1) A presigned POST with a content-length-range and an exact Content-Type. (2) Server-side validation before the link goes live: parse the moov (mediabunny runs in Node), and require one avc1 track at the exact compositor dimensions, an optional mp4a track, duration within the cap, and a server-issued nonce in udta. (3) A SHA-256 per object, because TIDA requires removing 'known identical copies'. (4) Fail-closed hide on the FIRST report, pending review. (5) An admin role and review queue; the repo has no admin concept at all (grep isAdmin/role returns nothing). (6) An alert channel to the 'grown-up'. (7) A global daily upload-byte circuit breaker with honest copy. Without the breaker, abuse cost is unbounded: 10k x 50 MB uploads/day held for 90 days is about 45 TB, about $675/month at $0.015/GB-month.

Per-IP rate limits will not work behind Cloudflare. getClientIP (lib/rate-limit.ts:151-171) keys on x-real-ip, or the rightmost X-Forwarded-For. Railway defines X-Real-IP as the client's remote IP (https://docs.railway.com/networking/public-networking/specs-and-limits), and prod answers 'server: cloudflare', so that IP is a Cloudflare edge address. Nothing in the repo reads CF-Connecting-IP. The limiter is also in-memory and per-replica, and resets on every deploy. The spec's '20 links/day/device + IP ceiling' would pool whole regions into one bucket, so kids who made no links would see 'You made lots of links today!', and attackers bypass it by rotating client device IDs. This pre-existing defect also weakens the signup, progress and ROM limiters, so it is security scope and must be fixed in the PR: use CF-Connecting-IP only when x-real-ip is inside Cloudflare's ranges, and persist link counters in Postgres.

Serving path is undefined, and the obvious path is forbidden. Cloudflare's CDN terms say non-Enterprise customers must use paid Stream/R2 'to serve video and other large files via the CDN' (https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-application-services/, /tmp/hh-clips/adv/cf-sst.md:110). Cloudflare also caches .mp4 and .jpg by extension by default (https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/), which delays takedowns. So clips AND posters must come from the Railway bucket via presigned URLs (bucket egress is free), never proxied through hankshits.com. Three pieces of config are missing. (1) The current CSP 'media-src self blob:' (apps/web/next.config.ts:35) blocks a bucket-hosted <video> on /c/<slug>. (2) Bucket CORS must be set with aws s3api put-bucket-cors, because Railway has no dashboard setting; it is needed for browser PUT and for the recipient page's fetch-then-share. (3) Railway buckets do not support lifecycle rules (https://docs.railway.com/storage-buckets), so '90-day expiry' needs a cron sweeper, and the spec never mentions one.

4.2 lets canPause=false games keep running under the editor. That list is 11 games: flappy, dino, endless, math-attack, hill-climb, monster-truck, four-wheeler-3d, wordle, cookie-clicker, retro-arcade and four-wheeler-adventure. Tapping Watch mid-run kills the run, which breaks P2 'never interrupt play' and the house 'don't punish' rule. The saved toast also puts a live [Watch] button at top-14 over the playfield during active play. Flappy's input is onPointerDown on the canvas (flappy-bird/Game.tsx:382), so a flap aimed near the top lands on Watch and opens the editor. The saved toast must be non-interactive during play; Watch should appear at the next natural break or from the long-press menu.

The natural-break rules (4.4, 4.5e, and 'menu frames' in 2.5) cannot be built with zero code. The shell has no run-start or run-end signal for canPause=false games, which render their own game-over screens. The spec needs a shared phase API (startRun/endRun/setMode, the Steam StartGamePhase/EndGamePhase/SetTimelineGameMode model) plus markMoment({at}) with a negative offset. Only that lets a game report 'the old best was passed 40 s ago' at game over instead of anchoring the auto clip on the crash.

The 3.5/3.6 classification is wrong in places. oregon-trail is listed as real-time canvas ('the last 30 seconds', Wide), but the feasibility study says it is mostly DOM: Title, Store, Travel, Event, River and GameUI screens, with a decorative travel strip and a hunting-only canvas that swap in and out (feasibility games[oregon-trail]). Its clip would show a parallax strip or nothing. The static Wide list also contradicts the 'aspect < 1.2 = Tall' Auto rule for viewport-sized canvases: hill-climb (Game.tsx:1187 sized to innerWidth x innerHeight), monster-truck and four-wheeler-3d are portrait on a portrait phone. Rotating the phone mid-ring changes the source aspect, and the spec never says what the compositor does then.

5.6 claims several edits are INSTANT, but the ring design cannot deliver that. If the ring stores COMPOSITED Tall/Wide frames, 'shape change' can only upscale a letterboxed game region, which looks blurry. The fix is to store the un-composited game surface plus a score/HUD timeline and composite at export, which makes style edits re-encodes. The end card cannot be 'pre-encoded' either: it carries a per-clip score, handle, sticker and NEW BEST badge. The spec must pick one design and state the tradeoff honestly.

The header width budget is off by the title padding (px-2 = 16 px). canPause=false guest games at 375 px overflow before step 4 runs, and 320 px (iOS Display Zoom on SE 2/3 and the minis) still overflows after step 4 (332 > 320). The budget needs a step 5, for example moving 📲/⛶ into the Capture menu below 400 px, or dropping the visible title completely and keeping only its aria-label. 320 px must join the acceptance matrix. Fix the dark ↻ glyph (RestartGameButton.tsx) in the same change.

The trim editor claims its handles are 'about 2 cm (64 CSS px)'. 64 CSS px is about 1 cm on phones, and true 2 cm handles do not fit a two-handle strip on a 390 px screen. Make the length chips and 'Start here / End here' the primary controls, make the handles tall (96 px or more) rather than wide, and state the NN/g gap honestly.

Local-first storage fails silently on iPhone Safari tabs. WebKit deletes ALL script-writable storage after 7 days of Safari use without interaction on the site, and it grants persist() mainly to Home Screen web apps (https://webkit.org/blog/14403/updates-to-storage-policy/, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage_API/Storage_quotas_and_eviction_criteria). A kid who stays away a week loses the whole library, Recent games, AND the only delete tokens for guest links. The spec's copy blames 'space runs low', which is the wrong cause. The fix: honest copy, steer the kid to Add to Home Screen (IOSInstallPrompt already exists), and give signed-in kids server-side link ownership so links stay deletable from any device.

Private windows break OPFS outright. navigator.storage.getDirectory() rejects in Safari private windows ('unknown transient reason') and in Firefox private windows (SecurityError) (https://detectincognito.com/how-it-works, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/StorageManager/getDirectory). Record-to-OPFS and an OPFS library therefore fail completely, not just 'disappear when you close the tab'. The spec needs an in-memory fallback, plus copy that says 'share it now'.

7.4 calls navigator.storage.persist() automatically on the first clip. Firefox shows a browser permission popup for persist() (MDN, same page), so a 7-year-old gets a scary browser prompt mid-game. Either explain first and let the kid choose, or skip the call on Firefox.

Record mode has no crash safety. iOS kills backgrounded tabs, and a kid switching to Messages is enough. 'Stops and saves on route change' does not cover a tab kill. Write Record as a fragmented MP4 to OPFS (mediabunny fastStart 'fragmented', /tmp/hh-rec/scrape-mb-outfmt.md:205-207) and recover orphaned recordings on the next load. Also follow Medal's precedent: during Record, a tap on the clip button should drop a ⭐ bookmark or save a clip, not stop the recording.

The '>50 MB: we'll make a smaller copy' promise fails for long Record videos. 50 MB over 30 min is about 220 kbps, which is mush. For long videos, Save to phone (download) must be the primary path, and a smaller copy should be offered only when a watchable bitrate fits. 6.5 also says 'Longer Record videos still get a link' with no size policy, which invites 1 GB uploads. Set an explicit, justified cap (per-request serving cost and abuse), and show and log every refusal.

Android portrait encode may fail. Blink and the Android NDK encoder only accept a size when width <= maxW AND height <= maxH, with no rotation (video_encoder.cc:248-251, ndk_video_encode_accelerator.cc:583-588). Chromium adds a portrait profile only if the codec reports isSizeSupported(maxH, maxW) (VideoAcceleratorUtil.java:381-383). On encoders that advertise landscape maximums only (e.g. 1920x1088), 720x1280 is rejected for hardware and falls to software encoding or fails. The Tall default must probe isConfigSupported, and if needed encode 1280x720 with rotation metadata (mediabunny supports track rotation, /tmp/hh-rec/scrape-mb-writing.md:164-165).

Link lifetime and 'Send to a phone' over-publish. Steam's hosted link lives 2 days and 'Send to Other Device' is device-bound. The spec makes every phone transfer a 90-day public link with a page and an unfurl. Add a short-lived private transfer link: single download, 48 h or less, no page, no og tags. Also add Safari on macOS to the 6.2 table: navigator.share with files works there, and AirDrop to the family iPhone needs no hosting at all.
The hosted page is missing noindex (X-Robots-Tag or a robots meta tag). An unlisted clip posted in a public Discord or forum gets crawled and indexed. 410 only helps after expiry.

'Two independent reports hide the clip' has no way to prove independence: device IDs are client-made and IP limits pool on Cloudflare IPs. Kids can prank-hide a friend's clip from two devices. NCII or CSAM content needs removal within hours, not a second report. Hide on the first report pending admin review, rate-limit reporters, and give owners a visible 'being checked' state. 8.3 also needs a Take It Down Act style removal-request path (see missedIssues).

The upgrade of the toast lane and PauseMenu must remove the slop that the spec says only 'do not copy'. AchievementCelebrations.tsx:94 uses a yellow-to-orange gradient, and PauseMenu.tsx:66 shows 'PAUSED' in all caps with an animate-pulse that ignores reduced motion. Both are files the spec edits. Jack's rule is to sweep these when polishing.
missedIssues: No privacy notice exists at all: there is no /privacy route and no link (apps/web/src/app has no privacy/terms), yet signup collects name + email from kids (app/signup page.tsx:157-203). Open public hosting requires the COPPA 312.4(d) notice to state that the site 'enables a child to make personal information publicly available', and 312.10 requires a WRITTEN retention policy inside that notice (/tmp/hh-clips/ecfr-312.txt:115,190-191). This is pre-existing, is legal/security scope, and must ship with the link feature.

Take It Down Act: in force since 2026-05-19. A covered platform must publish a clear process for requesting removal of non-consensual intimate imagery, remove valid requests AND known identical copies within 48 hours, and the FTC names 'video sharing, and gaming platforms' (https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-take-it-down-act). An open anonymous video host may qualify. The report flow needs this path, content hashes, and an SLA the owner can actually meet.

18 U.S.C. 2258A: once the site hosts user uploads, apparent CSAM it learns of must be reported to the NCMEC CyberTipline (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/2258A). The spec has no process, no admin tooling, and no preservation step.

DMCA 512(c) safe harbor for hosting clips of commercial retro-arcade ROM games requires a designated agent: $6 per filing, renewed every 3 years, and it publishes a street address unless a PO-box waiver is granted (https://www.copyright.gov/dmca-directory/, https://www.copyright.gov/rulemaking/onlinesp/NPR/faq.html). This is Jack's call (money plus a public address), and it should be raised before launch, not after a takedown.

Android in-app browsers (WebView) have no navigator.share (BCD webview_android false, /tmp/hh-rec/share-bcd-nav.json), and many drop a[download]. The /c/<slug> recipient page is usually opened inside exactly those browsers, so it needs an 'Open in Chrome' handoff.

Multi-tab: two game tabs means two rings and two encoders (double battery and heat), and OPFS sync access handles are exclusive, so Record in two tabs collides. Use a Web Locks or BroadcastChannel election so only one tab captures per origin.

Guest-to-account transition is unspecified. 7.5 partitions clips by account and 'device' for guests, but never says what happens to guest clips and guest-made links when that kid creates an account or signs in. The likely result is that the kid's clips vanish from view.

Fallback tier UX is undefined. 2.1 hides the button whenever VideoEncoder is missing, but the draft architecture includes fallback encoders. The spec needs a defined degraded state (for example, Record-only via MediaRecorder with the button acting as start/stop), not a disappearing feature on older iPhones.
The pre-existing restart glyph contrast defect in the header being redesigned (RestartGameButton.tsx sets no color, so the glyph is dark on bg-black/70) is a one-line fix and belongs in the PR.

Cost model is missing. At $0.015/GB-month with free bucket egress and free S3 ops (https://docs.railway.com/storage-buckets), 9 MB links held 90 days cost about $0.012 per daily link: 1k links/day is about $12/month and 10k/day about $122/month. That is cheap ONLY with a server-enforced size cap and a global daily byte budget. Unbounded renewals and Record-size links break the estimate.
verify.summary:
The research mostly holds up. The spec, though, has hard failures on the four axes Jack cares about: real names, abuse and cost, stability, and 10/10 UX. I confirmed the Steam, Switch, PS5, Roblox (including the 16+ restriction on 2026-07-28), NN/g 2 cm, Chromium 50 MB and house-style claims against primary sources and the repo. Four claims needed correction. The Steam Timeline API is stale: it is now AddInstantaneous/AddRangeTimelineEvent, and 'Standard' is not marker-only. The gamepad claim is refuted: Chromium exposes Xbox Series Share and Switch Pro Capture as buttons[17]. The TN3156 budget is 1 MB for the page plus 10 MB for all media together. The zero-code 'new best' fallback fires at game over, not at the record moment.

The spec breaks in these places:
- (1) 'PII-free by construction' is false. four-wheeler-3d paints kid-typed text, default 'HANK', onto the rider in WebGL, so every clip carries a real first name. drawing-app's free-draw canvas would be auto-discovered despite 2.1.
- (2) Hosted links accept arbitrary bytes, with no provenance check, no moderation, no admin role, no Take It Down Act, NCMEC or COPPA-notice process, and no privacy page on the site at all.
- (3) Per-IP limits key on Cloudflare edge IPs and live in memory, so the link rate limit is broken before it ships.
- (4) Serving video through hankshits.com violates Cloudflare's CDN terms, and the current CSP media-src blocks bucket-hosted video.
- (5) Watch on the 11 non-pausable games kills the run, and the tappable toast over the playfield invites mis-taps.
- (6) iOS Safari's 7-day storage wipe, private-window OPFS failure, Firefox's persist() prompt, Record crash loss, Android portrait-encode limits, the header budget math (off by 16 px, 320 px not covered) and '64 px = 2 cm' (really about 1 cm) are all wrong or missing.

Every fix is compatible with the settled open-sharing policy. None re-adds an age gate; the stronger abuse controls (Turnstile, fail-closed hide on first report) are proposals for Jack to approve. Scratch evidence is in /tmp/hh-clips/adv/.

games.registration:
File apps/web/src/games/arkanoid/Game.tsx. Insert the hook after the forceSync effect (after :50) and before the pointer effect at :52:
useClipSource('arkanoid', { canvas: () => canvasRef.current /* ref :11, <canvas> :420-426 */, phase: () => ({menu:'menu', playing:'playing', paused:'paused', gameOver:'result'} as const)[useArkanoidStore.getState().gameState], layout: { preset: 'fit-source' /* portrait 720x1280 when canvas.height > canvas.width, else landscape 1280x720 */, bandPx: {portrait:176, landscape:96}, letterbox: '#1e293b' }, fps: 60, hud: () => { const s = useArkanoidStore.getState(); return { score: s.score, best: s.progress.highScore, extras: [`${s.multiplier}x`] }; }, paintHud: paintArkanoidHud, paintResult: paintArkanoidResult }).
Put the painters in a new island file, games/arkanoid/lib/clipPainters.ts. They read useArkanoidStore.getState() on every tick and never read the DOM.

Lifecycle facts the hook must handle:
- The canvas never unmounts or remounts. There is no key, and the menu and game-over overlays are siblings at :462 and :484.
- The GameShell restart calls startGame (ArkanoidGameShell.tsx:29), and startGame emits runStart, which the kit treats as a cut.
- The resize effect (:367-380) rewrites canvas.width/height on rotation. The kit must re-fit on every tick and insert a cut when the source dimensions change.
- ArkanoidGame re-renders every frame: it calls useArkanoidStore() with no selector (:14-31), and updateBalls runs every frame (:229, :342). So useClipSource must keep its config in a ref and register once per canvas element, never on each render.
- The loop effect (:198-364) has stable dependencies, so it needs no loop migration. The kit samples the canvas in its own rAF, or through onAfterRender if the loop later moves to useGameLoop.
games.overlay:
The kit paints the HUD band and the result card. Arkanoid's canvas paints only the grid, walls, paddle and balls (:114-195), so a raw capture has no numbers at all.

(1) HUD band (paintArkanoidHud), above the game rect, copying the DOM strip at :394-406:
- Background #0f172a (bg-slate-900, :391).
- Score: bold white, centered, about 72 px in the portrait band (text-3xl/md:text-4xl), formatted with score.toLocaleString() like the DOM.
- Sub-line in #94a3b8: `${multiplier}x Multiplier • High: ${progress.highScore.toLocaleString()}`.
- Leave out the sound button (:409-415) and the launch hint pill (:429-435). They are UI chrome, not gameplay.

(2) Ball-counter chips on the game rect's top-left, copying :438-458:
- Draw them only when gameState==='playing' and the count is above 0.
- Chip: rgba(30,41,59,0.8), radius 8.
- Dot colors: #3b82f6 blue (h-6), #f97316 orange (h-6), #facc15 yellow (h-4).
- Label: bold white `x${n}`.
- Counts are balls.filter(b => b.type === ...) over getState().balls.

(3) Result card (paintArkanoidResult, phase 'result'), copying the DOM overlay at :484-502:
- Fill the game rect with rgba(15,23,42,0.95).
- 'Game Over!' in bold white.
- `Score: ${score.toLocaleString()}` in #facc15.
- '🎉 New High Score! 🎉' in #4ade80 when wasNewHighScore is true.
- `High Score: ${progress.highScore.toLocaleString()}` in #94a3b8.
- No Play Again button.

The loop returns before rendering on loss (:346-349). So the frame under the card is the last gameplay frame, which the kit re-draws. Emoji use the platform font, the same as the DOM.
games.layout:
The layout follows the source aspect, which is device-dependent because the arena is stretched to the viewport.

Portrait phones: 720x1280.
- HUD band: 176 px.
- Game rect: the canvas fitted into 720x1104, letterboxed with #1e293b (GAME.canvasColor, constants.ts:95) so the bars read as arena.

Desktop landscape: 1280x720.
- HUD band: 96 px.
- Game rect: fitted into 1280x624.

Scaling:
- The source is already viewport x devicePixelRatio (about 1170x2178 on a 3x iPhone, :371-375), so the kit always downsamples.
- Use imageSmoothingEnabled=true and imageSmoothingQuality='high'. The content is smooth vector art (radial gradients), not pixel art.
- Do not change the backing store.

Frame rate: 60 fps preferred (fast multi-ball motion), with the kit's adaptive drop to 30. This needs an H.264 Level 4.0 codec string (see groupNotes).
games.bragEvents:
Use the shared createRunBrag('arkanoid') helper from the store (lib/store.ts), so the edge detection lives in one place.

- runStart: in startGame (store.ts:99-116), call brag.start(progress.highScore) and reset runPeakMultiplier to 1.
- newHighScore (highlight): in addScore (:211-215), after computing the new score, call brag.score(newScore). It fires once per run, on the first moment newScore > bestAtRunStart, and only when bestAtRunStart > 0. First-ever runs stay silent, matching achievements/evaluate.ts:115-121. The payload is {prevBest: bestAtRunStart, newBest, runId}. The comparison is against the snapshot taken at runStart, never progress.highScore, which endGame bumps.
- combo, rising edge only: updateMultiplier (:217-224) runs every frame (Game.tsx:343), and ball counts flap around 10/20/50. So emit {type:'combo', tier} only when mult > runPeakMultiplier, then set runPeakMultiplier = mult. Each tier fires at most once per run. 5x and 10x are highlights; 2x is a marker.

prerequisiteFixes: The hunting animation loop wipes the herd. Verified on prod (/tmp/hh-clips/g7/input.out): with the mouse still there were three animals, at x = 702, 869 and 91; after ONE mouse move, only a fresh spawn at x = -17 remained. Cause: the effect's deps [cursorPos, recoil, paused] (Hunting.tsx:489) re-arm the loop on every aim move and every shot. 'let lastTime = 0' (269) then makes the first frame's delta timestamp/16, which is in the thousands, so every animal jumps off-screen and is deleted (334-338). On desktop you cannot aim without triggering this.

Hunting draws inside setState updaters: animals at 328-389, hit text at 392-414, bullet holes at 417-449. React runs only the first update of a frame eagerly. The others run during a later render task, after the frame has already been presented, and the next frame clears them. Verified: none of 8 screenshots taken 81-196 ms after a miss showed the bullet hole (/tmp/hh-clips/g7/huntfx.out). Rewrite the minigame as one long-lived rAF loop. Keep animals, effects, cursor, timer, score, food and ammo in refs, clamp dt to 50 ms, and draw directly each frame. Push HUD values to React state at 10 Hz or less for the DOM HUD.

Two shots per tap on phones. The container has onClick (542) and onTouchStart (543). React's passive touchstart plus the W3C compatibility click run shoot twice (the same class verified on hextris), so each tap costs two bullets. The touchstart path also never moves the crosshair to the tap point. Use one onPointerDown that sets the cursor and fires.

games.bragEvents:
All events go to the kit via a module-level emit (proposed: clips.emit({appId, type, priority, title, payload})). Priority 2 or higher auto-saves a highlight clip (pre-roll 8 s, post-roll 2 s). Lower priorities only drop a marker on the replay timeline.

1) TRICK LANDING (priority 2). Vehicle.tsx:149-157 is the landing branch (grounded after airborneTime > 0.5).
- Add a per-jump counter flipsThisJump. Increment it where a flip is credited (Vehicle.tsx:142-147). Reset it at takeoff (:131-134) and after landing.
- On landing, emit {type:'trick', flips, airtimeS} when flips >= 1 or airtimeS >= 2.0.
- Title: flips 1 = 'FLIP!', 2 = 'DOUBLE FLIP!', 3+ = 'TRIPLE FLIP!', else 'BIG AIR x.x s'.
- Rising edge is structural: the event fires exactly once per landing, because isAirborne goes false in the same branch (:158).

2) NEW RECORD (priority 3). Add persisted records {bestAirtimeMs, mostFlipsOneJump} with a store action recordJump(airtimeMs, flips). The action returns {airtimeRecord, flipRecord, prevAirtimeMs, prevFlips}. It compares against the value read in the SAME set() before writing, and only strictly-greater counts. A first-ever record needs airtime >= 1.5 s or flips >= 1, so the first tiny hop does not brag. Emit {type:'newHighScore', metric:'airtime'|'flips', value, previous, better:'higher'} after set(). Refresh-proof: the compare is against the persisted best.

3) CHALLENGE COMPLETE (priority 3). getChallengeCompletionUpdate (store.ts:267-281) already knows which challenges flip. Change it to also return newlyCompleted: Challenge[]. The five callers (addCoins 312-327, addAirtime 400-413, addFlip 415-428, addDestruction 430-443, collectStar 445-458) emit one event per newly completed challenge after their set(). Do NOT detect this with a store subscription on challenges[i].completed: cloud hydration (useAuthSync setState -> setProgress, store.ts:562-571) and persist rehydrate flip the same field and would fire bogus brags.

4) SMASH COMBO (priority 2). The Destructibles handlers (Destructibles.tsx:276-296) push performance.now() into a module ring. Three or more smashes inside 2.5 s emits {type:'combo', count} once, updated to the final count when the combo window closes. A car smash (:289-296) alone is a priority 1 marker.

5) MARKERS ONLY (priority 1): mystery box (Collectibles.tsx:288-294) and star pickup (:282-286).

NOT EVENTS: truck unlock and upgrades (Garage.tsx:31-47). They happen in the DOM garage while the kit is idle.

SRCDOC PRELUDE: in games/four-wheeler-adventure/Game.tsx:72-76, change `setGameHtml(html)` to `setGameHtml(injectClipPrelude(html))`. The prelude lives in the island at games/four-wheeler-adventure/clip/prelude.ts. It is inserted as the FIRST child of <head>, before Hank's only game <script> (public/games/four-wheeler-adventure/index.html:654). Hank's file itself stays byte-identical, which honors the wrapper contract in Game.tsx:12-20. CSP allows it: a srcdoc document inherits the parent CSP, and script-src has 'unsafe-inline', which Hank's own inline script already relies on.

WHAT THE PRELUDE DEFINES:
(a) AUDIO BUS. `class HHAudioContext extends (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)`. Its constructor calls super(), creates `bus = this.createGain()`, connects bus to super.destination, then Object.defineProperty(this, 'destination', {value: bus}). Assign window.AudioContext = window.webkitAudioContext = HHAudioContext and publish window.__hhAudio = {ctx, bus}. Every one of Hank's five output sites connects to audioCtx.destination (index.html:1631, 1711, 5182, 5195, 6044), so the whole mix now flows through bus.
(b) iOS AUTO-RESUME. On the first pointerdown, touchend or keydown, a capture listener on document calls ctx.resume() if the context is suspended. index.html never calls resume() (grep). The context is created by startAudio (:1705-1734) from the parent's programmatic playBtn.click() in onLoad (Game.tsx:54-57), which is not a gesture, so on WebKit the game is likely silent today (verify on a real iPhone).
(c) PROBE. window.__hhProbe = () => { try { return {running, raceState: race.state, raceTime: race.time, winner: race.winner, raceCar, collected, total, money, skulls: mountedSkulls, rainbowTimer, mode, inSpace, onPlanet}; } catch { return null; } }. It works without eval because all classic scripts share one global lexical environment, so Hank's top-level let/const bindings resolve at call time. Declarations: index.html:747 race, 756 raceCar, 772 inSpace/onPlanet, 884 mode, 933 mountedSkulls, 977 rainbowTimer, 1042-1043 collected/total/money, 5398 running.
(d) PANEL WATCH. A MutationObserver on the style attribute of [id$=Panel], #sleepPad and #calcPad keeps window.__hhPanelOpen current. Those are the 20+ modals at index.html:490-640 and 5908, which Hank toggles with style.display. It costs nothing per frame.
(e) KEY FORWARD. Forward the kit's clip shortcut key to the parent. It must avoid Hank's bindings: WASD, arrows, Space, B, C, E, F, G, M, N, O, P, R, T.

REGISTRATION: in handleIframeLoad (Game.tsx:52-62), after playBtn.click(), run `disposeRef.current?.(); disposeRef.current = registerAdventureClipSource(iframeRef.current!, {restoreFocus: () => iframeRef.current?.contentWindow?.focus()})`. The adapter lives at games/four-wheeler-adventure/clip/source.ts.

WHAT THE ADAPTER DOES:
- It pushes frames from the IFRAME's own rAF: win.requestAnimationFrame(tick), re-armed each tick. It registers after Hank's loop (index.html:5399-5405, first armed at :6614), so it runs after draw() in the same frame. The HTML spec runs a child document's rAF AFTER its container's (html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html, update the rendering), so parent-rAF reads would lag one frame. A 2D canvas is readable at any time anyway.
- Timestamps must be converted: tsParent = tsIframe + (win.performance.timeOrigin − performance.timeOrigin). Each document has its own time origin (w3c.github.io/hr-time).
- Audio: kit.attachForeignTap(win.__hhAudio.bus, win) (see groupNotes).
- Idle: !probe || !probe.running || win.__hhPanelOpen.
- Dispose on the next onLoad and in a useEffect cleanup on unmount.

RESTART: key={restartNonce} (Game.tsx:106) remounts the iframe. The prelude re-runs, onLoad fires, and the adapter re-registers. The old realm's context dies with its document, so the kit must drop that tap and zero-fill.

FOCUS: after any kit dialog closes, call restoreFocus(). Keyboard players otherwise lose control, because Game.tsx:61 hands focus to the iframe.

MECHANISM: the adapter polls __hhProbe() once per tick and edge-detects against the previous snapshot. After every (re)load, the FIRST snapshot is the baseline and emits nothing, so a restart or first load never fires a brag. The events:
1) RACE WIN (priority 3). Transition prev.raceState === 'racing' to now 'done' with winner === 'you' (index.html:2106-2115). race.time is frozen once the state is 'done' (:2082-2083), so timeMs = round(raceTime * 1000).
  - Per-vehicle personal best in a wrapper-owned, device-owned key fwa_race_best_v1 = {[raceCar]: ms}. Device-owned is consistent with Hank's fwa_myland_v1 (shared/lib/localProgress.ts:47-50), which is deliberately not cleared on sign-out.
  - newBest = no stored value || timeMs < stored. Read the stored value BEFORE writing.
  - Emit {type:'win', timeMs, vehicle: VLABEL, newBest, prevBestMs}, plus newHighScore {better:'lower'} when improving an existing best.
  - Do NOT add this key to DEVICE_OWNED_ALIASES; that would change the shelf stat source.
2) ALL BONES (priority 3). prev.collected < total && now.collected === total && total > 0 (the :2010 condition).
3) WORLD RECORD SKULLS (priority 3). now.skulls > max(312, peakEmitted), then set peakEmitted = now.skulls (the WR badge rule at :2151). mountedSkulls resets at :5150 and :5569, so the peak is per iframe session.
4) RAINBOW FISH (priority 3). prev.rainbowTimer <= 0 && now.rainbowTimer > 0 (set to 6 at :6107).
5) MARKERS (priority 1): each bone pickup (collected increments) and each race start (idle to countdown).

NO CASINO CLIPS: casino wins (index.html:5881-5886) are deliberately NOT auto-clipped, so the brag system does not promote gambling-style wins.

COMPOSITOR PIPELINE:
(1) Crop the picture out of the EJS canvas, computed per capture:
  - a = getVideoDimensions('aspect'), nw/nh = getVideoDimensions('width'/'height'). These are cwrap('get_video_dimensions') calls in EJS 4.2.3 and cost almost nothing.
  - For a canvas W×H: if W/H > a, the picture is vw = H·a, x0 = (W − vw)/2, y0 = 0.
  - Otherwise vw = W, vh = W/a, x0 = 0, and y0 = 0, i.e. TOP-aligned. EJS writes video_top_portrait_viewport = true into retroarch.cfg (getRetroArchCfg in emulator.min.js 4.2.3). EJS's own screenRecord centers it (ejs-emulator.js:6100-6108), which is wrong in portrait.
(2) Native recovery: drawImage(crop → an nw×nh 'native' canvas, imageSmoothingEnabled=false). EJS sets video_smooth = false, so the canvas is a nearest-neighbor upscale and sampling at pixel centers recovers the exact native frame at any DPR, with tolerance ±s/2 px.
(3) The native canvas is updated only on dirty captures. The encode tick paints the last native frame, so the output holds the last frame and never goes black.
(4) Pillarbox bars: flat brand panels. Left: 'Retro Arcade' plus the console name from SYSTEMS[system].name. Right: the catalog title (null for uploads) plus the handle. The bottom-right bar carries hankshits.com. No overlay ever covers the game picture, because retro HUDs often sit at the frame edges.

IDLE: ejs.paused || ejs.settingsMenuOpen || ejs.disksMenuOpen (the same flags EJS checks at ejs-emulator.js:1721), plus the loading screen before 'ready'. A paused main loop issues no draws, so the dirty gate also stops frames naturally.
games.layout:
OUTPUT: 1280x720 with the game picture pixel-perfect in the center.

SCALE: vertical integer scale k = floor(720 / nh). Width = round(k · nh · aspect) to an even number. Upscale native → output with imageSmoothingEnabled=false.

PER CORE:
- SNES and Genesis 224 lines: k=3, 896x672 (SNES 8:7 pixel aspect) or 960x672.
- NES 240 lines: 960x720.
- Game Boy 144 lines: k=5, 800x720.
- GBA 160 lines: k=4, 960x640.
- Atari 2600: whatever EJS reports; the same integer rule applies.

Hi-res modes: SNES 512/448 lines, or N64 variable resolution. When nh changes mid-game, recompute k and contain into the fixed 1280x720 output. The encoder never restarts.

FRAME RATE: 60 fps, not 30. The sink fires once per emulated frame, so capture follows the core's native 60 Hz and only decimates above 60 (for example a 120 Hz rAF). Scrolling shooters and platformers look choppy at 30.

BITRATE: 3 Mbps hint. Flat palettes compress well, but the sharp nearest-neighbor edges need bits.

games.audio:
SOURCE: EmulatorJS plays through Emscripten OpenAL in its OWN AudioContext inside the iframe realm. Keep that playback path untouched (zero-risk).

TAP POINT: Module.AL.currentCtx.gain. In Emscripten's OpenAL, alcCreateContext makes a context gain connected to ac.destination (github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/blob/main/src/lib/libopenal.js, `var gain = ac.createGain(); gain.connect(ac.destination)`, ~:2156-2157). EVERY source's gain connects to AL.currentCtx.gain (alGenSources, ~:2760-2761). So tapping ctx.gain catches all current AND future sources, post EJS volume slider. The slider sets source gains (ejs-emulator.js:2039-2043), so a muted emulator records silence, which is what the kid heard.

WHY NOT EJS's HELPER: this is better than EJS's collectScreenRecordingMediaTracks (ejs-emulator.js:6031-6071). That helper merges only the sources that exist at call time, through a ChannelMerger that downmixes each source to one channel.

TAP MECHANICS: kit.attachForeignTap(AL.currentCtx.gain, win). The worklet module must be a same-origin URL. The /emulator CSP script-src includes 'self' and blob:, but see groupNotes for the main-route rule. Build the node with win.AudioWorkletNode and transfer its port to the encoder worker. Map the clock with getOutputTimestamp() plus the timeOrigin delta.

RESUME: Emscripten auto-resumes on keydown, mousedown or touchstart (libcore.js autoResumeAudioContext, ~:1817-1825), and EJS shows a 'Click to resume Emulator' popup (ejs-emulator.js:1038-1055). While the context is suspended the tap is silent and the kit zero-fills.

Cues (all synthesized, no assets, variation seeded by entry.seq): move -> 'slide' 60 ms band-passed noise swish (1.2 kHz, gain .15); merge -> one 'pop' per move at the largest merged value, f = 330*1.12^(log2(v)-1) Hz sine+triangle 90 ms (4 -> 370 Hz, 2048 -> ~1025 Hz); spawn -> soft 20 ms tick; win -> C5-E5-G5-C6 arpeggio 90 ms steps; game over -> G4-E4-C4 triangle descend; undo -> reversed swish; newHighScore crossing -> 2-ping sparkle (1.3/1.9 kHz).
