groupNotes:
GROUP: arkanoid, asteroids, blitz-bomber, bomberman, breakout, dino-runner, endless-runner. All seven games are single Canvas2D surfaces that are always mounted. There are no second canvases, no key-remounts, no WebGL and no DOM replay, so preserveDrawingBuffer and replay do not apply. Two games (arkanoid, bomberman) keep their HUD and result screens in the DOM and need kit-painted overlays. The other five paint the HUD and result cards into the canvas.

VERIFIED LIVE ON hankshits.com, 2026-09-27 (Playwright, canvas-call instrumentation, rAF 121/s on a 120 Hz Mac):
(1) Blitz-bomber, dino-runner and endless-runner update only on every other frame, at half the designed speed:
- Blitz: plane on 60 of 121 frames, 89 px/s against a designed 180.
- Dino: score 3 in 0.9 s against about 5.4.
- Endless: 15.5 m/s against about 30.
- Motion steps at half the display rate, so any clip judders.
(2) Bomberman keyboard hold-to-move is dead. The player stayed on tile (1,1) through 0.7-1.2 s holds of ArrowRight and ArrowDown while playing.
Root cause, one sentence: the game loops are React effects whose dependencies change on every store update, so the rAF loop is torn down every frame and loses its timers (the dt skip-frame reset, moveTimer).
Class fix, required for this group: shared/hooks/useGameLoop(cb, { running, fixedStepMs?, maxDtMs = 50, timeScale }). It has one rAF chain per mount, the callback in a ref, state read through getState(), and a dt clamp. It exposes onAfterRender, so the clip kit captures exactly post-render.
- Frame-stepped simulations (asteroids, breakout) use fixedStepMs 1000/60. This also fixes today's 2x speed on 120 Hz screens.
- Blitz, dino and endless keep today's feel with timeScale 0.5. Jack decides whether to restore the designed 1.0; this is a gameplay feel choice, not the spec's.
Not yet filed as issues. Bomberman's keyboard is a real playability bug for desktop kids.

WHAT THE SHARED KIT MUST SUPPORT FOR THIS GROUP:
(a) useClipSource(appId, cfg). It keeps cfg in a ref and registers once per canvas element. All seven components re-render every frame because they subscribe with no selector, so registration must never churn. It reads canvas() on every tick and tolerates source-size changes (arkanoid rotation) by re-fitting and inserting a cut. It needs:
- phase(): 'menu' | 'playing' | 'paused' | 'interstitial' | 'result'. The store is the only reliable pause signal: asteroids and bomberman have in-game pause buttons that bypass GameShell, and dino and endless have canPause=false.
- hud() for the title, end and story cards.
- Optional paintHud/paintResult. These read store state only and never rasterize the DOM.
- A layout with gameRect and band colors, and an fps hint.
(b) Result-freeze. Keep sampling while phase==='result' or 'interstitial'. If the phase leaves before a 2.5 s post-roll ends (instant restart), finish the post-roll from the last result frame, copied into a freeze canvas with drawImage every tick. For games whose loop stops outside 'playing' (arkanoid, asteroids), repeat the last frame.
(c) A pause-on-document.hidden rule plus a cut marker, for canPause=false games.
(d) A non-React emitter, clipEvents.emit(appId, event), callable from zustand stores and a no-op when no kit is mounted. Also a createRunBrag helper with start(prevBest), score(n) (newHighScore fires once per run on the first crossing of bestAtRunStart, and only when bestAtRunStart > 0), tier(n) (once per tier per run), end(score) (strict greater-than, returns isNewBest) and raiseBest(n) (a mid-run cloud sync raises the snapshot).
Why the snapshot rule matters: breakout (store.ts:828) and blitz (store.ts:362) bump progress.highScore mid-run, and dino and bomberman compute the flag after maxing. So 'compare against the previous best' only works against the snapshot.
Event weights: 'highlight' auto-saves, 'marker' only chapters the ring.
Types: runStart, runAbort, cut, newHighScore, levelClear, win, combo, milestone, bonus, runEnd.
The achievements poll (useAuthSync.ts:424-436, evaluate.ts:115-121) is a lagging fallback for kid-made games only. It is up to 1 s late and silent on first scores.
(e) shared/lib/gameAudio:
- One AudioContext, per-app input gains, a per-app speaker mute (setSpeakerMuted), a master DynamicsCompressor and limiter, and a record tap taken before the speaker gain. Clips keep game sound when a kid mutes the speakers, and the editor has its own 'Game sounds' switch.
- voice(appId, key, {maxPerSec}) caps voices. Arkanoid chains, breakout multi-ball and bomberman bomb chains fire dozens of oscillators per frame.
- startLoop/stopLoop handles sustained voices (asteroids thrust and UFO, blitz engine) and auto-stops them on pause and unmount.
- A capture-phase pointerdown/keydown resume in GameShell. WebKit documents Web Audio as using sticky activation (webkit.org/blog/13862/the-user-activation-api), but a central resume also covers older iOS and contexts first created inside rAF, which is what asteroids, bomberman and breakout do today.
- Keep the default 'ambient' session. Do NOT set navigator.audioSession.type='playback': it bypasses the ringer switch (bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=237322; MDN AudioSession/type, Safari 16.4). Device-test whether the record tap still receives samples with the ringer switch on.
- Every SFX in this group is mono oscillator or noise synthesis, so mono capture loses nothing.
(f) Codec and sizes:
- Use H.264 Level 4.0 (for example avc1.640028). Level 3.1 caps 1280x720 at 30 fps (MaxFS 3,600 MBs, 108,000 MB/s), and 720p60 needs Level 3.2 or higher (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Video_Coding, levels table).
- Output sizes stay at or under 921,600 px, with even sides and multiples of 16 where possible: asteroids 960x960, blitz 1024x768, bomberman 936x900, breakout 720x960, dino 1280x720, endless 1280x720, arkanoid 720x1280 or 1280x720.
- The six fixed-size games get a shared useCanvasBackingScale plus ctx.setTransform(S,...) at the start of render, so the compositor draws 1:1 with no resampling. Crisp HUD text also sharpens today's CSS-upscaled on-screen canvases on retina phones.
- Nothing in these games reads canvas.width except arkanoid (grep verified), and arkanoid already renders at DPR. None of these games use bitmap sprites, so nearest-neighbour upscaling is not the right tool here. Keep imageSmoothingEnabled=false only for future pixel-sprite games that declare pixelArt:true.
- Adaptive fps: 60 for fast games, 30 for bomberman, and a drop to 30 when the encoder queue grows.
(g) The result share chip must be DOM, outside the canvas click path, with stopPropagation. In five games a canvas tap or Space restarts. Put the chip above z-50 (bomberman's fixed modals) and below the GameShell header (z-1000). It must also clear the IOSInstallPrompt bottom sheet, using the useStartOverlayPresence pattern from lessons.md. Dino and endless have no pause menu, so the 'Clip it!' entry cannot live only in PauseMenu.
(h) A shared result-input lockout helper: ignore e.repeat and use a 600 ms tap/key lockout after runEnd or an interstitial. Every game in the group needs it.

CROSS-CUTTING PERF, needed for recording headroom on low-end phones:
- Zustand persist 5.0.14 writes storage on EVERY set() (apps/web/node_modules/zustand/esm/middleware.mjs:358-373). All seven stores call set() at least once per frame, which is 60-120 synchronous localStorage writes per second.
- Fix the class with a deduped storage wrapper in shared/lib (cache the last serialized string per key), and stop the per-frame lastModified bumps in bomberman (store.ts:795) and breakout (store.ts:869).
- Narrow the whole-store subscriptions where the kit bench shows frame time over 16.7 ms p95 while recording.

TESTS, KIT LEVEL:
- A shared src/__tests__/canvas2d-mock.ts (a recording 2D-context mock). jsdom returns null for '2d', and setup.ts only mocks WebGL.
- A fake-rAF driver for useGameLoop tests.
- A Playwright clip smoke per game against a local build: MP4 dims, fps, non-blank frames, non-zero audio RMS, ends on the result frame. Run it on a quiet machine, per lessons.md.

FILE AS ISSUES (pre-existing, not clip-blocking):
- Breakout power-up timers use wall-clock time through pause (store.ts:462-474, :747-761).
- Bomberman shows two pause UIs at once (the GameShell menu over the game's own PAUSED modal, Game.tsx:393-409).
- Blitz counts gamesPlayed on every landing (store.ts:366).
- Bomberman keyboard: fixed by this spec, but file it so it is tracked.

EFFORT: about 98.5 expert hours for the seven per-game integrations. That covers the prerequisite fixes, new SFX, sound controls and tests. It excludes the shared kit, useGameLoop (about 4 h), useCanvasBackingScale (about 1 h), createRunBrag (about 2 h) and the gameAudio bus, which belong to the kit budget.

MAKE-A-GAME SKILL: once the kit ships, the template should wire useGameLoop, useClipSource, createRunBrag and gameAudio by default, so kid-built games get clips without per-game work.

GROUP 7: flappy-bird, hextris, hill-climb, math-attack, oregon-trail, platformer, space-invaders. All seven draw with Canvas2D; none uses WebGL, R3F or an iframe. Oregon Trail is the only hybrid: a live canvas hunt plus an offline journey recap. Total expert effort is about 124.5 h on top of the shared kit.

1) EVIDENCE FROM THIS PASS
All tests ran against prod https://hankshits.com, Playwright 1.62 Chromium, read-only play. Scripts and raw outputs are in /tmp/hh-clips/g7/.
- Loops (verify-loops.js -> loops.out): the loop re-arms every frame, so the simulation steps every other frame.
  - flappy: 57.4 cancelAnimationFrame calls/s at 114.8 fps.
  - platformer: 57.9 at 116.6.
  - space-invaders: 59.9 at 119.7.
  - Consequence: platformer Level 1 took 11,534 ms of wall time, but the stored bestTime was 5,862 ms. The platformer timer runs at half speed.
- Space Invaders AudioContext: 'suspended' at load, 'running' only after the first gesture.
- Input (verify-input.js -> input.out):
  - Oregon hunt: 3 on-screen animals were gone after ONE mouse move.
  - Hextris: one phone tap = 2 rotations (targetRotation 2.094 rad).
- Space Invaders controls (verify-si.js -> si.out): the Move-left DOM node is replaced within 100 ms, and a 1 s hold moved the cannon 5 px.
- Also from si.out: during play, the iOS 'Play Fullscreen!' prompt covered the Space Invaders Move-left button in iPhone emulation (hit-test landed on the prompt). IOSInstallPrompt.tsx:48-53 hides only while the start card shows, so it slides up, fixed at the bottom with z-[200], the moment play starts.
- Layout (verify-layout.js -> layout.out): the hill-climb and hunt canvases are innerWidth x innerHeight starting at y=56/48, so 56/48 px sit below the fold. The backing store is 1x even at DPR 3.
- Hunt effects (verify-hunt-fx.js -> huntfx.out): none of 8 screenshots showed the hunt's bullet hole.

2) WHAT THE SHARED KIT MUST SUPPORT FOR THIS GROUP
(a) useClipSource options:
- { gameId, sourceId?, canvasRef, active?, layout: 'portrait' | 'landscape' | 'auto', fit?: 'contain' | 'width', pixelated?, getHud, paintHud, endCard? }.
- canvasRef.current is re-read on every tick. Math Attack mounts a new canvas every run; hill-climb remounts through a key change and through the Garage.
- A null or inactive source holds the last frame.
- Registrations are keyed by gameId, so a remount continues the same ring buffer.
(b) Data and painter contracts:
- getHud() returns plain, serializable data and is sampled once per compositor frame.
- paintHud(ctx, hud, rects) and endCard(ctx, info, rects, tMs) are pure functions.
- rects = { frame, game, top, bottom, orientation }.
- Store the HUD snapshots as a side track, so export can re-lay the overlay for portrait or landscape.
(c) Module-level clipEvents, importable from zustand stores (no React, no-op in SSR and jsdom). This mirrors the Steam Timeline model of game modes plus prioritized timed events (https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/timeline):
- runStart, runEnd, phase('playing' | 'paused' | 'menu').
- mark({ kind, title, detail?, priority: 'standard' | 'featured', preMs?, postMs?, dedupe? }).
(d) Pause must be driven by store phase, not by the shell's isPaused. Hextris's in-game 'II' button and Space Invaders' mobile PAUSE button call store.pauseGame directly, and hill-climb and math-attack disable the shell pause.
(e) A post-roll ends at the next runStart. There is a minimum end-card hold: when a restart cuts the post-roll, freeze-extend the last frame to at least 1.5 s.
(f) A shared hi-DPI helper (backing = logical x min(dpr, 2), plus a per-frame setTransform). None of the 7 canvases uses DPR today.
(g) A shared audio bus in shared/audio:
- getGameAudio() returns { ctx, input } or null.
- Master chain: a DynamicsCompressor limiter, then master gain, which feeds both the destination and the recorder tap.
- resume() on the first pointerdown/keydown capture listener. The MDN Autoplay guide says contexts created without a gesture start suspended; WebKit gives no auto-resume.
- sfx helpers (tone, noise, arp, loop) that accept any BaseAudioContext plus a destination, so the Oregon recap and the DOM-replay games can render the same sounds with OfflineAudioContext.
- A global sound preference with a shared SoundToggle on GameStartOverlay and PauseMenu. Flappy, Platformer and Oregon have no settings UI; per-game soundEnabled gates stay in hextris, space-invaders, hill-climb and math-attack.
(h) An offline composition mode, used for the Oregon recap: explicit-timestamp frames plus OfflineAudioContext audio.
(i) Canvas text in the bands must use the loaded font. next/font renames Nunito, so read getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily and await document.fonts.ready.
(j) Clip UI placement:
- The header is full.
- Hill-climb's window touch zones claim every touch unless the target is filtered.
- The iOS install prompt currently slides up, fixed at the bottom, the moment play starts. Restrict it to non-play moments, or the clip bar and the game controls are covered.

3) CLASS DEFECTS FOUND (fix the class, not the instance)
(i) React registers touchstart as passive (react-dom-client.development.js:19251-19262 in the repo's React 19.2.3), so onTouchStart plus onClick double-fires through the W3C Touch Events §9 compatibility click (https://w3c.github.io/touch-events/). Instances: hextris Game.tsx:427-428 (verified), space-invaders Game.tsx:998-1004, oregon Hunting.tsx:542-543. Fix: a single onPointerDown, the flappy/platformer precedent.
(ii) Components defined inside components are remounted every render (https://react.dev/learn/preserving-and-resetting-state). Instances: space-invaders Game.tsx:755, 899, 948 (verified).
(iii) rAF effects keyed on per-render callbacks that reset lastTime:
- Oregon hunt: catastrophic, wipes the animals (verified).
- platformer: half-speed timer (verified).
- flappy and space-invaders: sim at half the frame rate. Harmless for clips because the canvas repaints every frame.
(iv) Movement per update instead of per dt, which ties difficulty to the display refresh rate: hextris store.ts:369-370 and 495-498; space-invaders store.ts:384, 394, 469 and 713 (bullets, alien fire chance, UFO). On 120 Hz Android these games run twice as hard.
(v) No DPR on any canvas.
(vi) New-best checks made after the write are true on a tie: hill-climb GameOverScreen.tsx:28, math-attack Game.tsx:380, space-invaders Game.tsx:534. Standard fix: a pre-write flag plus a bestAtRunStart snapshot, maxed with mid-run cloud setProgress.

4) PRE-EXISTING, NOT CLIP-RELATED: file as issues with evidence (PR-scope carve-out)
- Space Invaders keyboard movement and auto-fire run per loop frame (Game.tsx:634-648), so the cannon is 2x faster on 120/144 Hz monitors. This is the re-arm class plus (iv).
- Platformer totalStars adds starsThisRun on every completion (store.ts:607), and the leaderboard ranks by totalStars (leaderboard-extractors.ts:282-292). Replaying level 1 farms leaderboard score.
- The iOS install prompt covers bottom controls during play in every game with bottom controls (shared IOSInstallPrompt.tsx:48-53).

5) PRIVACY RULES FOR OVERLAYS
- Never rasterize DOM.
- Show only the leaderboard handle.
- Never paint age-named difficulty labels (math-attack DIFFICULTY_SETTINGS labels 'N years old', space-invaders age picker). Use speed stars.
- Oregon: no leaderName or party names anywhere, including the journey log. Party members appear only as a count.
- Keep the Oregon hunting audio cartoony (cork pop, boing).

6) SOURCES
- The file:line reads above (repo HEAD 20d56b1).
- W3C Touch Events: https://w3c.github.io/touch-events/
- react.dev Preserving and Resetting State: https://react.dev/learn/preserving-and-resetting-state
- MDN Autoplay guide: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Autoplay
- MDN Web Audio best practices: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Audio_API/Best_practices
- Steam Timelines: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/timeline
- Measurement scripts and outputs: /tmp/hh-clips/g7/

These notes cover the whole group (monster-truck, four-wheeler-3d, four-wheeler-adventure, retro-arcade). They list what the shared kit (apps/web/src/shared/clips) MUST support. Every item was checked against source code or a primary spec on 2026-09-27.

1. Sources push frames; the kit does not pull them.
- None of these four games can be captured from the kit's own rAF.
- R3F games push from addAfterEffect, which runs after all roots render in the same task (R3F 9.6.1 events-b389eeca.esm.js:16071-16100). useFrame runs before the render.
- EmulatorJS pushes from a microtask queued by the first default-framebuffer draw in a task.
- The adventure pushes from the iframe's own rAF.
- The HTML "update the rendering" step runs a child document's rAF callbacks after its container's (html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html). A parent-rAF read of the emulator's preserveDrawingBuffer:false canvas therefore returns the cleared buffer, which is black (WebGL 1.0 spec section 2.2: the buffer is cleared after compositing and only re-presented after a draw).
- Contract: source.pushFrame(ts, draw), where draw() runs synchronously inside that call and paints the source into the compositor. The kit decimates to the source fps and holds the last good frame.

2. iframe realms have their own clocks. Convert every iframe timestamp (rAF ts, performance.now, getOutputTimestamp().performanceTime) with (iframeWin.performance.timeOrigin - performance.timeOrigin). Each document has its own time origin (w3c.github.io/hr-time). Without this, A/V sync and brag timestamps drift by the iframe's load offset.

3. Output size is fixed for the whole session; the source rect may change.
- Games change size mid-session: canvas resize at adventure index.html:668, DPR changes, rotation, emulator hi-res modes.
- Remounts happen: keyed restarts in all four games, and a new iframe per emulator session.
- The compositor's output stays fixed. It recomputes the source rect each frame and hot-swaps sources, forcing a keyframe without resetting the ring. An encoder restart per resize is the wrong design.
- Fit rule 'auto': cover within ±20% of 16:9, otherwise contain, with the bars used as the HUD strip.
- The R3F games need cropTop:'shell-header', because their canvases are fixed inset-0 under the 48/56px header.
- Per-source fps and bitrate hints are needed: 30 fps / 4 Mbps for 3D, 30 / 3 for the 2D iframe, 60 / 3 for retro.
- Pixel-art sources need a nearest-neighbor path plus a "native recovery" intermediate canvas.

4. idle() predicate per source. The kit stops appending video and audio while idle and collapses the gap. Gaps are start screens, pause menus, menu panels (except four-wheeler-3d's 'fishing'), EJS menus, and document.hidden.
- The shared overlays that cover a game should publish presence the way shared/lib/startOverlayPresence.ts does: OrientationWarning, RestartConfirmationDialog, LeaderboardModal and IOSInstallPrompt. The kit idles while any is up.
- R3F games render every frame even while paused, so idle() is the only thing that keeps pause screens out of replays.

5. HUD and brag UI are painted by the kit, never rasterized from the DOM.
- Use a declarative HUD model: chips (icon, text, color), an optional gauge (value, max, redline), an optional race panel and countdown, and an escape-hatch paintExtra(ctx, frameRect, scale) for things like copying the adventure's #speedo canvas.
- Paint from getState() values with memoized strings, so no per-frame allocations.
- Banners are driven by brag events, and there are end-card and result-card templates.
- Emoji in fillText depend on OS fonts; that is fine on iOS, Android, ChromeOS and macOS.
- The kit's own UI must follow the no-slop rules: no gradients, glows or colored edge stripes.

6. Brag events.
- Module-level clips.emit({appId, type, priority, title, payload}), callable from useFrame and store actions without React.
- Priority 2 or higher auto-saves a highlight: pre-roll 8s, post-roll 2s, plus a result card when the game freezes on the moment (four-wheeler-3d race finish).
- Priority 1 drops a replay marker only. The kit coalesces events within 1s.
- Rising-edge detection stays in the game and must compare against the value read BEFORE the write. Never subscribe to persisted fields: cloud hydration (useAuthSync -> setProgress) and persist rehydrate flip them too (monster-truck challenges).
- iframe games baseline on the first probe after every load.

7. Audio.
- The class defect: no game here has a tappable output. monster-truck has 11 ctx.destination sites. four-wheeler-3d has 4 AudioContexts and closes 3 of them. The adventure's one-shots bypass its master. EJS uses its own context.
- Shared in-page context: getGameAudio(){ctx, channel(name), unlock()}, never closed, with a master gain feeding destination plus an AudioWorklet tap.
- unlock() must run synchronously inside a gesture handler: a document-level capture listener for pointerdown, touchend and keydown, plus a call in GameStartOverlay's click. It must not run from a React effect. monster-truck's current first-click resume fires before its context exists, then removes itself (Game.tsx:136-149).
- Foreign-realm taps: attachForeignTap(node, realmWin) installs the SAME worklet in another realm's context. Construct it with realmWin.AudioWorkletNode, transfer the port to the encoder worker, and map clocks per item 2. AudioWorklet, AudioWorkletNode.port and getOutputTimestamp are all Safari 14.1+ (mdn/browser-compat-data api/*.json). Zero-fill whenever a tap is suspended, silent or dead (its realm unloaded).
- CSP: an AudioWorklet module fetch is governed by script-src-elem, falling back to script-src (w3.org/TR/CSP3, "Get the effective directive": audioworklet -> script-src-elem). The main-route script-src (next.config.ts:35) has no blob:, so the worklet MUST be a same-origin file, e.g. new URL('./tap.worklet.js', import.meta.url), never a blob URL. srcdoc iframes inherit the parent CSP; /emulator has its own CSP, which allows 'self' and blob:.
- Add a class-level guard test: no 'new AudioContext', 'webkitAudioContext' or '.destination' under src/games/** except through the kit. Static iframe games (public/games/**) are covered by preludes.

8. iframe helpers the kit should own.
- injectPrelude(html, script), which puts the script as the first child of head and fails loudly otherwise.
- Realm disposal on iframe swap.
- restoreFocus after any kit UI closes. Both iframe games lose keyboard control when a header button takes focus.
- The kit's keyboard shortcut must avoid every game's bindings. The adventure alone uses WASD, arrows, Space, B, C, E, F, G, M, N, O, P, R and T. iframe games forward the key from their prelude.
- Invariant tests that neither game iframe gains a sandbox attribute.

9. Shell placement. All four games pass canPause={false} (monster-truck/GameShell.tsx:22, four-wheeler-3d/GameShell.tsx:29, the adventure page.tsx:36, retro page.tsx:30). The shared PauseMenu never mounts, so the Clip control must live in the header right cluster. It must never go before the title, because four-wheeler-3d/adventure.css:917 targets nth-child(2). The retro route lacks appId.

10. Memory and performance on phones.
- Encode from a ≤1280x720 compositor, never the DPR canvas. The spike measured Monster Truck at 41 fps idle, 4-6 fps recording the raw canvas, and about 34 fps through a 960-wide compositor.
- Default the iOS ring to 30s for the two 3D games. Four-wheeler-3d is the heaviest scene.
- Adapt fps down (30 to 24) when the game's own rAF interval degrades.

11. Pre-existing defects found while reading. Classify them per the PR-scope rule; items (c) and (e) are one-liners.
(a) monster-truck flip detector wraps at ±π and credits false flips (Vehicle.tsx:138-139).
(b) monster-truck triple horn that ignores soundEnabled (Game.tsx:124-126, MobileControls.tsx:86-91, Vehicle.tsx:316-327). Merges with #18i.
(c) monster-truck start hint says Shift boosts, but Shift brakes (Game.tsx:232 vs useControls.ts:84-90).
(d) monster-truck pause does not pause physics (Game.tsx:74).
(e) monster-truck dead music toggle, and an engine sound that is never started.
(f) Likely silent on iOS: monster-truck, whose context is created outside a gesture and never resumed, and the adventure, which never calls resume(). Both need real-iPhone confirmation.
(g) retro EmulatorView's Exit bar is hidden under the GameShell header (Game.tsx:274-295).
(h) retro 'ready' accepts any same-origin window (Game.tsx:211).
(i) four-wheeler-3d Photos saves via <a download> of a data: URL (PhonePanel.tsx:861), which lands in Files, not Photos, on iOS.

12. Owner decisions (my proposals, not settled policy): whether retro-arcade clips may use the hosted /c/ link path (issue #25i gory titles, plus commercial-ROM footage on our domain), and nothing else. Hunting in four-wheeler-3d and the adventure is existing game content that matches Hank's stated interests; I add no restriction there. I deliberately exclude the adventure's casino wins from auto-clips as a design choice; flag it if the owner disagrees.

13. QA matrix for this group:
- real iPhone on iOS 26 (AudioEncoder present) and iOS 17/18 (fallback audio path)
- a mid-range Android on Chrome
- a school Chromebook
- desktop at 60 Hz and 120 Hz; the 120 Hz case exercises the EJS decimation and dirty gate
Each run records a 30s instant replay per game and checks decode, the frame-luma floor, HUD presence and audio RMS.

14. Effort totals for this group (expert hours, on top of the shared kit): monster-truck 41, four-wheeler-3d 32, four-wheeler-adventure 34, retro-arcade 26. That is about 133h. It is dominated by the audio-bus migrations, the sound effects that were never there (engine, music, celebrations), and truthful brag detection (the flip wrap fix and persisted records).

GROUP VERDICT: all 8 are pure React DOM (re-verified in code; live prod probe at 390x844 DPR3 found no canvas). No phone API can capture DOM pixels, so every one is a `dom-replay` source: the game appends a tiny event log, and the clip is RE-RENDERED into a canvas and encoded after the fact. That beats a live compositor for this group on every axis. Steady-state cost while playing is ~0 (no painting or encoding, so no fps or battery hit on Chromebooks). Frames are exact. Portrait and landscape are re-rendered, not cropped, so the editor toggle, trim, slow-mo and idle-compression are instant and cost nothing until export. My Clips can store replay docs of a few KB instead of MP4s.

SHARED KIT MUST SUPPORT (apps/web/src/shared/clips/replay):
1) createReplayLog<S,E>({appId, clock:'tick'|'game'|'wall', keyframeEvery:'event'|'round'|{ms}|{ticks}, reduce?, ringMs(default 90000)}) with round(key, meta) / append(ev, keyAfter?) / slice(from,to) (always self-contained: starts at a keyframe) / subscribe / clearSession. The ring is time-based on the post-retiming timeline and never drops data inside a requested window. Record mode marks a range and streams to OPFS every 10 s (cookie-clicker is the only one that grows past about 100 KB/10 min).
2) useClipReplaySource(source, {active}): registers with the GameShell ClipProvider. It is idempotent under StrictMode, emits a resume keyframe on active false->true, and clears the session on unmount unless a highlight render is pending. Hooks must be called above early returns (memory-match Game.tsx:382).
3) Offline render pipeline: render on the main thread with backpressure-yielding. The DOM paint is 1-3 ms/frame, the fonts and emoji are identical to the page, and it avoids WorkerGlobalScope.fonts plus next/font URL plumbing. Frames come from mediabunny CanvasSource.add(timestamp, duration) with explicit timestamps (faster than real time, promise backpressure: https://mediabunny.dev/guide/media-sources#backpressure). 30 fps by default, 60 fps for snake. The editor preview draws frames live from the log (no encode). The Share button enables only after the File is finalized (transient activation).
4) Timeline retimer: idle-gap compression and slow-mo windows produce a time map applied to both video frames and audio cues. Presets: 'last N s' (applied AFTER compression, so turn-based games get more action), 'whole round', and brag highlight (pre/post roll).
5) Audio for replay sources = cue re-synthesis, not a PCM ring. SFX voices are pure functions (ctx: BaseAudioContext, dest, when, params) that run live on the shared bus and in an OfflineAudioContext (Safari 14.1+, MDN BCD api/OfflineAudioContext). The result goes to mediabunny AudioBufferSource (https://mediabunny.dev/guide/media-sources#audiobuffersource), so mediabunny's AAC path and its WebKit-302253 fix apply. Variation is seeded by entry.seq. One deterministic voice limiter is shared live/offline. There is a persisted global mute, plus per-game soundEnabled gating where the field exists (snake, memory-match, cookie-clicker, wordle all carry DEAD soundEnabled fields today, the same class as issue #24; progress-schemas already declare them, so keep the fields and wire them). Never route speechSynthesis read-aloud into clips.
6) Render kit: portrait 720x1280 / landscape 1280x720 frames, brand bar, handle chip (gaming_profiles.handle only, none for guests), HUD pill primitives, result/title cards, brag banner.
   - Emoji: an emoji sprite cache rasterized at <=128 px with a blank-pixel check. Skia historically dropped emoji above ~256 px on Android: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50965784. Desktop Chrome 153 drew 512 px fine in my probe. The sprite also caps memory.
   - Font: resolve with getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily (prod computes 'Nunito, "Nunito Fallback"') plus document.fonts.load per weight before frame 0.
   - Palette: Tailwind v4 tokens are oklch and partly P3 (node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css). Ship precomputed sRGB hex via a gamut-mapped converter (e.g. green-800 #016630, amber-600 #da7700, blue-500 #3280ff) instead of parsing oklch in canvas; Chrome parses it but canvas is sRGB and Safari parse behavior is unverified.
   - Easing library matching CSS ease/ease-out/ease-in-out and Tailwind bounce/pulse/ping.
   - Avoid ctx.filter (Safari 18+) and letterSpacing (Safari 18.4+); roundRect is fine (Safari 16), per MDN BCD. The VideoFrame baseline is Safari 16.4.
7) Chess pieces: compile react-chessboard's exported defaultPieces (svg/g/path/circle + one matrix transform) to Path2D. This means no image decode, no taint risk, and worker-safe. Plain SVG data URLs do not taint modern Safari either (only iOS 10.3-11.2 did: https://github.com/niklasvh/html2canvas/pull/2683), but Path2D removes the question.
8) Brag pipeline: pure brags(entry, round) per source. Baselines travel in the round meta as primitives, because stores mutate their bests before the UI reads them: 2048 store.ts:127, snake :222, memory :195. Dedupe keys are per round. Auto-highlights run only for single-player or vs-AI play; hot-seat modes (chess local, checkers vs-friend, quoridor local) get manual clips and toasts.
9) Extra share actions per source: Wordle 'Share squares' (text; iOS video share stays files-only) and PNG still cards (cookie-clicker bakery card, wordle squares card). image/png and video/mp4 are both on Chromium's share allowlist (chrome/browser/webshare/share_service_impl.cc:154,166 via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/main/chrome/browser/webshare/share_service_impl.cc).
10) Test infrastructure:
   - RecordingContext2D test double (jsdom has no canvas).
   - Playwright golden-frame harness: the live board element screenshot vs the renderer output for the same state, compared by SSIM. It needs a test-only store hook (window.__hhClipTest in E2E builds only).
   - MP4 verification via mediabunny Input.
   - Seeded Math.random for deterministic runs.
11) Privacy: logs hold only declared game fields and no names. Wordle guesses are dictionary words, and dictionary safety is enforced at the source (see the wordle fixes). Hosted uploads send the MP4, plus optionally the replay doc validated server-side against the same schema.

DISCOVERED DEFECTS OUTSIDE CLIP SCOPE (file as issues with this evidence, or fold into the per-game PRs):
(a) chess, checkers and quoridor pass canPause with no onPause, so AI moves land under the pause menu (chess store.ts:230,268; checkers :188-229; quoridor :202,264-385). Defer AI while paused.
(b) STREAK_ALIASES omits bestWinStreak (shared/lib/achievements/definitions.ts:55-60), so chess, checkers and quoridor never fire streak trophies. This is a one-line fix: do it.
(c) checkers picks the FIRST valid move matching a destination (store.ts:154), so two capture chains ending on the same square are ambiguous to the kid.
(d) checkers types a 'draw' status that is unreachable, and recordWin treats any non-red status as a black win (store.ts:186).

EFFORT: about 177 expert hours across the 8 islands (per-game numbers above: renderer + instrumentation + SFX + brags + fixes + tests + device QA). This excludes the shared kit, which the canvas/R3F/iframe tracks also depend on. Per-game work is 19-27 h, not the feasibility study's 'trivial/small', because every island needs a faithful renderer, real SFX (all 8 are silent today) and the listed correctness fixes.

Scratch evidence: /tmp/hh-clips/dom-probe/layout.cjs and layout.out (read-only prod probe), plus the research files /tmp/hh-clips/emoji-canvas.md, svg-taint.md, mediabunny-sources.md, dom-bcd-api-*.json and dom-ssi.cc.

platform.audioBusMigration:
EVERY AUDIO SOURCE (grep of apps/web/src and apps/web/public, 2026-09-27). There are 12 AudioContext creation sites in first-party modules, 1 in an iframe document, and 1 in EmulatorJS. There is NO 'new Audio(', Howler, Tone, OfflineAudioContext or createMediaElementSource anywhere.
1 games/asteroids/lib/store.ts:181 (lazy singleton 179-186, connects to destination at :195, never calls resume)
2 games/hextris/lib/store.ts:137 (destination :151, no resume)
3 games/breakout/lib/store.ts:225 (destination :239, no resume)
4 games/bomberman/lib/store.ts:264 (destination :278, no resume)
5 games/space-invaders/Game.tsx:39-40 (SoundManager constructor, built at module import time; destination :59 and :95; never resumes, so on Chrome it can stay suspended for the whole session)
6 games/monster-truck/lib/sounds.ts:11 (getContext 9-14; 11 destination connects at :52,80,109,148,171,203,225,251,277,311,342; a click/touchstart resume listener at Game.tsx:136-149)
7 games/four-wheeler-3d/lib/sounds.ts:5-11 defaultFactory (lazy ctx() 38-43; destination :83,167,197; resume :41,:59)
8 games/four-wheeler-3d/lib/radioAudio.ts:65 (a NEW context per radio track; destination :51; close() :26)
9 games/four-wheeler-3d/components/Hunting.tsx:185 (destination :206,:788; close() :146)
10 games/four-wheeler-3d/components/TransportActions.tsx:321 (destination :340; close() :306)
11 apps/drum-machine/lib/store.ts:118-120 (destination :149; resume :125)
12 apps/virtual-pet/lib/store.ts:134 (destination :148, no resume)
13 public/games/four-wheeler-adventure/index.html:1708, inside the srcdoc iframe realm. master gain :1710-1711 carries only the engine; the one-shots at :1631, :5182, :5195, :6044 bypass master; the engineAudio HTMLAudioElement hook is null (:1697, :2057-2061).
14 retro-arcade: the EmulatorJS core loaded from the unpinned CDN 'stable' path (public/emulator/index.html:169, 236-240). Emscripten OpenAL uses Module.AL.currentCtx.audioCtx (feasibility spike).
speechSynthesis (useReadAloud.ts) cannot be routed into Web Audio and stays out of clips by design. Silent modules (no AudioContext at all): arkanoid, blitz-bomber, dino-runner, endless-runner, flappy-bird, platformer, hill-climb, math-attack, snake, 2048, chess, checkers, quoridor, memory-match, wordle, cookie-clicker, oregon-trail. Several of these have dead sound toggles (the make-a-game rule says wire it or delete it), so they must get real sounds or their clips stay silent.

PLAN:
(1) ONE SHARED BUS: apps/web/src/shared/lib/audio/gameAudio.ts. It lazily creates one AudioContext on the first unlock. Graph: per-module channel GainNodes -> master GainNode -> limiter DynamicsCompressorNode -> ctx.destination. Also master -> AudioWorkletNode('pcm-tap') -> zero-gain -> destination; the zero-gain keeps the tap pulled on Safari. The limiter is needed because summing sounds that used to be separate contexts can clip. API: getGameAudio() returns { context: BaseAudioContext, channel(appId): { input: GainNode, dispose() }, unlock(), state, onStateChange }. The context is typed as BaseAudioContext, which has no close()/suspend(), so TypeScript rejects the fw3d close() pattern. A module leaves by calling channel.dispose(), never by closing the context.
(2) TAP WORKLET is a static same-origin file at apps/web/public/clips/pcm-tap.worklet.js. CSP3 maps audioworklet requests to script-src-elem, which falls back to script-src (w3.org/TR/CSP3 effective-directive table). script-src on normal routes is 'self' ... without blob:, so a blob-URL worklet is blocked. It posts transferable Float32Array chunks (for example 2048 frames) with the render frame index. The main thread maps frames to wall-clock time with ctx.getOutputTimestamp() and performance.timeOrigin+now(). No SharedArrayBuffer: that would need COOP/COEP, which would break the cross-origin EmulatorJS CDN scripts, Cloudflare Insights and Google avatar images.
(3) PER-SITE MIGRATION, 2-3 lines each inside the module's own folder (one-island rule): replace the creation with getGameAudio().context, and replace ctx.destination with the module's channel input. fw3d radio/hunting/transport become channels of the one context, and their close() calls (radioAudio.ts:26, Hunting.tsx:146, TransportActions.tsx:306) become channel.dispose(). space-invaders SoundManager becomes lazy. monster-truck drops its own resume listener. fw3d goes from 4 contexts to 1.
(4) IFRAMES (foreign realms we preserve as-is): add a constructor shim, class extends AudioContext. In its constructor it defines an OWN 'destination' property whose value is a GainNode bus; that bus connects to the real destination and to a pcm-tap worklet in the same context. It then calls parent.__hankClipAudio.attachForeignContext(this, bus). For four-wheeler-adventure, prepend the shim to the srcDoc string the parent already fetches (Game.tsx:69-77), so Hank's HTML file stays byte-identical and the one-shots that bypass master are captured. For retro-arcade, add an inline script in our own public/emulator/index.html before loader.js. This captures all EJS OpenAL sources without depending on EJS internals (collectScreenRecordingMediaTracks) that the floating 'stable' CDN can change. Foreign contexts deliver PCM at their own sampleRate and on their own document time origin, so the clip engine resamples and aligns with performance.timeOrigin.
(5) ENFORCEMENT (fix the class): add an ESLint no-restricted-syntax override for src/games/** and src/apps/** that bans new AudioContext, window.(webkit)AudioContext, .destination and new Audio(, with the message 'Use getGameAudio() from @/shared/lib/audio so clips can hear your game'. Add a vitest scan test: every public/games/**/*.html that mentions AudioContext must be loaded through the shim.
(6) AUTOPLAY UNLOCK: call getGameAudio().unlock() synchronously inside GameStartOverlay handleStart (GameStartOverlay.tsx:138-142). That is every game's Play tap. Call resume() inside the gesture, never after an await. The ClipProvider in GameShell also installs a once-only capture-phase pointerdown/keydown listener, for modules with no start card (drawing-app, drum-machine, the retro-arcade launcher). This fixes the latent silent-audio bugs: space-invaders creates its context at import and never resumes; asteroids, hextris, breakout, bomberman and virtual-pet never resume, so a first sound fired from a timer lands on a suspended context.
(7) iOS AUDIO SESSION: keep navigator.audioSession at its default 'auto'. It exists only in Safari 16.4+ (MDN BCD api/AudioSession.json); Chrome has none. Do not set 'playback': that ignores the silent switch and stops the kid's music. On a statechange to 'suspended' or 'interrupted', re-unlock on the next gesture. While the context is not running, the tap writes silence-gap markers so the muxer can insert silence and keep A/V sync. A physical-iPhone check must confirm that the tap still receives samples with the ringer switch on silent. Consolidating 4 fw3d contexts into 1 also removes the risk of the historic per-page AudioContext limits on iOS.

SOURCE OF TRUTH: apps/web/next.config.ts:13-56. There is no middleware.ts or proxy.ts. Headers merge per key and the last matching rule wins (comment at :11-12).
RULE 1 source '/:path*' (:17-38):
- Permissions-Policy (:29-30): change 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()' to 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), display-capture=(), web-share=(self)'. The default allowlist for display-capture is self (MDN), so this makes 'never capture the screen' structural. The web-share default is also self (MDN); writing it explicitly documents that only the top document shares. The iframes keep allow='autoplay; fullscreen' (four-wheeler-adventure/Game.tsx:111) and 'autoplay; fullscreen; gamepad' (retro-arcade/Game.tsx:313) with NO web-share, because all share UI lives in the parent.
- CSP (:33-35): change ONLY media-src, to "media-src 'self' blob: https://<CLIPS_BUCKET_NAME>.t3.storageapi.dev;". Use the exact virtual-hosted host (Railway docs 'URL style'), not a *.t3.storageapi.dev wildcard, and write it as a literal in next.config because the Dockerfile declares no build ARGs (Dockerfile:1-45), so bucket env is not visible to headers() at build time. The bucket name is not a secret. Leave every other directive as is. img-src 'self' data: https: blob: already covers posters. connect-src 'self' https: covers presigned PUT, multipart UploadPart PUT, XHR upload progress and mediabunny UrlSource reads (code must never fetch a blob: URL, which connect-src forbids). worker-src 'self' blob: covers a static encoder worker AND @mediabunny/aac-encoder, whose dist creates a blob URL + new Worker and WebAssembly.instantiate on ~1 MB of inline wasm (package inspected in /tmp/hh-clips/aacpkg). script-src 'unsafe-eval' already permits WebAssembly (MDN: 'unsafe-eval' overrides 'wasm-unsafe-eval'), and 'self' permits /clips/pcm-tap.worklet.js. Do NOT add blob: to script-src. Do NOT add COOP/COEP (no SharedArrayBuffer).
NEW RULE (append after rule 1, before the emulator rule): { source: '/c/:path*', headers: [{ key: 'X-Robots-Tag', value: 'noindex, nofollow, noarchive' }] }. Use this, NOT a robots.txt Disallow, because Twitterbot and others honor robots.txt and would stop unfurling. /c pages keep X-Frame-Options DENY + frame-ancestors 'none', so there is no iframe twitter:player card. Use a direct-MP4 og:video instead: Apple Messages downloads and auto-plays an og:video MP4 inline, with an associated-resource cap of 10 MB (developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3156-create-rich-previews-for-messages).
Redirect handlers set their own Cache-Control: private, max-age=300. Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin already sends only the origin to the bucket host, so slugs do not leak.
EMULATOR RULE (:41-54) + meta CSP (public/emulator/index.html:7-15): no change needed. Both allow 'self' and 'unsafe-inline' scripts, so the inline AudioContext shim and addModule('/clips/pcm-tap.worklet.js') work. This rule sets no Permissions-Policy, so rule 1's new value applies there too. Optional hygiene in index.html:184-192: add screenRecord { visible:false } to EJS_Buttons so there is exactly one recorder.
FOUR-WHEELER-ADVENTURE srcdoc: no header change. A srcdoc document inherits the parent's CSP (CSP3 section 7: local-scheme documents including srcdoc inherit the source document's policies) and the parent's base URL, so its shim can load the same-origin worklet.
WORKER BUNDLING CONSTRAINT: next is 16.2.9 (apps/web/package.json). Turbopack production builds of 'new Worker(new URL(..., import.meta.url))' crash with 'e.indexOf is not a function' on 16.2.x (vercel/next.js#94015, still reproduced on 16.2.10). The fix is PR #96307, merged 2026-07-28 and first released in 16.3.0 (npm time 2026-08-03; 16.2.12 predates it). So either upgrade Next to >=16.3.x in the same effort, or prebuild the encoder worker with a small esbuild step into public/clips/*.js during 'pnpm build', like the existing generate:metadata step. Both keep worker-src 'self' sufficient.
BUCKET CORS (not a Next header, but the other half of the policy): Railway has no dashboard setting. Configure it with 'aws s3api put-bucket-cors --endpoint-url https://t3.storageapi.dev' (the station.railway.com/questions/cors-error-e073c7c9 answer marked Solved): AllowedOrigins ['https://hankshits.com'], AllowedMethods [GET, HEAD, PUT, POST], AllowedHeaders ['*'], ExposeHeaders ['ETag'] (multipart needs the part ETags), MaxAgeSeconds 3600. Read it back with get-bucket-cors before trusting it. Uploads cost no service egress (docs.railway.com/storage-buckets/uploading-serving).
METADATA: app/layout.tsx:23-42 has no metadataBase or og:image. /c/[slug] generateMetadata builds absolute URLs from the request host, so rebranded clones (site.json) work too.

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE (read-only prod queries under PGOPTIONS default_transaction_read_only=on, 2026-09-27): Postgres 17.11; 9 public tables whose column counts match the Drizzle schema exactly; 4 users, 4 gaming_profiles, 0 opted out of leaderboards, 47 app_progress rows, 25 leaderboard_entries. Table drizzle.__drizzle_migrations DOES NOT EXIST, so the baseline (packages/db/drizzle/0000_overrated_mulholland_black.sql, meta/_journal.json with 1 entry) was applied with db:push or raw SQL, never with 'drizzle-kit migrate'. Running 'drizzle-kit generate' in a scratch copy (/tmp/hh-clips/dbcheck) prints 'No schema changes, nothing to migrate', so the 0000 snapshot is in sync and a new generate emits a purely additive 0001. No migration runs at deploy: railway.toml has build + healthcheck only, and the Dockerfile CMD is 'node apps/web/server.js'.

NEW FILE packages/db/src/schema/clips.ts, exported from schema/index.ts:1-8. It uses the repo's existing conventions: text UUID PKs via crypto.randomUUID, timestamp() without timezone, cascade FKs like leaderboards.ts.
export const gameClips = pgTable('game_clips', {
  id: text('id').primaryKey().$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
  slug: text('slug').notNull().unique(), // 16 base62 chars from crypto.getRandomValues (about 95 bits): unguessable, never sequential (FRAMEWORK_ROADMAP.md:18)
  userId: text('user_id').references(() => users.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }), // null = guest clip
  gamingProfileId: text('gaming_profile_id').references(() => gamingProfiles.id, { onDelete: 'set null' }),
  guestTokenHash: text('guest_token_hash'), // sha256 of the one-time guest owner token
  uploaderIpHash: text('uploader_ip_hash').notNull(), // HMAC-SHA256(CLIPS_IP_PEPPER, ip), quotas only, never a raw IP
  appId: text('app_id').notNull(),
  kind: text('kind').notNull(), // 'replay' | 'highlight' | 'recording'
  status: text('status').notNull().default('uploading'), // 'uploading' | 'ready' | 'hidden' | 'removed'
  titleId: text('title_id').notNull(), // preset phrase id; free text is never stored (typed text = PII doctrine)
  showHandle: boolean('show_handle').notNull().default(true),
  score: bigint('score', { mode: 'number' }), // client-reported, display only, never 'verified'
  scoreLabel: text('score_label'),
  videoKey: text('video_key').notNull(), previewKey: text('preview_key'), posterKey: text('poster_key').notNull(),
  videoBytes: bigint('video_bytes', { mode: 'number' }).notNull(), previewBytes: bigint('preview_bytes', { mode: 'number' }), posterBytes: integer('poster_bytes').notNull(),
  durationMs: integer('duration_ms').notNull(), width: integer('width').notNull(), height: integer('height').notNull(),
  videoCodec: text('video_codec').notNull(), audioCodec: text('audio_codec'),
  multipartUploadId: text('multipart_upload_id'),
  viewCount: integer('view_count').notNull().default(0),
  reportCount: integer('report_count').notNull().default(0),
  hiddenReason: text('hidden_reason'),
  createdAt: timestamp('created_at').notNull().defaultNow(),
  readyAt: timestamp('ready_at'),
  uploadExpiresAt: timestamp('upload_expires_at').notNull(),
  expiresAt: timestamp('expires_at').notNull(), // written retention: 90 days, owner-renewable, shown on the page
}, (t) => [
  index('game_clips_user_created_idx').on(t.userId, t.createdAt),
  index('game_clips_profile_app_score_idx').on(t.gamingProfileId, t.appId, t.score), // leaderboard 'watch the run'
  index('game_clips_status_expires_idx').on(t.status, t.expiresAt), // sweeper
  index('game_clips_ip_created_idx').on(t.uploaderIpHash, t.createdAt), // guest quotas
]);
export const clipReports = pgTable('clip_reports', {
  id: text('id').primaryKey().$defaultFn(() => crypto.randomUUID()),
  clipId: text('clip_id').notNull().references(() => gameClips.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }),
  reporterKey: text('reporter_key').notNull(), // userId or HMAC(ip)
  reason: text('reason').notNull(), // 'mean' | 'personal-info' | 'scary' | 'not-a-game' | 'other'
  createdAt: timestamp('created_at').notNull().defaultNow(),
}, (t) => [unique('clip_reports_once').on(t.clipId, t.reporterKey)]);
Object keys are server-derived and never client-chosen: clips/v1/<clipId>/video.mp4, preview.mp4 (<=8 MB so Apple Messages can inline it), poster.jpg.

LEADERBOARD LINKAGE: no FK on leaderboard_entries. The leaderboard query LEFT JOIN LATERALs the best ready clip for (gaming_profile_id, app_id) through the new index.

ACHIEVEMENTS: no DB change. Clip trophies are ids in the existing synced achievements blob (achievementsSchema at lib/progress-schemas.ts:721-730 accepts any bounded string key). Counters live in local-only achievements watermarks.

VALID_APP_IDS INTERPLAY: do NOT validate clip appIds against VALID_APP_IDS (packages/db/src/schema/app-progress.ts:59-95). 'four-wheeler-adventure' is not in it (it never syncs progress), yet it is a game that needs clips. Validate against the build-time registry GAME_METADATA keys instead (shared/lib/gameMetadata.generated.ts:18, getGameMetadata :289). Add a literal 'clips' field to metadata.ts, parsed by scripts/generate-game-metadata.ts:26-55 and game-registry.ts (same regex-literal rule as madeByKid): default true for games, false for category 'apps' unless it opts in (drawing-app, drum-machine, virtual-pet).

LOCAL LIBRARY (device, not Postgres): IndexedDB database 'hanks-hits-clips' v1, store 'clips' {id, ownerKey ('user:<id>' | 'guest'), appId, kind, createdAt, durationMs, width, height, bytes, titleId, starred, opfsVideo, opfsPoster, hosted?: {clipId, slug, guestToken?, status, expiresAt}}. Media bytes live in OPFS /clips/<id>.mp4 plus the poster. The owner scoping is described in identity.

MIGRATION MECHANISM (the repo's existing way, made safe):
(1) Run 'pnpm --filter @hank-neil/db db:generate' (package.json:16-20) and commit drizzle/0001_*.sql + snapshot as the reviewable artifact.
(2) Apply to prod with 'psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f 0001_*.sql' (all-or-nothing), then verify with '\d+ game_clips', '\d+ clip_reports' and a zero-row count before deploying code. The change is additive, so apply the DDL first and ship the code second. This is a production WRITE and needs Jack's explicit per-action grant.
(3) Never run 'drizzle-kit migrate' against prod unless you first baseline drizzle.__drizzle_migrations with the 0000 hash; otherwise it replays CREATE TABLE on existing tables.
Postgres PITR (bucket postgres-pitr-a4nmqurghp0) keeps deleted rows for the PITR window. State that in the written retention policy.
platform.apiRoutes:
SERVER MODULES (new, apps/web/src/lib/clips/):
- bucket.ts: SigV4 client. Recommend aws4fetch (MIT, 0 deps) over @aws-sdk v3 to minimize supply-chain surface. The app has no S3 client today (apps/web/package.json). Env: CLIPS_BUCKET, CLIPS_BUCKET_ENDPOINT=https://t3.storageapi.dev, CLIPS_BUCKET_ACCESS_KEY_ID, CLIPS_BUCKET_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, CLIPS_BUCKET_REGION, CLIPS_IP_PEPPER, CLIPS_ADMIN_USER_IDS, CLIPS_STORAGE_BUDGET_GB. Functions: virtual-hosted URL builder; presignPut with signed content-type AND content-length (exact size); presignGet with the signing time bucketed to the hour, so the same URL repeats within the hour and browsers cache it; multipart create/presignUploadPart/complete/abort; head; rangeGet; delete; listPrefix.
- ids.ts: 16-char base62 slug with rejection sampling.
- schemas.ts: Zod .strict() with the bounds style of progress-schemas.ts:16-35.
- quota.ts: DB-backed quotas.
- validate.ts: MP4 check.
- sweeper.ts.
- lib/gaming-profile.ts: extract the race-safe get-or-create handle block from app/api/progress/[appId]/route.ts:287-320 so clips and progress share it.

ROUTES:
1 GET /api/clips/config (public, s-maxage 300) returns {hosting, maxDurationMs, maxBytes, previewMaxBytes}. hosting is false when bucket env is missing (a local dev clone) or the global storage breaker is tripped; the UI then hides 'Get a link' instead of showing a dead button.
2 POST /api/clips (create an upload intent). The session is optional (auth() from lib/auth.ts). Guests are allowed (open sharing for everyone). The body is strict: appId in GAME_METADATA with clips enabled, kind, titleId enum, showHandle, optional score <= MAX_CURRENCY, durationMs, even width/height <= 1920, video {bytes, codec 'avc1.*'}, preview {bytes <= 8 MB}, poster {bytes <= 1 MB, 'image/jpeg' | 'image/webp'}. Check order:
- In-memory burst limiter checkRateLimit('clip-create:'+(userId ?? ipHash), 10, 60000) (lib/rate-limit.ts:48-99, IP from getClientIP :151-175).
- DB quotas, which survive deploys (the in-memory store resets on restart, rate-limit.ts:1-6): live hosted clips per account, creates per day per account or per ipHash for guests, and bytes per owner.
- Global breaker: SUM(bytes) of live rows vs CLIPS_STORAGE_BUDGET_GB.
- Every refusal returns a kid-readable reason. Nothing is dropped silently.
Then insert a row with status 'uploading', upload_expires_at +1 h, expires_at +90 d; call getOrCreateGamingProfile for signed-in users. Response: {clipId, slug, guestToken (guests only, shown once), uploads: {video: PUT url | multipart {uploadId, partSize, partUrls}, preview, poster}}. Clips up to ~20 MB use a single PUT with an XHR progress bar; long recordings use multipart parts for resume. If Tigris ignores the signed content-length (verify), fall back to presigned POST with the content-length-range condition from Railway's own example.
3 POST /api/clips/[id]/complete. Owner only: session.user.id === row.user_id, or header X-Clip-Token whose sha256 matches guest_token_hash (constant-time compare). Steps: for multipart, CompleteMultipartUpload with the client ETags; HEAD each object and require size == declared; ranged GET of the first 512 KB of video.mp4 (the fast-start moov), parsed with mediabunny Input over a BufferSource. Require exactly 1 H.264 video track, at most 1 AAC audio track, duration within 5% of declared, and matching dimensions; check poster magic bytes. On pass: status 'ready', ready_at. On fail: delete the objects and the row, return 422, and write a values-free log (reason code, byte counts, never a URL), following the ROM route's host-only logging (roms route.ts:62-75). Bucket egress is free and ingress costs nothing, so validation is effectively free.
4 GET /api/clips/mine (signed-in) returns own hosted clips with status, views, expiry and a hidden-for-review flag. POST /api/clips/status {items:[{id, token}] <= 50} refreshes guest-held links.
5 PATCH /api/clips/[id] (owner) {showHandle?, titleId?, renew?:true}. renew sets expires_at = now()+90 d.
6 DELETE /api/clips/[id] (owner) runs DeleteObject for video, preview and poster, then deletes the row (clip_reports cascade). DELETE /api/clips/mine removes all of the owner's links (the parent 'turn it off' path, FRAMEWORK_ROADMAP.md:42).
7 POST /api/clips/by-slug/[slug]/report (public) {reason}. Limiter checkRateLimit('clip-report:'+ipHash, 10, 3600000). reporterKey = userId or ipHash, unique per clip. A 'personal-info' or 'scary' report hides the clip at once; 2 distinct reports of any reason also hide it. Status becomes 'hidden' and the clip enters the admin queue.
8 POST /api/clips/by-slug/[slug]/view: a beacon after 2 s of playback, limited per ipHash+slug; increments view_count. Kids love view counts.
9 PAGE app/c/[slug]/page.tsx (dynamic server component). The slug must match /^[A-Za-z0-9]{16}$/ (the segment-allowlist idea from roms route.ts:31-40). It serves only status='ready' AND expires_at > now(). generateMetadata sets:
- a generic og:title such as 'A Monster Truck clip on Hank's Hits' (no handle, no name; FRAMEWORK_ROADMAP.md:18),
- og:image = presigned poster (7-day expiry, minted per request),
- og:video and og:video:secure_url = presigned preview.mp4 (7-day expiry, <=8 MB) with og:video:type video/mp4 and width/height,
- twitter:card summary_large_image.
The body has a <video playsInline controls poster> fed by /c/[slug]/video, the handle (a live join that respects show_handle AND show_on_leaderboards), the game name and score, a 'Play <Game>' button to /games/<id> (the brag loop), a ReadAloudButton and a Report button. A hidden, removed or expired clip gets a friendly page with no media (404/410).
10 GET /c/[slug]/video, /poster, /preview (route handlers) return a 302 to a presigned bucket GET. Limiter 120/min/IP (the ROM preset pattern at rate-limit.ts:144-146). The player re-requests on a media error, so an expired signature mid-view heals itself. NEVER proxy the bytes: Cloudflare's non-Enterprise terms bar serving video via the CDN, a proxy costs service egress, and the ROM proxy pattern returns no Range/206 (roms route.ts:120-126), which iOS <video> requires. Presigned GETs come straight from the bucket with free egress (docs.railway.com/storage-buckets/uploading-serving).
11 ADMIN: app/admin/clips/page.tsx + GET/PATCH /api/admin/clips, gated by session.user.id in CLIPS_ADMIN_USER_IDS. Do not gate by email: credentials signup has no email verification (design/SECURITY_BACKLOG.md:84-91), and the old ADMIN_SECRET has no consumer (SECURITY_BACKLOG.md:29). Actions: list hidden/reported clips, restore, remove.
12 SWEEPER (lib/clips/sweeper.ts). Railway buckets do not support lifecycle configuration (docs.railway.com/storage-buckets 'Not yet supported: Bucket lifecycle configuration'), and the service has no cron (railway.toml). So routes 2 and 9 fire 'void maybeSweep()' at most every 15 min, guarded by pg_try_advisory_lock so it is multi-replica safe. It deletes: 'uploading' rows older than 2 h (after AbortMultipartUpload), expired rows, removed rows, and orphans found by ListObjectsV2 on clips/v1/ that have no row after 24 h (orphans come from the user->clips cascade). Correctness never depends on the sweeper, because every read also checks expiry.
REUSED UTILITIES: checkRateLimit rate-limit.ts:48-99; getClientIP :151-175; presets :106-146; the separate in-memory limiter in app/api/profile/route.ts:7-27; the ROM hardening patterns in roms route.ts:20-126 (allowlist, timeout, byte-metering, host-only logs). The redirect allowlist in lib/rom-redirect.ts:10-31 matches only the exact hostnames 't3.storageapi.dev' and 'storage.railway.app' and would reject the virtual-hosted clips bucket, so clips need their own pinned CLIPS host constant.
COST (storage-only): $0.015/GB-month with free API operations and free bucket egress (Railway docs). One 30 s 720p30 H.264 clip at ~2.5 Mbps is ~9.4 MB, plus a <=3 MB preview and ~60 KB poster, so 1,000 hosted clips is about 12.5 GB, about $0.19 per month. Service CPU and egress stay small because only HTML and 302s pass through the app.
platform.identity:
PUBLIC NAME ON CLIPS: only gaming_profiles.handle (packages/db/src/schema/leaderboards.ts:28), the auto-generated kid-safe pseudonym from fixed word pools (lib/handle-generator.ts:77-107). Handle customization stays disabled (app/api/gaming-profile/route.ts:59). Today a handle is created lazily only inside a leaderboard-eligible progress save (progress route.ts:287-320), so a signed-in kid can exist without one. Extract that race-safe block to lib/gaming-profile.ts and call it from POST /api/clips so every signed-in clipper gets a handle.
The page resolves the handle LIVE at view time through a join; it is not snapshotted. So a later opt-out removes the name from every hosted page at once. Pixels are different: the handle is burned into the video end card only when the kid leaves 'Put my gamer name on the video' on in the editor. The default follows show_on_leaderboards.
NEVER users.name: validateDisplayName (lib/validators.ts:12-49) allows real full names, and the header dropdown shows it (LoginButton.tsx:94-95,140-146). Also never users.image or the email. The header avatar is DOM, and the compositor paints only registered canvases, so the avatar can never enter a frame. Add a unit test proving that the end-card and /c page inputs carry no users.* field.
OPT-OUT: show_on_leaderboards (leaderboards.ts:29, default true) governs leaderboards (api/leaderboards/[appId]/route.ts:97-103), the clip page handle, and the end-card default. PRE-EXISTING PARITY GAP: no UI control writes it. Only PATCH /api/gaming-profile (route.ts:61-116) exists, with no client caller. Add a real toggle on the profile, labeled 'Show my gamer name on leaderboards and clips', and render the handle card even when the kid has no ranks (today it renders only inside My Rankings, ProfilePage.tsx:307-330).
GUESTS: guests play fully without an account (GuestWarning.tsx). With open sharing (Jack, 2026-09-27) a guest can also get a hosted link. It is attributed 'A Hank's Hits player' with no handle. Ownership is a per-clip 32-byte base64url guest token, returned once and stored in the local library record; the server keeps only its sha256. Guest quotas key on uploader_ip_hash (HMAC with CLIPS_IP_PEPPER).
LOCAL LIBRARY vs SHARED FAMILY DEVICES: every IndexedDB/OPFS clip carries ownerKey 'user:<id>' or 'guest', and the library, home shelf and /clips list only the current identity's clips. signOutAndClear (lib/auth-client.ts:36-52) clears only localStorage (lib/storage-keys.ts:65-90). It must NOT delete clips: they are device-only until hosted, so deleting them would be silent data loss. Scoping by owner prevents one kid seeing another kid's clips. This matches the fail-closed PROGRESS_OWNER_KEY design (storage-keys.ts:41-55): guest clips never auto-adopt into an account.
The in-memory replay ring is flushed whenever session.user.id changes: sign-in, sign-out, and the foreign-purge reload (shared/hooks/useAuthSync.ts:236-266). So kid B can never 'Clip it!' kid A's last 30 seconds. The cross-tab SIGNOUT_BROADCAST_KEY reload (useAuthSync.ts:100-110) already destroys other tabs' rings.
Device preferences (replay length, auto-clips on/off, 'always ready' on/off, coach mark seen) use a key such as 'hanks-hits-clip-prefs' that matches no CLEARED_SUFFIXES (storage-keys.ts:82), so they survive sign-out like other device settings. Clip trophy counters live in achievements watermarks under 'achievements-progress', which the '-progress' suffix clears on sign-out (achievements/store.ts:98-104).
OWNER CONTROLS (not a gate): delete one clip, renew one clip, and 'Remove all my clip links' on the profile. A guest deletes from the device that holds the token. Everyone else uses report + takedown.

Railway buckets support no lifecycle rules (docs), and user deletes cascade DB rows but not objects. Expiry and orphan cleanup depend on the app sweeper plus read-time expiry checks; without them storage grows forever.

Bucket CORS can only be set via 'aws s3api put-bucket-cors' (Railway station answer), and whether Tigris enforces a signed Content-Length is unverified. If it does not, a client can upload more bytes than declared. Verify both, and fall back to presigned POST content-length-range plus the HEAD size check at complete.
In-memory limiters reset on every deploy (lib/rate-limit.ts:1-6). With open anonymous hosting, cost-bounding quotas and the global storage breaker MUST be Postgres-backed.

Apple Messages inlines og:video only when page resources total <=10 MB (TN3156). A 30-60 s full clip exceeds that, so a separate <=8 MB preview rendition is required or unfurls fall back to a still image.

Never serve clip bytes through hankshits.com: Cloudflare non-Enterprise terms bar CDN video serving, a proxy costs service egress, and a ROM-style proxy lacks Range/206, which iOS <video> requires. Presigned bucket redirects only.
Presigned GETs expire mid-view on long pauses. The player must re-request /c/<slug>/video on a media error, and og URLs must be minted per request with a multi-day expiry.

Legal lane, flagged but not relitigated: Jack settled open sharing for everyone on 2026-09-27. The amended COPPA Rule has been fully in force since 2026-04-22, the site has no age or parent data, and hosting clips attributed to a persistent handle may be a disclosure question. Written retention (90 days + renew, PITR window) and report/takedown reduce exposure but do not answer it.

PII can enter pixels without mic or camera: oregon-trail typed leader and party names (components/TitleScreen.tsx:47,64), free drawing in drawing-app, and future kid-built games that print typed text. Mitigate with clip overlays that never paint typed text, report + auto-hide on 'personal-info', unlisted links, and no public gallery.

Safari deletes script-written storage after 7 days without interaction unless the site is on the Home Screen (webkit.org/blog/10218), and non-persistent origins can be evicted (webkit.org/blog/14403). Local-only clips can vanish, so request storage.persist() and push Save to Photos or a link.
Sign-out mid-game: unless the replay ring is flushed on every session identity change, the next kid could clip and upload the previous kid's play under their own account.
A mid-play interactive toast would steal taps from games with top-of-screen controls (monster-truck GameUI.tsx:239). Clip toasts must be non-interactive during active play.
Shared-context mixing of foreign iframe contexts needs resampling and time-origin alignment (each iframe document has its own performance.timeOrigin). A naive merge gives drifting audio.

It is unverified on a real iPhone whether the PCM tap still receives samples with the ringer switch on silent or during an 'interrupted' state. It needs a physical device via the /clips/diagnostics page.
